title: ECS Health & Safety
subtitle: Twenty-seven ECS mock and topic tests
description: A comprehensive ECS health and safety exam set covering the full ECS safety spread: electrotechnical safety, special site hazards, work equipment, working at height, fire, hygiene, PPE, accident reporting, manual handling, general health and safety and environmental practice.
format: Twenty-seven rotating source tests: sixteen full ECS mocks plus eleven topic tests. The category pass threshold is set at 86%, matching the full ECS mock standard.

scoring.label: Strong — secure for ECS health and safety mocks
Pass — review missed safety topics before booking
Near miss — revise the weak safety areas
Major gaps — rebuild health and safety fundamentals first

priorities: Electrical safety, isolation, site rules and supervisor reporting.
Work at height, ladders, PPE, manual handling and work equipment.
Fire prevention, emergency action, hygiene, COSHH and environmental responsibilities.
Accident reporting, RIDDOR-style duties and general risk assessment.
Answer as a site safety decision; avoid shortcuts that sound convenient but unsafe.

questions.prompt: If you discover a hole or gap in a fire rated wall or floor that has not been fire-stopped, what should you do?

options.A: Cover the hole or gap with insulating tape
options.B: Ignore it unless it is causing a draught
options.C: Report it to your supervisor without delay
options.D: Use decorators' sealant to fill the gap

questions.explanation: Supervisors need to be made aware of any observed inadequacies in fire-stopping - which can undermine fire precautions catastrophically during the construction of buildings and on their completion. Only a limited range of products are suitable and they must be correctly applied to provide the required degree of fire-stopping.

A.text: Insulating tape has no tested fire-resistance rating and cannot reinstate a breached fire compartment.

B.text: A draught is irrelevant: any unsealed penetration can let smoke and flame bypass the fire-rated barrier.

C.text: Supervisors need to be made aware of any observed inadequacies in fire-stopping - which can undermine fire precautions catastrophically during the construction of buildings and on their completion. Only a limited range of products are suitable and they must be correctly applied to provide the required degree of fire-stopping.

D.text: Ordinary decorators' sealant is not a certified fire-stopping system matched to the wall or floor construction.

questions.prompt: In addition to preserving fire separation between areas of a building, which other important fire safety function can fire-stopping achieve?
questions.explanation: Many structural elements, such as timber joists or steel beams, lose strength quickly when exposed to fire and rely on linings like plasterboard for protection. Fire-stopping the gaps where services pass through maintains that protection, helping prevent premature structural collapse and giving occupants time to escape safely.

A.text: Many structural elements, such as timber joists or steel beams, lose strength quickly when exposed to fire and rely on linings like plasterboard for protection. Fire-stopping the gaps where services pass through maintains that protection, helping prevent premature structural collapse and giving occupants time to escape safely.

B.text: Acoustic sealing may be a secondary benefit, but it is not the additional life-safety function being tested here.

C.text: Nuisance alarms concern detection-system design; sealing service penetrations does not prevent detector activation.

D.text: Energy efficiency can improve when gaps are sealed, but it does not describe fire-stopping's structural protection role.

questions.prompt: Intumescent materials used to provide fire-stopping are designed to:
questions.explanation: A limited number of fire-resistant materials may be used to provide fire-stopping. These include intumescent products, which are designed to expand and provide fire-stopping when subjected to heat. Examples include intumescent 'pillows' (used to provide internal sealing of trunking) and intumescent mastic.

A.text: A limited number of fire-resistant materials may be used to provide fire-stopping. These include intumescent products, which are designed to expand and provide fire-stopping when subjected to heat. Examples include intumescent 'pillows' (used to provide internal sealing of trunking) and intumescent mastic.

B.text: Intumescent compounds react to elevated temperature, not merely to the presence of smoke particles.

C.text: Blocking sound is an acoustic treatment and does not describe the heat-driven action of an intumescent product.

D.text: Shrinking would enlarge the penetration during a fire; intumescent material must swell to close the opening.

questions.prompt: The purpose of fire-stopping in a building is to:

options.B: Delay the passage of fire and smoke through openings in walls and floors

questions.explanation: Fire-stopping is a passive fire protection measure used to seal any openings created in a fire resistance-rated wall or floor assembly, e.g. to allow pipes or wiring systems to pass through. During fire conditions this will impede the spread of fire and smoke.

A.text: Sprinkler activation is an active-system function; fire-stopping is passive protection within walls and floors.

B.text: Fire-stopping is a passive fire protection measure used to seal any openings created in a fire resistance-rated wall or floor assembly, e.g. to allow pipes or wiring systems to pass through. During fire conditions this will impede the spread of fire and smoke.

C.text: Fire-stopping cannot prevent ignition, but it can contain the products of a fire after one starts.

D.text: Alarm initiation belongs to detectors and call points, not to the material sealing a compartment boundary.

questions.prompt: What should you do if you disturb fire-stopping around a wiring system penetrating a wall or floor whilst carrying out work?

options.A: Ensure that the fire-stopping is reinstated to the necessary standard as soon as possible
options.B: Fill any holes or gaps with squashed paper
options.D: Nail a piece of wood over any gaps

questions.explanation: It is essential that the integrity of fire compartments is maintained during the construction of buildings and on their completion. Compromising compartmentation, such as failing to adequately fire-stop (seal) openings for services to pass through, can undermine fire precautions catastrophically. Only a limited range of products are suitable and they must be correctly applied to provide the required degree of fire-stopping.

A.text: It is essential that the integrity of fire compartments is maintained during the construction of buildings and on their completion. Compromising compartmentation, such as failing to adequately fire-stop (seal) openings for services to pass through, can undermine fire precautions catastrophically. Only a limited range of products are suitable and they must be correctly applied to provide the required degree of fire-stopping.

B.text: Paper is combustible, untested and easily displaced, so it cannot restore the required fire resistance.

C.text: Recording the damage does not close the penetration or protect occupants while the breach remains open.

D.text: A nailed board leaves untested joints and may itself be combustible; it is not a compliant penetration seal.

questions.prompt: Which of the following does NOT help sustainability during construction projects?

options.B: Leaving engines and motors running when they are not needed
options.D: Vehicle sharing or using public transport to get to work

questions.explanation: Leaving engines and motors running wastes fuel, creates avoidable emissions and adds unnecessary site noise. Switching plant off when it is not needed is the sustainable choice.

A.text: Avoiding unnecessary heating reduces energy use and emissions, so this action supports site sustainability.

B.text: Leaving engines and motors running wastes fuel, creates avoidable emissions and adds unnecessary site noise. Switching plant off when it is not needed is the sustainable choice.

C.text: Separating waste enables reuse and recycling instead of contaminating recoverable material in a mixed skip.

D.text: Sharing vehicles or taking public transport reduces fuel consumption and travel emissions per worker.

questions.prompt: From an environmental point of view, why should materials be reused, where possible?

options.A: A lot of energy and raw materials go into making most construction products
options.B: It makes less mess on site

questions.explanation: Although reducing the amount of waste is the first priority, the re-use of materials can also contribute to effective waste management.

A.text: Although reducing the amount of waste is the first priority, the re-use of materials can also contribute to effective waste management.

B.text: Less mess is useful housekeeping, but it does not explain the upstream environmental cost avoided by reuse.

C.text: Reuse is not justified by a blanket European-law requirement; its benefit comes from conserving resources and energy.

D.text: Client savings may follow, but cost alone is not the environmental reason for retaining useful material.

questions.prompt: You are on site and you need to dispose of some waste liquid that has oil in it and you are not sure what to do with it. What should you do?

options.A: Ask your supervisor about the correct way to deal with this waste.
options.B: Dispose of it in a sealed container into the site skip
options.C: Pour it onto the ground, it will soak away
options.D: Take it outside and set light to it

questions.explanation: Dealing with hazardous/special waste will include proper storage and segregation before it is taken away by an authorized waste carrier as required by environmental legislation. An oil spillage could also get into the ground or drains, which may also be an offence under environmental law. Burning waste on site is also an offence, under air pollution legislation, and can lead to local complaints.

A.text: Dealing with hazardous/special waste will include proper storage and segregation before it is taken away by an authorized waste carrier as required by environmental legislation. An oil spillage could also get into the ground or drains, which may also be an offence under environmental law. Burning waste on site is also an offence, under air pollution legislation, and can lead to local complaints.

B.text: An ordinary site skip is not an authorised route for oily liquid, even when the liquid is put in a sealed container.

C.text: Oil can contaminate soil, groundwater and drains; allowing it to soak away is pollution, not disposal.

D.text: Burning oily waste creates fire and air-pollution hazards and is not an authorised waste-treatment method.

questions.prompt: A portable electric generator on site has two power outlets, 110 volts and 230 volts. What colour would the 110 volt outlet be?
questions.explanation: On UK sites a standard colour code identifies supply voltages at a glance for safety. Yellow denotes 110 V reduced low voltage equipment, so the 110 V outlet, its plugs and connectors are yellow, while 230 V kit uses blue, clearly separating the safer site supply from the higher mains voltage.

A.text: Black is not the BS EN 60309 identification colour for a 110 V reduced-low-voltage site connector.

B.text: Blue identifies the normal 200-250 V range, so it distinguishes 230 V equipment from the site 110 V supply.

C.text: Red identifies the 380-480 V range, commonly used for 400 V three-phase connections rather than 110 V.

D.text: On UK sites a standard colour code identifies supply voltages at a glance for safety. Yellow denotes 110 V reduced low voltage equipment, so the 110 V outlet, its plugs and connectors are yellow, while 230 V kit uses blue, clearly separating the safer site supply from the higher mains voltage.

questions.prompt: What is the most serious effect that electric shock can have if you come into contact with a live part?

options.A: The electric current can cause a slight tingling in the fingers
options.B: The electric current can cause burn marks on the fingers
options.C: The electric current can cause the finger muscles to twitch
options.D: The electric current can cause the heart to stop, resulting in death

questions.explanation: Contact with live electrical parts can be fatal. If you do not know otherwise, always assume that electrical parts are live.

A.text: Tingling is an early shock effect, but it is less severe than a current path that stops the heart.

B.text: Burns can be serious and deep, yet cardiac arrest presents the more immediate fatal consequence listed.

C.text: Muscle twitching shows physiological stimulation, but it is not the most severe outcome among these choices.

D.text: Contact with live electrical parts can be fatal. If you do not know otherwise, always assume that electrical parts are live.

questions.prompt: Which of the following does the Electricity at Work (EAW) regulations apply to?

options.A: All persons engaged for work purposes

questions.explanation: The EAW Regulations impose duties on employers, employees and the self employed.

A.text: The EAW Regulations impose duties on employers, employees and the self employed.

B.text: The Regulations also impose duties beyond employees, including on employers and self-employed people at work.

C.text: Employers carry major duties, but employees and self-employed people also have obligations under the Regulations.

D.text: Self-employed people are covered, but limiting the scope to them excludes employees and employers who are also covered.

questions.prompt: In accordance with the Electricity at Work regulations, when considering whether to work live a responsible person should:
questions.explanation: To identify and assess the risks involved and the methods of controlling them.

A.text: To identify and assess the risks involved and the methods of controlling them.

B.text: A client's demand cannot displace the legal duty to assess and control the danger created by live work.

C.text: Dead working is the normal approach, but the decision process still requires assessment of the actual circumstances.

D.text: Live work is exceptional, not an automatic method to choose without first evaluating whether it is justified.

questions.prompt: Under Regulation 14 of the Electricity at Work Regulations 1989, when may work on or near a live conductor that may give rise to danger proceed?

options.A: Only when it is unreasonable in all the circumstances for the conductor to be dead, it is reasonable to work live, and suitable precautions are taken to prevent injury
options.B: When the means of isolation cannot be identified
options.C: When the person carrying out the work is a competent person
options.D: When the person working on the equipment is wearing rubber gloves

questions.explanation: All three Regulation 14 conditions must be satisfied. Live work must be justified because making dead is unreasonable, carrying it out live must itself be reasonable, and suitable precautions, including suitable protective equipment where necessary, must prevent injury.

A.text: All three Regulation 14 conditions must be satisfied. Live work must be justified because making dead is unreasonable, carrying it out live must itself be reasonable, and suitable precautions, including suitable protective equipment where necessary, must prevent injury.

B.text: Difficulty identifying isolation does not satisfy the statutory tests; the supply must be traced and the work properly planned.

C.text: Competence is necessary for dangerous electrical work, but competence alone does not justify leaving the conductor live.

D.text: Rubber gloves are only one possible precaution and cannot replace the three legal conditions for live work.

questions.prompt: Which listed device is specifically intended to provide additional protection against electric shock by rapidly disconnecting for some residual-current faults?

options.A: A 3 amp fuse should prevent a person receiving a fatal electric shock
options.B: A 30 mA Residual Current Device (RCD), although it does not make contact with live parts safe or guarantee survival
options.C: A 5 amp rewireable fuse should prevent a person receiving a fatal electric shock
options.D: A 6 amp circuit breaker should prevent a person receiving a fatal electric shock

questions.explanation: A 30 mA RCD can limit the energy in some electric shocks and can save life, but it detects only residual-current imbalance and is additional protection. It cannot replace isolation, earthing, basic protection or safe working practice, and it does not guarantee that a shock will not be fatal.

A.text: A 3 A fuse protects wiring against sustained overcurrent; it may carry far more than a lethal body current without operating.

B.text: A 30 mA RCD can limit the energy in some electric shocks and can save life, but it detects only residual-current imbalance and is additional protection. It cannot replace isolation, earthing, basic protection or safe working practice, and it does not guarantee that a shock will not be fatal.

C.text: A rewireable fuse responds to circuit overcurrent, not the small residual imbalance associated with a person receiving a shock.

D.text: A 6 A breaker is intended for overload and short-circuit protection and is not sensitive enough for personal shock protection.

questions.prompt: You are asked to enter a manhole where a toxic or oxygen-deficient atmosphere may be present, but no assessed safe system or suitable respiratory protection has been provided. What should you do?

options.A: Just get on with the job, and accept the risks
options.B: Look into the manhole to see if you can see any harmful gases
options.C: Sniff the atmosphere in the manhole to see if you can smell harmful gases
options.D: Do not enter; report it so entry can be avoided or a competent risk-assessed system, atmosphere controls, training and rescue arrangements can be put in place

questions.explanation: Confined-space entry should be avoided where possible. If it is essential, the employer must assess the atmosphere and other risks, implement a safe system, provide suitable equipment and training, and establish adequate rescue arrangements before entry. Asking only for generic RPE would be incomplete.

A.text: Entering without controls risks rapid collapse, poisoning or asphyxiation and may also endanger would-be rescuers.

B.text: Many toxic gases and oxygen deficiency are invisible, so looking into the opening cannot establish a safe atmosphere.

C.text: Hazardous atmospheres may have no warning odour, and sniffing exposes the worker before any measurement is made.

D.text: Confined-space entry should be avoided where possible. If it is essential, the employer must assess the atmosphere and other risks, implement a safe system, provide suitable equipment and training, and establish adequate rescue arrangements before entry. Asking only for generic RPE would be incomplete.

questions.prompt: When working alone:

options.A: Don't bother anyone if you have a problem, always sort it out yourself
options.B: Make sure someone responsible knows where you are
options.C: Wear headphones, it will make the day go more quickly
options.D: You can do away with protective equipment

questions.explanation: Employees should adhere to safe working arrangements put in place by their employer. When working alone, such arrangements should include informing a responsible person of your location periodically.

A.text: Lone-working arrangements must provide a way to obtain assistance; self-reliance cannot control emergencies or incapacitation.

B.text: Employees should adhere to safe working arrangements put in place by their employer. When working alone, such arrangements should include informing a responsible person of your location periodically.

C.text: Headphones can mask alarms, vehicles and calls for help, increasing isolation rather than managing it.

D.text: Working alone does not remove any hazard, so the assessed protective equipment remains necessary.

questions.prompt: What is the preferred nominal voltage for portable hand tools on construction sites?
questions.explanation: Construction sites use 110 V centre-tapped-to-earth supplies for portable tools because this limits the voltage to earth to around 55 V, greatly reducing the severity of any electric shock in the damp, hazardous site environment while still powering tools effectively.

A.text: Construction sites use 110 V centre-tapped-to-earth supplies for portable tools because this limits the voltage to earth to around 55 V, greatly reducing the severity of any electric shock in the damp, hazardous site environment while still powering tools effectively.

B.text: Twelve volts may suit specialist very-high-risk conditions, but it is not the standard nominal site-tool supply.

C.text: Portable 230 V tools create a greater shock risk and are not the preferred general construction-site arrangement.

D.text: Twenty-four volts can be used for particular equipment, but UK site power tools normally use 110 V centre-tapped-to-earth.

questions.prompt: What is most commonly used to reduce 230 volts to 110 volts on site?
questions.explanation: A transformer, usually coloured yellow, will transform 230 volts (mains voltage) down to a relatively safe 110 volts.

A.text: A circuit-breaker disconnects excessive current; it does not change a 230 V supply into 110 V.

B.text: An RCD detects current imbalance and disconnects faults, but its output voltage remains the supply voltage.

C.text: A generator can produce 110 V independently, but it is not the usual device for reducing an existing 230 V supply.

D.text: A transformer, usually coloured yellow, will transform 230 volts (mains voltage) down to a relatively safe 110 volts.

questions.prompt: If an extension cable is to be run across a site road, what action should you take?

options.A: Don't do anything to protect the cable
options.B: Lay the cable over wooden boards
options.C: Place a rubber protection ramp over it and put up a sign stating 'Ramp Ahead'

questions.explanation: It is essential that the cable is protected from damage caused by passing traffic. A sign will warn road traffic of the ramp.

A.text: An unprotected cable can be crushed or cut by traffic, exposing live conductors and interrupting the supply.

B.text: Loose boards can shift, split or create a vehicle hazard and do not provide a designed cable-crossing system.

C.text: It is essential that the cable is protected from damage caused by passing traffic. A sign will warn road traffic of the ramp.

D.text: Casually thrown boards provide neither reliable mechanical protection nor adequate warning to approaching drivers.

questions.prompt: Why may a confined space be dangerous to work in?

options.A: Air in the space may be unbreathable due to poisonous gas
options.C: Temperature and poor ventilation may affect the worker
options.D: There may not be sufficient working space

questions.explanation: There can be a range of hazards associated with confined spaces, and these can include all of those mentioned

A.text: A poisonous or oxygen-deficient atmosphere is one confined-space hazard, but heat, access and restricted movement also matter.

B.text: There can be a range of hazards associated with confined spaces, and these can include all of those mentioned

C.text: Temperature and ventilation are important, but this choice omits atmospheric toxicity and restricted working space.

D.text: Restricted space can hamper work and rescue, but it does not capture the separate atmospheric and thermal dangers.

questions.prompt: Before moving a mobile tower scaffold, to what maximum height should the tower be reduced under current HSE guidance?
questions.explanation: HSE says to reduce a tower to a maximum height of 4 m before moving it. The route must also be checked for overhead lines and obstructions, the ground must be firm and level, and no person or material should remain on the tower while it moves.

A.text: Reducing below 4 m may be prudent for a particular route, but 2 m is not HSE's stated general maximum before moving.

B.text: Three metres is conservative but does not state the published 4 m maximum that this factual question asks for.

C.text: HSE says to reduce a tower to a maximum height of 4 m before moving it. The route must also be checked for overhead lines and obstructions, the ground must be firm and level, and no person or material should remain on the tower while it moves.

D.text: Five metres exceeds HSE's maximum reduced height and increases overturning risk while the tower is moved.

questions.prompt: What do the letters SWL stand for?
questions.explanation: Machinery and accessories for lifting loads should be clearly marked to indicate their safe working loads.

A.text: SWL marks a permissible load, not a working height or level from which equipment may be used.

B.text: Machinery and accessories for lifting loads should be clearly marked to indicate their safe working loads.

C.text: The recognised term uses 'safe working', not 'satisfactory weight', because it defines an equipment loading limit.

D.text: 'Satisfactory working limit' is not the standard expansion shown on lifting equipment and accessories.

questions.prompt: When working above public areas, what should be considered?

options.A: Keeping the areas open to the public

questions.explanation: There is a significant risk to the public from falling materials, if this is not considered before and during work.

A.text: Keeping the area open exposes people below; access should instead be prevented or falling objects contained.

B.text: Production pressure cannot take priority over controlling a potentially fatal falling-object hazard.

C.text: Avoiding complaints is not the safety objective; a falling item can seriously injure someone before any complaint occurs.

D.text: There is a significant risk to the public from falling materials, if this is not considered before and during work.

questions.prompt: You have been asked to operate a cherry-picker (mobile elevated work platform) when it is very windy. What should your FIRST consideration be?

options.A: Does the wind-speed make it unsafe to use the machine
options.B: Tie all light-weight objects to the hand-rails of the basket
options.C: Wear a safety harness and clip it to the structure that you are working on
options.D: Wear an extra layer of clothing to keep warm

questions.explanation: The priority in safety is eliminating risk at source - in this case by not working in dangerous conditions - rather than trying to stay safe by using protective equipment.

A.text: The priority in safety is eliminating risk at source - in this case by not working in dangerous conditions - rather than trying to stay safe by using protective equipment.

B.text: Securing loose items helps, but it does not establish whether wind can overturn or destabilise the MEWP itself.

C.text: Clipping to the external structure can create crushing or ejection hazards and does not make excessive wind safe.

D.text: Extra clothing addresses comfort only; it provides no control over the machine's wind-speed operating limit.

questions.prompt: How many people should be working on a ladder at one time?

options.B: One on each section of an extension ladder
options.C: Three if it is long enough

questions.explanation: Only one person should be working on a ladder, although another person may be footing it, for extra stability.

A.text: Only one person should be working on a ladder, although another person may be footing it, for extra stability.

B.text: An extension ladder is still designed for one user; separate sections do not create independent working positions.

C.text: Length does not increase the ladder's person rating, and three moving users would severely reduce stability.

D.text: Two workers create extra loading and movement on equipment intended to support one climber at a time.

questions.prompt: What is the ideal angle for a ladder against a wall and floor?

options.A: Four metres up for every metre out from the wall
options.B: One metre up for every metre out from the wall
options.C: One metre up for every two metres out from the wall
options.D: Two metres up for every metre out from the wall

questions.explanation: The correct angle for a ladder is 75 degrees, which an be judged using the angle indicator marked on the stiles of some ladders or using the 1 in 4 rule.

A.text: The correct angle for a ladder is 75 degrees, which an be judged using the angle indicator marked on the stiles of some ladders or using the 1 in 4 rule.

B.text: A one-to-one slope is about 45 degrees, far shallower and less stable than the recommended 75-degree angle.

C.text: One metre up for two metres out is about 27 degrees, making the ladder dangerously close to horizontal.

D.text: A two-to-one slope is about 63 degrees, still too shallow compared with the one-in-four setup rule.

questions.prompt: How often should a first-aider qualified in First Aid at Work (FAW) or Emergency First Aid at Work (EFAW) receive retraining?
questions.explanation: First Aid at Work (FAW) and Emergency First Aid at Work (EFAW) certificates are valid for three years and first-aiders are required to undertake retraining at the end of this period. However, the HSE also strongly recommends that first-aiders undertake annual (half-day) refresher training.

A.text: Four years exceeds the three-year validity period of an FAW or EFAW certificate, leaving a gap in qualification.

B.text: Six months is not the certificate-renewal interval; HSE separately recommends shorter annual refresher practice.

C.text: First Aid at Work (FAW) and Emergency First Aid at Work (EFAW) certificates are valid for three years and first-aiders are required to undertake retraining at the end of this period. However, the HSE also strongly recommends that first-aiders undertake annual (half-day) refresher training.

D.text: Two-year retraining may be chosen voluntarily, but it is not the standard three-year certificate cycle asked for.

questions.prompt: A person nearly collapses complaining of stomach pains. What should you do?

options.A: Ask them if they want something to eat
options.B: Go and find them something to drink
options.C: Help them to find somewhere comfortable to sit

questions.explanation: Unexplained collapse with severe stomach pain could signal a serious medical emergency, so the priority is to get trained help fast. Sending someone for the first-aider brings competent assessment quickly; offering food or drink could be harmful if the casualty needs treatment or surgery.

A.text: Food can complicate urgent treatment and does not obtain a trained assessment for a person close to collapse.

B.text: Giving a drink may be unsafe if surgery or reduced consciousness follows, and it delays summoning competent help.

C.text: A comfortable seat may prevent a fall, but it does not address the unexplained pain and near-collapse medically.

D.text: Unexplained collapse with severe stomach pain could signal a serious medical emergency, so the priority is to get trained help fast. Sending someone for the first-aider brings competent assessment quickly; offering food or drink could be harmful if the casualty needs treatment or surgery.

questions.prompt: Where would you go in the event of a fire?

options.A: To the canteen for a cup of tea
options.C: To the fire to see what is going on

questions.explanation: Going to the designated fire assembly point lets marshals carry out a roll call and confirm everyone is safely out, so no one is wrongly believed still inside. Staying near the fire or wandering to huts puts you at risk and disrupts the head count.

A.text: A canteen is not necessarily outside the danger area and prevents the fire roll call from accounting for you.

B.text: Going to the designated fire assembly point lets marshals carry out a roll call and confirm everyone is safely out, so no one is wrongly believed still inside. Staying near the fire or wandering to huts puts you at risk and disrupts the head count.

C.text: Approaching the fire increases exposure to smoke, heat and structural danger and obstructs emergency responders.

D.text: A site hut is not a safe destination unless it is specifically designated as the assembly point.

questions.prompt: What must your employer do if the daily personal noise exposure is at or exceeds 85 db(A)?

options.A: Issue hearing protection to those exposed and ensure that it is worn
options.B: Provide hearing protection to those employees who ask for it
options.C: Report it to the Health and Safety Executive
options.D: Tell employees to buy their own hearing protection

questions.explanation: This is an interim measure under the Control of Noise at Work Regulations 2005 when the daily personal noise exposure is at or exceeds the upper exposure action value of 85 dB(A). Exposure should subsequently be reduced by implementing organizational or technical measures.

A.text: This is an interim measure under the Control of Noise at Work Regulations 2005 when the daily personal noise exposure is at or exceeds the upper exposure action value of 85 dB(A). Exposure should subsequently be reduced by implementing organizational or technical measures.

B.text: Providing protection only on request applies at the lower action value; at 85 dB(A) its use must be ensured.

C.text: Crossing the upper action value requires exposure controls and hearing protection, not routine notification to HSE.

D.text: Required PPE must be supplied by the employer without charge; workers cannot be told to buy their own.

questions.prompt: Which of the following animals can carry Weil's disease?
questions.explanation: Weil's disease is a serious and sometimes fatal infection that can be transmitted to humans by contact with infected rats. Another form of Leptospirosis infection can be transmitted from cattle to humans.

A.text: Pigs can carry other zoonoses, but rats and their urine are the classic construction-site source of Weil's disease.

B.text: Weil's disease is a serious and sometimes fatal infection that can be transmitted to humans by contact with infected rats. Another form of Leptospirosis infection can be transmitted from cattle to humans.

C.text: Sheep are associated with different occupational infections; they are not the expected reservoir in this question.

D.text: Snake exposure is unrelated to leptospiral infection from urine-contaminated water or wet ground.

questions.prompt: An emergency route(s) must be provided on construction sites to ensure:

options.A: Safe passage to a secure place of safety
options.B: Safe passage to the ground from height
options.C: Safe passage to the open air
options.D: Safe passage to the rest area

questions.explanation: Emergency routes exist so people can reach a secure place of safety quickly if danger arises, not merely escape from height or reach a rest area. The aim is a clear, protected path leading away from harm to somewhere genuinely safe.

A.text: Emergency routes exist so people can reach a secure place of safety quickly if danger arises, not merely escape from height or reach a rest area. The aim is a clear, protected path leading away from harm to somewhere genuinely safe.

B.text: Reaching ground level addresses only escape from height and may still leave people inside the danger zone.

C.text: Open air is not automatically safe if it remains exposed to fire, smoke, collapse or another site emergency.

D.text: A rest area is provided for welfare, not necessarily as a protected destination during an emergency.

questions.prompt: Exposure to asbestos fibres may cause which one of the following?
questions.explanation: Breathing in asbestos fibres can also lead to a number of other diseases, including lung cancer and mesothelioma

A.text: Breathing in asbestos fibres can also lead to a number of other diseases, including lung cancer and mesothelioma

B.text: Asthma can have many workplace causes, but it is not the characteristic fibrotic lung disease caused by asbestos fibres.

C.text: Dermatitis is an inflammatory skin condition; inhaled asbestos primarily causes serious diseases of the lungs and pleura.

questions.prompt: What is the preferred nominal voltage for local lighting up to 2 kW on construction sites?
questions.explanation: Reduced low voltage at 110V centre-tapped to earth limits any shock to about 55V to earth, greatly reducing danger in the harsh, often wet conditions on site. 230V and 400V carry far higher shock risk for portable equipment.

questions.prompt: To operate a powered hand tool you must be:
questions.explanation: There are no general age restrictions in legislation relating to the use of work equipment. Any person using work equipment, however, must be competent to do so, which will require initial and refresher training.

D.text: There are no general age restrictions in legislation relating to the use of work equipment. Any person using work equipment, however, must be competent to do so, which will require initial and refresher training.

questions.prompt: Of the following, which is the poorest method of securing a ladder?

options.B: Securing the base of the ladder

questions.explanation: Footing a ladder is the last resort and should be avoided. Other more suitable access equipment should be used where practicable.

A.text: Footing a ladder is the last resort and should be avoided. Other more suitable access equipment should be used where practicable.

B.text: Securing the base is a physical restraint and is more reliable than depending on another person's attention and strength.

C.text: Tying the ladder near the top provides positive restraint and is preferred where a suitable point is available.

D.text: A suitable stability device controls movement mechanically and is preferable to relying on a person footing it.

questions.prompt: What must you do when work equipment is found damaged?

options.B: Locked up so no one can use it
options.C: Take it out of use and report the defect to your supervisor or other responsible person

questions.explanation: Damaged equipment must not remain available for use. Remove it from service and report or label it through the site procedure so a competent person can assess, repair or replace it before it is used again.

A.text: A label alone is incomplete unless the equipment is also removed from availability and the defect is reported.

B.text: Locking equipment away controls immediate use but does not communicate the defect for assessment, repair or replacement.

C.text: Damaged equipment must not remain available for use. Remove it from service and report or label it through the site procedure so a competent person can assess, repair or replace it before it is used again.

D.text: Immediate disposal may be wasteful or unsafe; a competent person should determine whether repair or replacement is appropriate.

questions.prompt: When can you work from a ladder?

options.A: For short periods and then only if it is safe to do so
options.D: When not being used for access

questions.explanation: Ladders are primarily means of access, not workplaces. They can be worked from, but only if the use of other, more suitable, work equipment is not appropriate and the task is of low risk and of short duration.

A.text: Ladders are primarily means of access, not workplaces. They can be worked from, but only if the use of other, more suitable, work equipment is not appropriate and the task is of low risk and of short duration.

B.text: Availability is not a risk assessment; a safer platform may be required even when a ladder is close at hand.

C.text: Sufficient length addresses reach only and says nothing about duration, task risk, stability or maintaining handhold.

D.text: A ladder used as access does not become a suitable workplace merely when nobody is climbing through it.

questions.prompt: On a mobile elevating work platform, what should you attach your safety harness to?

options.B: A secure anchorage point inside the platform
options.C: A strong part of the structure you are working on

questions.explanation: The priority is to stay within the platform (which is the safest place), and in any event you cannot be sure of the strength of other fixtures.

B.text: The priority is to stay within the platform (which is the safest place), and in any event you cannot be sure of the strength of other fixtures.

C.text: Clipping to the work structure defeats the platform's movement and can pull the worker from the basket.

D.text: The boom is not automatically a designated anchor and may expose the lanyard to moving or trapping points.

questions.prompt: What should you do if your work activity requires you to wear a full body safety harness and one is not available?

options.A: Borrow a harness from a colleague
options.B: Carry on working and hope that everything will be alright
options.C: Make a harness from items found on site
options.D: Stop work immediately and tell your supervisor that you do not have the correct PPE

questions.explanation: Always advise the supervisor if you do not have the correct PPE.

A.text: A borrowed harness may not fit, be compatible or have an inspection history, so it cannot simply be assumed suitable.

B.text: Hope provides no fall protection; proceeding without the assessed system risks an uncontrolled fatal fall.

C.text: Improvised materials are not tested fall-arrest equipment and can fail under the very high forces of a fall.

D.text: Always advise the supervisor if you do not have the correct PPE.

questions.prompt: In an emergency situation at work you should do what?

options.A: Ensure your work mates are all accounted for

questions.explanation: A site emergency plan should have been drawn up and you should be familiar with the emergency procedure.

B.text: Leaving by an unplanned route may enter the hazard area and prevents an accurate roll call at the assembly point.

C.text: A site emergency plan should have been drawn up and you should be familiar with the emergency procedure.

D.text: HSE is not the site's emergency-response service; calling it does not replace alarm, evacuation and emergency contacts.

questions.prompt: The type of accident that kills most construction site workers is:
questions.explanation: Although the other dangers can kill or cause injury, falling from height is the biggest cause of fatalities.

A.text: Falling objects can kill, but recent construction fatality statistics attribute the largest share to falls from height.

B.text: Electrical accidents remain serious, yet they account for fewer construction deaths than falls from height.

C.text: Although the other dangers can kill or cause injury, falling from height is the biggest cause of fatalities.

D.text: Trench collapses are foreseeable and often fatal, but they are not the leading fatal-accident type in the listed data.

questions.prompt: After checking that approaching the casualty will not expose you or them to immediate danger, what should you do first on finding an injured person on site?

options.A: Call for the trained first-aider and appropriate emergency help
options.C: Tell the casualty to visit their doctor
options.D: Try and find out what happened

questions.explanation: First make sure it is safe to approach, then summon competent help promptly and follow the emergency procedure. Do not investigate the incident or move the casualty unnecessarily before urgent needs have been assessed.

A.text: First make sure it is safe to approach, then summon competent help promptly and follow the emergency procedure. Do not investigate the incident or move the casualty unnecessarily before urgent needs have been assessed.

B.text: HSE notification is not the immediate clinical priority and is handled later by the responsible person if reportable.

C.text: A casualty may need urgent treatment and should not be sent away without assessment by the first-aider.

D.text: Incident details matter later, but questioning first can delay emergency assessment and summon no competent help.

questions.prompt: Your workmate suddenly gets a foreign body in the eye. What should you do?

options.B: Take your workmate to the supervisor
options.C: Use a clean handkerchief to try and remove it
options.D: Wash your hands before touching your mate's face

questions.explanation: A foreign body in the eye needs trained first-aid care; sending for the first-aider gets competent help without delay. Trying to remove it yourself with a handkerchief risks scratching the eye or driving the object in deeper, causing lasting damage.

A.text: A foreign body in the eye needs trained first-aid care; sending for the first-aider gets competent help without delay. Trying to remove it yourself with a handkerchief risks scratching the eye or driving the object in deeper, causing lasting damage.

B.text: A supervisor is not necessarily trained to assess an eye injury, so this detour can delay appropriate first aid.

C.text: A handkerchief can scratch the cornea or push an embedded particle deeper into the eye.

D.text: Clean hands do not make untrained removal safe; the eye should be assessed by the first-aider.

questions.prompt: If there had been a small fire, who should you report it to?
questions.explanation: The supervisor should be aware, so that further preventative measures can be considered.

D.text: The supervisor should be aware, so that further preventative measures can be considered.

questions.prompt: What should you do if the toilets on your site are continually dirty?

options.A: Ask in a nearby cafe or pub if you can use their toilets
options.B: Find some cleaning materials and clean it up yourself
options.C: Ignore the problem - its normal on a construction site
options.D: Make sure you tell someone who can sort it out

questions.explanation: How often welfare facilities on site require cleaning will depend on the number of people on site and how quickly they get dirty. The person in control of the site should make sure someone is responsible for keeping the facilities clean and tidy.

B.text: Workers should leave sanitation and hazardous cleaning to the arranged service rather than silently taking it on themselves.

D.text: How often welfare facilities on site require cleaning will depend on the number of people on site and how quickly they get dirty. The person in control of the site should make sure someone is responsible for keeping the facilities clean and tidy.

questions.prompt: Exposure to asbestos fibres may cause which one of the following?
questions.explanation: Breathing in asbestos fibres can also lead to a number of other diseases, including lung cancer and mesothelioma

D.text: Glandular fever is a viral infection and has no causal link to breathing asbestos fibres.

questions.prompt: The number of toilets provided on site depends on:

options.B: The number of personnel on site

questions.explanation: Guidance on the provision of welfare facilities is given in HSE publication 'Health and Safety in Construction'.

D.text: The work type may influence additional washing needs, but it does not replace the workforce-size calculation.

questions.prompt: When using personal protective equipment (PPE) legally you must do which of the following?

options.B: Not interfere with it or misuse it

C.text: The employer provides and replaces required PPE without charging the worker for ordinary wear or damage.

questions.prompt: When is head protection required to be worn on a construction site to comply with the Personal Protective Equipment at Work Regulations?

options.A: At all times except by those who are self employed
options.B: At all times unless there is no foreseeable risk of injury to the head other than by falling.
options.C: At all times unless you are working on scaffold

questions.explanation: If there is no risk of injury to the head, then hard hats are not required by law. However, on construction sites, despite controls being in place, there will almost always be situations where a risk of head injury remains and require head protection to be worn. Site rules will also require the wearing of head protection other than in any designated safe areas.

A.text: Self-employed status does not remove the need for head protection where the assessment identifies a foreseeable injury risk.

However, on construction sites, despite controls being in place, there will almost always be situations where a risk of head injury remains and require head protection to be worn. Site rules will also require the wearing of head protection other than in any designated safe areas.

C.text: Scaffold work can expose the head to falling or swinging objects; location on a scaffold is not an exemption.

D.text: Personal preference cannot override the risk assessment, site rules or instructions for required protective equipment.

questions.prompt: If personal protective equipment (PPE) is defective, what should you do?

options.A: Complain to the Health and Safety Inspector
options.B: Get your work mate to mend it if possible
options.C: Repair if possible and continue to use it

questions.prompt: What type of eye protection would you wear when using a cartridge-operated tool, such as a nail gun?

questions.prompt: What is the aim of carrying out an accident investigation?

options.A: To determine the cause(s) and prevent similar accidents
options.B: To establish the cost of any damage incurred
options.C: To establish what injuries were sustained

questions.explanation: An accident investigation should not only assess the cause, but also how similar accidents can be prevented in the future.

B.text: Damage cost may be recorded, but it does not explain the unsafe conditions and actions that must be prevented.

C.text: Documenting injuries describes consequences only and does not identify why the event happened or how to stop recurrence.

D.text: A blame-led inquiry discourages evidence and misses underlying task, equipment and management causes.

questions.prompt: If a person at work suffers an injury (other than a specified injury) due to an accident at work, it is reportable under RIDDOR if they are incapacitated for work for:
questions.explanation: An over-seven-day injury is one which is not a specified injury but results in the injured person being away from work or unable to do the full range of their normal duties for more than seven days (including any days they wouldn't normally be expected to work such as weekends, rest days or holidays) not counting the day of the injury itself.

A.text: One day of incapacity is below the over-seven-day worker reporting threshold for this category.

C.text: An over-seven-day injury is one which is not a specified injury but results in the injured person being away from work or unable to do the full range of their normal duties for more than seven days (including any days they wouldn't normally be expected to work such as weekends, rest days or holidays) not counting the day of the injury itself.

D.text: Half a day does not trigger over-seven-day reporting and should not be confused with accident-book recording.

questions.prompt: Before picking up a load, you should:

options.A: Ask a work mate to help you

questions.explanation: You or your employer must assess the risk of injury before lifting.

A.text: Help may be one control, but requesting it before assessing the load and task can create an unplanned team lift.

B.text: You or your employer must assess the risk of injury before lifting.

D.text: Gloves can improve grip or protect skin, but they do not establish whether the lift itself is safe.

questions.prompt: If a load has an uneven centre of gravity, how should you lift it?

options.A: Keep the heaviest side of the load away from you
options.B: Keep the heaviest side of the load on the strongest arm
options.C: Keep the heaviest side of the load on the weakest arm
options.D: Keep the heaviest side of the load towards you

questions.explanation: There is less risk of injury if a weight's centre of gravity is near the torso.

A.text: Holding the heavy side away increases the load's moment and forces the back and arms to work harder.

B.text: Loading one arm according to perceived strength creates imbalance; the heavy side should be kept close to the body.

C.text: Deliberately loading the weaker arm reduces control and does nothing to manage the offset centre of gravity.

D.text: There is less risk of injury if a weight's centre of gravity is near the torso.

questions.prompt: What should you ensure if you suffer an injury through a manual handling operation?

options.B: You get help and carry on working
options.C: You get paid for the job

questions.explanation: All injuries must be recorded in the Company accident book (BI 510)

B.text: Continuing after assistance can worsen an injury; the event must be reported and assessed before work resumes.

C.text: Payment is a contractual issue and does not create the health record needed after a handling injury.

D.text: Time away may or may not be medically required, but it does not replace recording and reporting the injury.

questions.prompt: Where there has been a major change in a manual handling operation, what should the employer do?

options.C: Review the number of people involved

questions.explanation: This is a specific requirement of the Manual Handling Operations regulations 1992.

C.text: Staffing is only one factor; a major change can affect the whole task, load, environment and individual capability.

D.text: This is a specific requirement of the Manual Handling Operations regulations 1992.

questions.prompt: The Health and Safety (Safety Signs and Signals) Regulations require the colour coding of safety signs. What colours are used on a sign indicating a mandatory activity, for example "Safety helmets must be worn"?
questions.explanation: Mandatory signs use blue with white, telling you an action must be taken, such as wearing a helmet. Yellow and black means warning, red means prohibition, and green means safe condition, so each colour conveys a distinct instruction.

A.text: Mandatory signs use blue with white, telling you an action must be taken, such as wearing a helmet. Yellow and black means warning, red means prohibition, and green means safe condition, so each colour conveys a distinct instruction.

B.text: Green and white marks safe conditions and emergency facilities, not an instruction that must be followed.

C.text: Red, black and white prohibits an activity; it is not used for a positive helmet-wearing command.

D.text: Yellow and black warns of a hazard but does not prescribe the action that the viewer must take.

questions.prompt: Before performing manual lifting what is the first thing you should do?

options.C: Kick it to see if it is stable

questions.explanation: If you assess the whole task first, you will have a clear idea of possible hazards and how to overcome them, before lifting

A.text: If you assess the whole task first, you will have a clear idea of possible hazards and how to overcome them, before lifting

B.text: Headroom is one environmental factor, but it cannot replace assessment of the full lift, route and person.

C.text: Kicking a load can damage it or injure the foot and gives no reliable information about handling stability.

D.text: Weight alone omits shape, grip, posture, travel, frequency and capability, all of which can determine risk.

questions.prompt: The Health and Safety at Work Act 1974 and any regulations made under the Act are:

options.C: Not compulsory, but should be complied with if convenient
options.D: Practical advice for the employer to follow

questions.explanation: The requirements of health and safety law are mandatory and failure to follow them can lead to prosecution.

A.text: Acts and regulations impose enforceable duties; they are not optional recommendations for companies or individuals.

B.text: The requirements of health and safety law are mandatory and failure to follow them can lead to prosecution.

C.text: Convenience is not a defence to non-compliance with a statutory health and safety requirement.

D.text: Practical guidance explains ways to comply, whereas the Act and regulations themselves create legal obligations.

questions.prompt: Where should you look for Official advice on health and safety matters?

options.A: A professionally approved guide book on regulations
options.B: A set of health and safety guidelines provided by suppliers
options.C: Guidance issued by the Health and Safety Executive
options.D: The health and safety rules as laid down by the employer

questions.explanation: The HSE is the UK enforcing body and its guidance can be regarded as 'official'

A.text: A commercial guide may help interpretation, but it is not necessarily current or issued by the enforcing authority.

B.text: Supplier guidance is valuable for products but cannot provide authoritative coverage of general legal duties.

C.text: The HSE is the UK enforcing body and its guidance can be regarded as 'official'

D.text: Employer rules apply locally and may exceed legal minima, but they are not the source of official national advice.

questions.prompt: In a health and safety risk assessment, what does the term risk describe?

options.B: Any work activity that can be described as dangerous
options.C: Something with the potential to cause injury
options.D: The chance that a hazard will cause harm, considered together with how serious that harm could be

questions.explanation: A hazard is something with the potential to cause harm. Risk concerns the chance that harm will occur and the possible severity of its consequences; it is not simply the unsafe thing or activity itself.

B.text: Calling work dangerous identifies concern but does not evaluate how likely harm is or how severe it could be.

C.text: Something with potential to cause harm defines a hazard; risk evaluates that potential in its circumstances.

D.text: A hazard is something with the potential to cause harm. Risk concerns the chance that harm will occur and the possible severity of its consequences; it is not simply the unsafe thing or activity itself.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following must be in a company's written Health and Safety Policy:

options.A: Aims and objectives of the company
options.C: Name of the Health and Safety Adviser
options.D: Organization and arrangements in force for carrying out the health and safety policy

questions.explanation: This is a specific requirement of the Health and Safety at Work Act.

A.text: Aims belong in the statement of intent, but this choice omits the required responsibilities and practical arrangements.

B.text: A director's private address is not part of the policy structure and contributes nothing to managing workplace risk.

C.text: Naming an adviser does not allocate all responsibilities or describe the systems through which the policy operates.

D.text: This is a specific requirement of the Health and Safety at Work Act.

questions.prompt: What do the letters CDM stand for?

options.D: Control of Demolition and Management Regulations

questions.explanation: The CDM Regulations impose duties to manage construction projects, ensure physical safeguards are provided to prevent danger during such projects and that adequate welfare facilities are provided.

B.text: The CDM Regulations impose duties to manage construction projects, ensure physical safeguards are provided to prevent danger during such projects and that adequate welfare facilities are provided.

C.text: Dangerous materials are addressed by regimes such as COSHH; they are not the expansion of CDM.

D.text: This rearrangement omits Construction and Design, the two defining words in the Regulations' title.

questions.prompt: In addition to preserving fire separation between areas of a building, which other important fire safety function can fire-stopping achieve?
questions.explanation: Many structural elements such as timber joists, studs and steel beams lose strength quickly in a fire and rely on their linings for protection. A.text: Many structural elements such as timber joists, studs and steel beams lose strength quickly in a fire and rely on their linings for protection. Fire-stopping the gaps where services pass through maintains that protection, so the structure stays standing long enough for people to escape.

B.text: Acoustic sealing may be a secondary benefit, but it is not the additional life-safety function being tested here.

C.text: Nuisance alarms concern detection-system design; sealing service penetrations does not prevent detector activation.

D.text: Energy efficiency can improve when gaps are sealed, but it does not describe fire-stopping's structural protection role.

questions.prompt: The purpose of fire-stopping in a building is to:

options.B: Delay the passage of fire and smoke through openings in walls and floors

questions.explanation: Fire-stopping is a passive fire protection measure used to seal any openings created in a fire resistance-rated wall or floor assembly, e.g. to allow pipes or wiring systems to pass through. During fire conditions this will impede the spread of fire and smoke.

A.text: Sprinkler activation is an active-system function; fire-stopping is passive protection within walls and floors.

B.text: Fire-stopping is a passive fire protection measure used to seal any openings created in a fire resistance-rated wall or floor assembly, e.g. to allow pipes or wiring systems to pass through. During fire conditions this will impede the spread of fire and smoke.

C.text: Fire-stopping cannot prevent ignition, but it can contain the products of a fire after one starts.

D.text: Alarm initiation belongs to detectors and call points, not to the material sealing a compartment boundary.

questions.prompt: What can help to prevent harm to the environment from oil spillages?

questions.explanation: The use of a bund (fully walled storage area) or a drip tray will help any spillage to be contained in a small area for clear up. Any spillage could get into the ground or drains, which is likely to be an offence under environmental legislation.

questions.prompt: Under environmental law, which statement is true?

options.A: Companies and individuals can be prosecuted if they do not follow the law
options.B: Companies can be prosecuted, but not individuals
options.C: It is legal to disturb protected species' habitats
options.D: It is legal to transport business waste without proper paperwork

questions.explanation: Most environmental law is enforced against companies, but the regulator in the relevant part of the UK (the Environment Agency, SEPA or NIEA) can also prosecute company officers and even have powers to prosecute employees if they wilfully contribute to environmental harm.

A.text: Most environmental law is enforced against companies, but the regulator in the relevant part of the UK (the Environment Agency, SEPA or NIEA) can also prosecute company officers and even have powers to prosecute employees if they wilfully contribute to environmental harm.

B.text: Individuals as well as companies can commit environmental offences depending on their acts and responsibilities.

C.text: Protected species and habitats are subject to controls; deliberate disturbance is not generally lawful.

D.text: Business waste movements require the appropriate duty-of-care documentation and an authorised carrier or recipient.

questions.prompt: Which of the following work procedures on electrical systems will always require a permit-to-work to be issued?
questions.explanation: An electrical permit-to-work should state what circuit or equipment has been made safe, how that has been achieved and what work is to be done. A.text: An electrical permit-to-work should state what circuit or equipment has been made safe, how that has been achieved and what work is to be done. A permit should not, therefore, be used for live working. Such a permit is always required for work on high-voltage systems, but can also be used for low-voltage systems.

B.text: Low-voltage dead work often uses secure isolation procedures, but it does not invariably require a formal permit.

C.text: High-voltage live work is exceptional and governed by specialised safety rules; a dead-work permit does not authorise it.

questions.prompt: The use of a multi-lock hasp with the appropriate number of padlocks is a recommended method of safe isolation where:

options.C: More than one person will be working on circuits supplied from the same distribution board
options.D: You know the health and safety inspector is in the area

questions.explanation: When several people work on circuits from one board, each fits their own padlock to the hasp so the isolator cannot be switched back on until everyone has finished and removed their lock. This guarantees no one re-energises the supply while another worker is still exposed.

A.text: The need for a hasp comes from multiple personal locks, not from the absence of a device for one circuit-breaker.

B.text: Unidentified circuits must be traced and labelled; a multi-lock hasp cannot correct uncertainty about the isolation point.

C.text: When several people work on circuits from one board, each fits their own padlock to the hasp so the isolator cannot be switched back on until everyone has finished and removed their lock. This guarantees no one re-energises the supply while another worker is still exposed.

D.text: Isolation arrangements are based on people exposed to reconnection risk, not on whether an inspector is nearby.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is classed as hazardous/special waste?
questions.explanation: Hazardous wastes (special wastes in Scotland) are specified in waste legislation. Fluorescent tubes are included because of their mercury content.

A.text: Empty cement bags are normally a non-hazardous construction waste stream when uncontaminated and correctly segregated.

B.text: Hazardous wastes (special wastes in Scotland) are specified in waste legislation. Fluorescent tubes are included because of their mercury content.

C.text: Non-asbestos insulation is not automatically hazardous, although dust and product-specific controls may still be needed.

D.text: Clean polythene and shrink wrap are generally segregated for recycling rather than treated as hazardous waste.

questions.prompt: What colour cable USUALLY signifies 110 volt power supply on site?
questions.explanation: Yellow is the recognised site colour for 110 V reduced low voltage equipment, used on cables, plugs, sockets and transformers. The colour lets workers instantly identify the safer 110 V centre-tapped supply and distinguish it from 230 V blue equipment.

A.text: Black is not the recognised site connector and cable identification for the 110 V reduced-low-voltage system.

B.text: Blue is associated with the 230 V range and would risk connecting equipment to the wrong nominal supply.

C.text: Red is associated with 400 V three-phase supplies, not the ordinary 110 V site-tool system.

D.text: Yellow is the recognised site colour for 110 V reduced low voltage equipment, used on cables, plugs, sockets and transformers. The colour lets workers instantly identify the safer 110 V centre-tapped supply and distinguish it from 230 V blue equipment.

questions.prompt: The probes of voltage detectors and test instruments used on electrical systems should be:

options.D: Shaped or have barriers to prevent finger contact with the tips

questions.explanation: In addition, to protect against damage by overcurrent whilst in use, the probes or instrument should incorporate suitable high breaking capacity (hbc) fuses with a low current rating (usually not exceeding 500 mA), or current-limiting resistors.

A.text: Calibration evidence concerns instrument accuracy; it does not stop a finger sliding onto an exposed probe tip.

B.text: Colour can help identification but provides no physical protection against touching conductive metal.

C.text: Country of manufacture does not determine probe safety; construction, ratings and exposed-tip protection do.

D.text: In addition, to protect against damage by overcurrent whilst in use, the probes or instrument should incorporate suitable high breaking capacity (hbc) fuses with a low current rating (usually not exceeding 500 mA), or current-limiting resistors.

questions.prompt: A mobile plant operator can let you ride in the machine:

options.B: If it is designed to carry passengers
options.D: If you have a long way to go

questions.explanation: You may only ride in mobile plant that is purpose-built with a proper passenger seat. Climbing onto machines not designed to carry people risks falls, crushing or being struck by moving parts, so it is forbidden however convenient it seems.

A.text: Plant must never carry people on steps, buckets or other undesigned positions merely because the operator agrees.

B.text: You may only ride in mobile plant that is purpose-built with a proper passenger seat. Climbing onto machines not designed to carry people risks falls, crushing or being struck by moving parts, so it is forbidden however convenient it seems.

C.text: Rain increases slip and visibility hazards and does not create an exception to passenger-design requirements.

D.text: Journey length cannot justify riding on machinery that lacks a designated seat and restraint.

questions.prompt: Test instruments used for working on electrical systems should:
questions.explanation: To protect the user from electric shock whilst using the instrument, i.e. handling the probes.

A.text: Age does not demonstrate electrical condition or suitability; instruments require appropriate design, maintenance and checks.

B.text: Yellow colour has no protective function and cannot establish voltage rating or finger-safe construction.

C.text: To protect the user from electric shock whilst using the instrument, i.e. handling the probes.

D.text: Bare probes increase the chance of bridging conductors or touching live metal and conflict with safe test-lead guidance.

questions.prompt: To prove a circuit or equipment is dead after isolation what is the FIRST activity in the sequence of events?

options.C: Check that the voltage detector is working on a proving device, known live source or in- built test feature
options.D: Make sure equipment is not working

questions.explanation: This will prove that that the voltage detector (such as a two-pole voltage detector or proprietary test lamp) is working, i.e. indicating voltage.

A.text: Testing line to earth is part of proving dead, but the detector must first be proved functional.

B.text: A line-neutral test can falsely reassure if the detector has failed; pre-use proving must precede circuit measurements.

C.text: This will prove that that the voltage detector (such as a two-pole voltage detector or proprietary test lamp) is working, i.e. indicating voltage.

D.text: Equipment not operating may result from a control fault and does not prove every conductor is dead.

questions.prompt: What must be considered first when planning to carry out work in a confined space?

options.A: Can the work be done from the outside
options.C: Has the job been priced properly
options.D: Have the correct tools been arranged

questions.explanation: Working outside will remove the risks of working in the confined space.

A.text: Working outside will remove the risks of working in the confined space.

B.text: Staffing is considered only after establishing that entry is unavoidable and assessing the confined-space hazards.

C.text: Commercial pricing cannot determine whether a worker should be exposed to a dangerous enclosed atmosphere.

D.text: Tool selection follows the safe method; arranging tools first assumes entry before avoidance has been considered.

questions.prompt: While digging a trench, you uncover a length of yellow marker tape at a depth of about 150mm. What does the presence of the marker tape mean?

options.A: The area has a high water-table and precautions must be taken to prevent an in-rush of water
options.B: The excavation has reached a depth where the sides must now be supported
options.C: There is a buried electrical cable and further excavation must be carried out with care
options.D: There is contaminated soil below the level of the marker tape and all excavation must stop

questions.explanation: The coloured tape indicates that there are buried services below the route of the tape.

A.text: Electrical warning tape identifies a service route, not groundwater conditions or a need to dewater the excavation.

B.text: Support requirements depend on ground and excavation risk, not on the colour of buried service marker tape.

C.text: The coloured tape indicates that there are buried services below the route of the tape.

D.text: Contaminated land requires separate evidence and controls; yellow service tape is not a soil-contamination marker.

questions.prompt: How often should user (visual) checks be carried out on portable electrical equipment?
questions.explanation: All items of portable electrical equipment should be visually checked for safety by the user before being put into use.

A.text: An annual check can miss damage for many months on equipment that is handled and moved repeatedly.

B.text: Daily checking is too infrequent where the same item changes users or is used several times in one day.

C.text: All items of portable electrical equipment should be visually checked for safety by the user before being put into use.

D.text: Weekly inspection leaves each use dependent on conditions that may have changed since the previous check.

questions.prompt: If you are about to use a power tool and discover the guard is missing, you should:

options.A: Make up a temporary guard yourself
options.B: Not use the tool until a proper guard has been fitted
options.C: Use the tool but try to work quickly
options.D: Use the tool but work carefully and slowly

questions.explanation: Visual checks should be carried out before using equipment. Any faults should be reported immediately and rectified before use.

A.text: A homemade guard lacks the tool's tested strength, clearances and interlocks and may create new trapping hazards.

B.text: Visual checks should be carried out before using equipment. Any faults should be reported immediately and rectified before use.

C.text: Working quickly increases loss-of-control risk and gives no protection from the exposed moving part.

D.text: Slow operation does not prevent contact, ejection or entanglement with an unguarded power tool.

questions.prompt: What is the best method of securing a ladder?

options.B: Tying it to a suitable point
options.C: Using an effective ladder stability device
options.D: Wedging the ladder (eg against a wall)

questions.explanation: Tying the ladder is the safest option, making sure both stiles are tied.

A.text: Footing depends on another person's continuous attention and is HSE's last-resort method when securing is not practicable.

B.text: Tying the ladder is the safest option, making sure both stiles are tied.

C.text: A stability device is useful where tying is not practicable, but positive tying remains the preferred method listed.

D.text: Wedging can move or crush and does not provide the reliable upper restraint achieved by tying to a sound point.

questions.prompt: The electric drill you are about to use has a faulty on/off switch. What action should you take?

options.A: Find another machine and carry on working
options.B: Stop work and inform your supervisor
options.C: Tape the switch on to keep it running and carry on working

questions.explanation: A faulty on/off switch means the tool cannot be reliably controlled or stopped, which is dangerous. You should stop, take it out of use and report it so it can be repaired or replaced; you must never bodge or keep using defective equipment.

A.text: Using another drill may keep the task moving, but the defective tool remains unreported and available to others.

B.text: A faulty on/off switch means the tool cannot be reliably controlled or stopped, which is dangerous. You should stop, take it out of use and report it so it can be repaired or replaced; you must never bodge or keep using defective equipment.

C.text: Taping a switch on removes control of the tool and can cause unexpected starting or inability to stop it.

D.text: Untrained repair can expose live parts or defeat safety features; the fault requires competent attention.

questions.prompt: When should visual checks of portable hand-held equipment be made by the user?
questions.explanation: The user needs to be satisfied that the tool has no obvious defect before use.

A.text: The user needs to be satisfied that the tool has no obvious defect before use.

B.text: A monthly interval cannot catch damage that occurs during a particular use or between scheduled checks.

C.text: Weekly checking is not enough for a user check because condition may change each time equipment is handled.

D.text: Waiting until replacement is needed abandons the preventive purpose of finding defects before exposure.

questions.prompt: A working platform used for construction work, and from which a person could fall 2 metres or more, must not be used unless it has been inspected (and a report is subsequently prepared) by a competent person:
questions.explanation: Under these specific circumstances a report is required to be prepared by the competent person and given to the person for whom the inspection was done (e.g. the site manager). This is in addition to the more general requirement to inspect equipment for work at height: prior to use in that position (or site if it is mobile); following exceptional circumstances (e.g. high winds); and at suitable intervals.

A.text: An accident triggers an additional inspection, but it is not the only event requiring a platform inspection.

B.text: Inspection on the same day may be prudent but is not the maximum recurring seven-day interval stated in the Regulations.

C.text: A month is too long between recorded inspections for a construction working platform from which a person may fall.

D.text: Under these specific circumstances a report is required to be prepared by the competent person and given to the person for whom the inspection was done (e.g. the site manager). This is in addition to the more general requirement to inspect equipment for work at height: prior to use in that position (or site if it is mobile); following exceptional circumstances (e.g. high winds); and at suitable intervals.

questions.prompt: If work on or near a fragile roof cannot be avoided, which listed measure is part of the required fall-protection approach?

options.A: As long as you avoid any fragile areas it is safe
options.B: Use suitable stagings or platforms and combine them with appropriate edge protection and measures that prevent or mitigate a fall
options.C: It is safe to walk on the purlins
options.D: Walk straight across the roof to where you need to get to

questions.explanation: HSE's first requirement is to avoid work on or near a fragile surface where possible. Where access is unavoidable, a planned combination of stagings or platforms, guardrails, coverings, restraint or arrest and safety nets is normally needed; a crawling board by itself is not a complete control system.

A.text: Fragile areas may be hidden or poorly marked, and simply intending to avoid them provides no fall prevention.
