B.text: HSE's first requirement is to avoid work on or near a fragile surface where possible. Where access is unavoidable, a planned combination of stagings or platforms, guardrails, coverings, restraint or arrest and safety nets is normally needed; a crawling board by itself is not a complete control system.

C.text: Purlins are not designed as access routes and a slip can put the worker directly onto a fragile sheet.

D.text: Crossing directly gives no protection against misidentified panels, loss of balance or a surface failing unexpectedly.

questions.prompt: In an emergency situation at work you should do what?

options.A: Ensure your work mates are all accounted for

questions.explanation: A site emergency plan should have been drawn up and you should be familiar with the emergency procedure.

A.text: Accounting for colleagues is a designated marshal's function within the plan, not a reason to delay following the procedure.

B.text: Leaving by an unplanned route may enter the hazard area and prevents an accurate roll call at the assembly point.

C.text: A site emergency plan should have been drawn up and you should be familiar with the emergency procedure.

D.text: HSE is not the site's emergency-response service; calling it does not replace alarm, evacuation and emergency contacts.

questions.prompt: What does the sound of a siren on-site normally indicate?
questions.explanation: A site siren is the general alarm signalling an emergency that requires everyone to respond, usually by evacuating to the assembly point. It is not specific to one hazard, so you treat any siren as a call to leave the area immediately.

A.text: Fire may be one emergency signalled, but workers should follow the site procedure rather than assume one cause.

B.text: A toxic release may use a siren, yet the same general alarm can cover other events requiring different actions.

C.text: A site siren is the general alarm signalling an emergency that requires everyone to respond, usually by evacuating to the assembly point. It is not specific to one hazard, so you treat any siren as a call to leave the area immediately.

D.text: An explosion could trigger the alarm, but the sound itself does not establish that this specific event occurred.

questions.prompt: Most deaths on site are caused by:
questions.explanation: Although the other dangers can kill or cause injury, falling from height is the bigger cause of fatalities.

A.text: Chemical burns cause serious harm but account for a smaller share of construction fatalities than falls from height.

B.text: Although the other dangers can kill or cause injury, falling from height is the bigger cause of fatalities.

C.text: Solvent inhalation is a controlled health risk, not the leading immediate fatal-accident category on sites.

D.text: Vehicle movements kill workers, but current construction statistics still show falls from height as the largest category.

questions.prompt: The rung of a wooden ladder has started to split, what should you do?

options.B: Do not use it, tell your supervisor
options.C: Jump on it to see if it holds your weight

questions.explanation: A split rung can give way under load and cause a serious fall, so the ladder must be taken out of use and reported. Taping or cutting it does not restore its strength, and testing it by standing on it risks injury.

A.text: Cutting the rung changes the ladder's structure and leaves an incomplete climbing surface rather than a sound repair.

B.text: A split rung can give way under load and cause a serious fall, so the ladder must be taken out of use and reported. Taping or cutting it does not restore its strength, and testing it by standing on it risks injury.

C.text: Loading a visibly split rung may make it fail and cause the very fall the check is intended to prevent.

D.text: Tape cannot restore the timber's load capacity and may conceal growth of the split from the next user.

questions.prompt: A red-labelled fire extinguisher should NOT be used:

options.D: Where there is a risk of electrocution

questions.explanation: Red denotes water. Liquids should not be used on electrical fires, since they can conduct electricity.

A.text: Water can cool burning clothing once electrical sources are excluded; electrocution is the distinctive prohibition here.

B.text: Water is suitable for many ordinary solid combustibles such as furniture when no electrical or liquid-fuel hazard exists.

C.text: Wood is a Class A fuel for which a water extinguisher is normally effective after electrical risks are ruled out.

D.text: Red denotes water. Liquids should not be used on electrical fires, since they can conduct electricity.

questions.prompt: In an on-site emergency, which of the following must a first-aider NOT do?

options.B: Give medicines to patients without authorization

questions.explanation: First-aid is concerned with preserving life and limb, and first-aiders are not trained to dispense medical treatments.

A.text: Controlling severe bleeding with appropriate first-aid measures is within the trained first-aider's role.

B.text: First-aid is concerned with preserving life and limb, and first-aiders are not trained to dispense medical treatments.

C.text: Resuscitation is a core emergency skill and must not be withheld when a casualty is not breathing normally.

D.text: An unconscious casualty requires assessment and appropriate care; unconsciousness is not a reason to avoid treatment.

questions.prompt: A workmate lifting a big box suddenly shouts "oh, my back" and drops the box. What should you do?

options.A: Find them somewhere comfortable to sit and rest
options.B: Help them to lift the box
options.D: Tell them to leave it for someone else to lift

questions.explanation: The priority for any back injury is to obtain first-aid advice, in order to prevent further damage.

A.text: Rest may feel helpful, but sudden back pain after lifting needs assessment before the casualty is moved or work resumes.

B.text: Continuing the lift can worsen the casualty's injury and expose the helper to the same uncontrolled load.

C.text: The priority for any back injury is to obtain first-aid advice, in order to prevent further damage.

D.text: Leaving the box addresses the task but not the injured person, who still needs competent first-aid assessment.

questions.prompt: Which fire extinguisher should not be used on flammable liquid fires?
questions.explanation: Water must never be used on flammable liquid fires because the burning liquid floats on the water and is spread around, enlarging the fire. Foam, CO2 or powder smother the flames and cut off oxygen, which is why they are suitable instead.

A.text: Carbon dioxide can smother a small flammable-liquid fire without spreading the burning liquid across the floor.

B.text: Suitable foam forms a blanket over many flammable liquids and suppresses vapour when used for its rated fire class.

C.text: Dry powder interrupts combustion and is rated for flammable-liquid fires, although its discharge has visibility drawbacks.

D.text: Water must never be used on flammable liquid fires because the burning liquid floats on the water and is spread around, enlarging the fire. Foam, CO2 or powder smother the flames and cut off oxygen, which is why they are suitable instead.

questions.prompt: If you discover a fire at work, what should you do first:

options.A: Raise the alarm and warn fellow workers
options.B: Run around looking for an alarm to sound
options.D: Use a fire extinguisher to put it out

questions.explanation: Raising the alarm will reduce the risk to others, particularly if the fire spreads.

A.text: Raising the alarm will reduce the risk to others, particularly if the fire spreads.

B.text: Searching without immediately warning others delays evacuation; use the nearest recognised alarm method at once.

C.text: Emergency services should be called under the procedure, but people in immediate danger must first be alerted.

D.text: Trying to fight the fire before raising the alarm can trap the worker and leaves everyone else unaware.

questions.prompt: Excessive sunlight on bare skin can cause which serious health problem?
questions.explanation: Ultraviolet rays in sunlight can cause sunburn and premature ageing of the skin. The most serious effect, however, is an increased chance of developing skin cancer.

A.text: Acne is not the principal serious disease linked to cumulative ultraviolet exposure from working in strong sunlight.

B.text: Some exposures cause dermatitis, but ultraviolet radiation's major long-term danger is malignant skin change.

C.text: Rickets is associated with vitamin D deficiency, not excessive ultraviolet exposure to bare skin.

D.text: Ultraviolet rays in sunlight can cause sunburn and premature ageing of the skin. The most serious effect, however, is an increased chance of developing skin cancer.

questions.prompt: Asbestos is suspected in the workplace, during renovation do you:
questions.explanation: Competent advice must be sought, to prevent exposure to the worker or others, either at the time, or subsequently.

A.text: Ignoring suspected asbestos can release fibres during further disturbance and expose everyone in the work area.

B.text: Painting does not identify the material or make unplanned drilling, cutting or removal safe.

C.text: Removal is licensed or specially controlled work in many circumstances and must not start on suspicion alone.

D.text: Competent advice must be sought, to prevent exposure to the worker or others, either at the time, or subsequently.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not required to be provided under the Construction (Design and Management) Regulations?
questions.explanation: Guidance on the provision of welfare facilities as required by CDM is given in HSE publication 'Health and Safety in Construction'.

A.text: Wholesome drinking water is a required basic welfare provision from the start of construction work.

B.text: Guidance on the provision of welfare facilities as required by CDM is given in HSE publication 'Health and Safety in Construction'.

C.text: Suitable sanitary conveniences are mandatory welfare facilities; workers cannot be expected to find their own.

D.text: Washing facilities are required to protect hygiene and health, with additional provision where work creates contamination.

questions.prompt: A colleague has drilled holes in the top of his safety helmet because the weather is hot. Is this:

options.B: Acceptable if the holes are small

questions.explanation: Interfering with or misusing items provided in the interests of health, safety or welfare is an offence under the HSW Act 1974 (section 8).

A.text: Drilling the shell invalidates its tested construction and can reduce impact and penetration resistance.

B.text: Even small holes create stress concentrations and unauthorised modification; size does not make the alteration acceptable.

C.text: PPE must be used according to instructions, so its wearer cannot choose to weaken or modify it.

D.text: Interfering with or misusing items provided in the interests of health, safety or welfare is an offence under the HSW Act 1974 (section 8).

questions.prompt: Why should a high visibility vest be worn when working on roads?

options.A: Because it will keep you warm
options.B: Because you were told to do so
options.C: So road users and plant operators can see you
options.D: So that your mates can see you

questions.explanation: So road users and plant operators can see you is correct because site transport and plant risks are controlled by separation, competence, visibility, and following the planned system of work. The chosen option reduces the chance of being struck or crushed.

A.text: A high-visibility vest is not thermal clothing and may provide little insulation in cold conditions.

B.text: Following an instruction is required, but it does not explain the road-traffic hazard that the garment controls.

C.text: So road users and plant operators can see you is correct because site transport and plant risks are controlled by separation, competence, visibility, and following the planned system of work. The chosen option reduces the chance of being struck or crushed.

D.text: Colleague recognition is secondary; the critical need is early detection by approaching drivers and mobile-plant operators.

questions.prompt: If you are drilling into concrete with a masonry drill, in which one of the following circumstances will you need to wear eye protection?

options.B: Not if drilling into the floor
options.C: Only if the drill is bigger than 10mm

questions.explanation: Suitable eye protection must always be worn when working with power-driven tools where chippings are likely to fly or abrasive materials could be propelled.

A.text: Suitable eye protection must always be worn when working with power-driven tools where chippings are likely to fly or abrasive materials could be propelled.

B.text: Floor drilling can still eject sharp aggregate and dust upward or sideways into the operator's eyes.

C.text: A small bit can release high-speed fragments just as readily; bit diameter is not the trigger for protection.

D.text: Overhead work increases exposure but is not the only orientation in which concrete particles can strike the eye.

questions.prompt: Why is it important to report 'near miss' accidents to your employer?

options.B: So lessons can be learned, preventing an accident next time
options.C: So that someone can be disciplined
options.D: To make the figures look good

questions.explanation: The HSE advises that 'near misses' should be investigated to prevent their recurrence.

A.text: Not every near miss is itself RIDDOR-reportable, so prevention rather than a blanket statutory report is the reason.

B.text: The HSE advises that 'near misses' should be investigated to prevent their recurrence.

C.text: Discipline-focused reporting discourages openness and does not address the conditions that could injure someone next time.

D.text: Near-miss reporting can initially raise figures; its purpose is learning and risk reduction, not cosmetic statistics.

questions.prompt: When working in dusty conditions, what of the following would give the LEAST level of protection?
questions.explanation: Protection factors are given in HSE publication HSG53 'Respiratory protective equipment at work - A practical guide'

A.text: A supplied-air helmet provides clean air and a high assigned protection factor when correctly selected and used.

B.text: Protection factors are given in HSE publication HSG53 'Respiratory protective equipment at work - A practical guide'

C.text: A positive-pressure powered respirator generally provides greater inward-leakage protection than a negative-pressure half mask.

D.text: Self-contained breathing apparatus supplies its own breathable air and provides far higher protection for suitable trained use.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following is classified as a reportable occupational disease under RIDDOR?
questions.explanation: Certain occupational diseases likely to have been caused or made worse by work are reportable under RIDDOR. This would include occupational asthma where the person's work includes significant or regular exposure to a known respiratory sensitizer.

A.text: Amputation is a reportable specified injury caused by an incident, not an occupational disease diagnosis.

B.text: Ordinary influenza is infectious illness and is not the work-caused respiratory sensitisation category listed here.

C.text: Mental ill health is important but is not included as a reportable occupational disease under the listed RIDDOR categories.

D.text: Certain occupational diseases likely to have been caused or made worse by work are reportable under RIDDOR. This would include occupational asthma where the person's work includes significant or regular exposure to a known respiratory sensitizer.

questions.prompt: When picking up an object, you should:

options.C: Adopt a stable stance, keep the load close and use a slight bend of the back, hips and knees without further flexing the back while lifting

questions.explanation: Current HSE guidance does not prescribe a deep squat or simply say 'bend your knees'. Use a stable position, secure hold and slight bend at the back, hips and knees, keep the load close and move smoothly without twisting or further back flexion.

A.text: Arm position alone does not stabilise the body or control back loading, grip, load distance and twisting.

B.text: Deliberately bending through the back while lifting increases spinal loading and loss of control.

C.text: Current HSE guidance does not prescribe a deep squat or simply say 'bend your knees'. Use a stable position, secure hold and slight bend at the back, hips and knees, keep the load close and move smoothly without twisting or further back flexion.

D.text: A back brace is not a substitute for avoiding hazardous handling, assessing the task and using sound movement.

questions.prompt: Which would you consider to be generally correct when lifting a load?

options.A: Keep the load away from the body
options.B: Larger loads should be split into smaller loads if possible
options.C: The feet should be together and the load lifted at arm's length
options.D: When lifting you should bend your back

questions.explanation: Splitting a large load into smaller, more manageable loads reduces the weight handled at one time and the strain on the back. Keeping loads close to the body, feet apart and the back straight are the correct techniques, which the other options reverse.

A.text: Holding a load away from the trunk greatly increases leverage and stress on the back and shoulders.

B.text: Splitting a large load into smaller, more manageable loads reduces the weight handled at one time and the strain on the back. Keeping loads close to the body, feet apart and the back straight are the correct techniques, which the other options reverse.

C.text: Feet together reduce stability, while an arm's-length load creates unnecessary leverage and poor control.

D.text: Further flexing a bent back under load is specifically avoided in HSE's handling technique guidance.

questions.prompt: Under RIDDOR, which one of the following must be reported to the enforcing authority?

options.A: Accidents where the injured person wishes to make a claim
options.B: All 'near misses' even if no one is hurt
options.D: Fracture other than to fingers, thumbs or toes

questions.explanation: This is one of a number of reportable 'specified injuries' and must be reported to the enforcing authority under the Reporting of Injuries, Diseases and Dangerous Occurrences Regulations (RIDDOR).

A.text: A possible civil claim does not determine RIDDOR status; the event and injury category do.

B.text: Near misses are valuable internally, but only listed dangerous occurrences require notification when nobody is hurt.

C.text: Minor injuries belong in workplace records but are not all reportable to the enforcing authority.

D.text: This is one of a number of reportable 'specified injuries' and must be reported to the enforcing authority under the Reporting of Injuries, Diseases and Dangerous Occurrences Regulations (RIDDOR).

questions.prompt: What would you NOT consider in making a judgement of the risks from a load?
questions.explanation: A, C and D can all affect the difficulty of lifting an object.

A.text: An offset centre of gravity changes how a load tips and how close its heavy side must be held.

B.text: A, C and D can all affect the difficulty of lifting an object.

C.text: Size, damage and shape affect grip, visibility, stability and whether mechanical assistance is needed.

D.text: Weight directly affects handling force and must be considered alongside posture, frequency and capability.

questions.prompt: In manual handling, which of the following general statements is true?

options.A: Anyone can carry any load as long as they are strong enough
options.B: Large loads should be broken down into smaller loads where possible
options.C: Loads should be held at arm's length while carrying
options.D: You should keep your back bent when lifting

questions.explanation: Breaking a large load into smaller portions lowers the weight lifted in one go, reducing the risk of back and muscle injury. Carrying at arm's length or with a bent back increases strain, and capacity depends on the person and load, not just strength.

A.text: Strength alone does not control posture, repetition, grip, route or sudden movement, so it cannot make any load acceptable.

B.text: Breaking a large load into smaller portions lowers the weight lifted in one go, reducing the risk of back and muscle injury. Carrying at arm's length or with a bent back increases strain, and capacity depends on the person and load, not just strength.

C.text: Arm's-length carrying multiplies back and shoulder loading; loads should normally be kept close.

D.text: Maintaining a bent back while force is applied increases strain and conflicts with controlled handling guidance.

questions.prompt: The Health and Safety (Safety Signs and Signals) Regulations require the colour coding of safety signs. What colours are used on a sign indicating a prohibited activity, for example "No access for pedestrians"?
questions.explanation: Prohibitory signs are round and feature a black pictogram on a white background with red edging and diagonal line.

A.text: Blue and white communicates a mandatory positive instruction rather than an activity that is forbidden.

B.text: Green and white identifies a safe condition or emergency facility and does not prohibit pedestrian entry.

C.text: Prohibitory signs are round and feature a black pictogram on a white background with red edging and diagonal line.

D.text: Yellow and black warns of a hazard; prohibition requires the red circular form with black and white detail.

questions.prompt: Under the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974, which of the following have a duty to work safely?
questions.explanation: Employers, employees and the self-employed all have duties to work safely under the Act.

A.text: Employers, employees and the self-employed all have duties to work safely under the Act.

B.text: Employees have duties, but employers and self-employed people also must conduct work without endangering others.

C.text: Employers carry overarching duties, yet workers must also take reasonable care and cooperate with controls.

D.text: Members of the public are protected by work duties, but the question asks who at work carries a duty to work safely.

questions.prompt: What do the letters ACoP stand for?
questions.explanation: An ACOP is a code of practice approved by the Health and Safety Executive (or the Health and Safety Commission prior to April 2008).

A.text: The statutory term is Approved, not Accepted; an ACOP has a specific evidential status under health and safety law.

B.text: Neither 'Accepted' nor 'Provisions' forms the recognised title used for HSE-approved practical guidance.

C.text: An ACOP is a code of practice approved by the Health and Safety Executive (or the Health and Safety Commission prior to April 2008).

D.text: An ACOP is a Code of Practice, not a single approved condition attached to an activity.

questions.prompt: Complete the following sentence: A risk assessment

options.A: Is a means of analysing what might go wrong
options.B: Is a piece of paper required by law

questions.explanation: Risk assessment involves a careful review of what can cause harm and the practical measures to be taken to reduce the risk of harm.

A.text: Risk assessment involves a careful review of what can cause harm and the practical measures to be taken to reduce the risk of harm.

B.text: The assessment is a decision process, not merely paperwork; recording supports rather than replaces analysis and action.

C.text: A suitable assessment guides priorities and controls and is central to preventing harm, not an optional administrative exercise.

D.text: Assessment alone cannot prevent an accident unless its findings are implemented, monitored and revised when conditions change.

questions.prompt: Who should sign the statement of intent in a company's health and safety policy?

options.C: The employer or most senior person in the company

questions.explanation: HSE says the employer or most senior person should sign the policy statement and review it regularly. That may be the managing director in one company, but the role rather than a particular job title is the governing principle.

A.text: A safety officer may advise and administer the system, but the most senior leadership must own the statement of intent.

B.text: Company-secretary status does not necessarily carry executive control over the undertaking's health and safety commitments.

C.text: HSE says the employer or most senior person should sign the policy statement and review it regularly. That may be the managing director in one company, but the role rather than a particular job title is the governing principle.

D.text: A site manager controls a location but is not ordinarily the most senior person responsible for the company-wide policy.

questions.prompt: Identify one method of enforcing regulations that are available to the Health and Safety Executive:
questions.explanation: An Improvement Notice is a formal HSE enforcement tool requiring a duty holder to correct a breach of health and safety law within a set time. It is one of the statutory powers inspectors hold, alongside the Prohibition Notice that stops dangerous activity at once.

A.text: 'Health Notice' is not one of the statutory improvement or prohibition notices used to enforce these duties.

B.text: An Improvement Notice is a formal HSE enforcement tool requiring a duty holder to correct a breach of health and safety law within a set time. It is one of the statutory powers inspectors hold, alongside the Prohibition Notice that stops dangerous activity at once.

C.text: Insurance pricing is a commercial consequence and is not an enforcement power available to HSE inspectors.

D.text: Obstruction may be an offence, but an 'Obstruction Notice' is not the statutory notice described here.

questions.prompt: If you discover a hole or gap in a fire rated wall or floor that has not been fire-stopped, what should you do?

options.A: Cover the hole or gap with insulating tape
options.B: Use decorators' sealant to fill the gap
options.C: Ignore it unless it is causing a draught
options.D: Report it to your supervisor without delay

questions.explanation: Reference: Supervisors need to be made aware of any observed inadequacies in fire-stopping - which can undermine fire precautions catastrophically during the construction of buildings and on their completion. Only a limited range of products are suitable and they must be correctly applied to provide the required degree of fire-stopping.

A.text: Insulating tape has no tested fire-resistance rating and cannot reinstate a breached fire compartment.

B.text: Ordinary decorators' sealant is not a certified fire-stopping system matched to the wall or floor construction.

C.text: A draught is irrelevant: any unsealed penetration can let smoke and flame bypass the fire-rated barrier.

D.text: Reference: Supervisors need to be made aware of any observed inadequacies in fire-stopping - which can undermine fire precautions catastrophically during the construction of buildings and on their completion. Only a limited range of products are suitable and they must be correctly applied to provide the required degree of fire-stopping.

questions.prompt: In addition to preserving fire separation between areas of a building, which other important fire safety function can fire-stopping achieve?
questions.explanation: Reference: During the fire, it is essential that the load-bearing capacity of elements of the building structure are maintained until the occupants have escaped. Timber studs, joists or 'I' beams, for example, may only have a short survival time if exposed to fire and may rely on linings, such as plasterboard ceiling, for fire resistance. Services passing through such linings should therefore be fire-stopped.

A.text: Reference: During the fire, it is essential that the load-bearing capacity of elements of the building structure are maintained until the occupants have escaped. Timber studs, joists or 'I' beams, for example, may only have a short survival time if exposed to fire and may rely on linings, such as plasterboard ceiling, for fire resistance. Services passing through such linings should therefore be fire-stopped.

B.text: Nuisance alarms concern detection-system design; sealing service penetrations does not prevent detector activation.

C.text: Energy efficiency can improve when gaps are sealed, but it does not describe fire-stopping's structural protection role.

D.text: Acoustic sealing may be a secondary benefit, but it is not the additional life-safety function being tested here.

questions.prompt: Intumescent materials used to provide fire-stopping are designed to:
questions.explanation: Reference: A limited number of fire-resistant materials may be used to provide fire-stopping. These include intumescent products, which are designed to expand and provide fire-stopping when subjected to heat. Examples include intumescent 'pillows' (used to provide internal sealing of trunking) and intumescent mastic.

A.text: Intumescent compounds react to elevated temperature, not merely to the presence of smoke particles.

B.text: Shrinking would enlarge the penetration during a fire; intumescent material must swell to close the opening.

C.text: Blocking sound is an acoustic treatment and does not describe the heat-driven action of an intumescent product.

D.text: Reference: A limited number of fire-resistant materials may be used to provide fire-stopping. These include intumescent products, which are designed to expand and provide fire-stopping when subjected to heat. Examples include intumescent 'pillows' (used to provide internal sealing of trunking) and intumescent mastic.

questions.prompt: The purpose of fire-stopping in a building is to:

options.C: Delay the passage of fire and smoke through openings in walls and floors

questions.explanation: Reference: Fire-stopping is a passive fire protection measure used to seal any openings created in a fire resistance-rated wall or floor assembly, e.g. to allow pipes or wiring systems to pass through. During fire conditions this will impede the spread of fire and smoke.

A.text: Fire-stopping cannot prevent ignition, but it can contain the products of a fire after one starts.

B.text: Sprinkler activation is an active-system function; fire-stopping is passive protection within walls and floors.

C.text: Reference: Fire-stopping is a passive fire protection measure used to seal any openings created in a fire resistance-rated wall or floor assembly, e.g. to allow pipes or wiring systems to pass through. During fire conditions this will impede the spread of fire and smoke.

D.text: Alarm initiation belongs to detectors and call points, not to the material sealing a compartment boundary.

questions.prompt: What are fire-stops designed to do?

options.B: Protect services (such as wiring systems) against fire damage
options.D: Delay the passage of fire and smoke through openings in walls and floors

questions.explanation: Reference: Fire-stops are designed to maintain the fireproofing of a wall or floor assembly. Fire-stopping delays the spread of fire and, generally, the spread of smoke as well.

A.text: Door closers act on fire doors; fire-stops seal gaps and service penetrations in compartment boundaries.

B.text: The main purpose is to maintain compartmentation, not to shield the cable or pipe itself from heat damage.

C.text: Fire-stopping contains fire and smoke but does not extinguish the burning material or replace firefighting equipment.

D.text: Reference: Fire-stops are designed to maintain the fireproofing of a wall or floor assembly. Fire-stopping delays the spread of fire and, generally, the spread of smoke as well.

questions.prompt: When storing liquids (such as oils, fuels or chemicals) on-site, what must you do?

options.A: Keep the tops off, to prevent pressure from building up
options.B: Store them in suitable closed and labelled containers, securely and away from traffic, with containment such as a bund or drip tray where leakage could pollute
options.C: Use a transparent container so you can check how much liquid is in it

questions.explanation: Site liquids must be stored in suitable compatible containers, identified and secured against damage or unauthorised access. Where a leak could pollute land or drains, appropriate secondary containment is also needed; simply putting a container out of traffic is not enough.

A.text: Open containers allow vapour, rain ingress and spills and are not a safe means of relieving pressure.

B.text: Site liquids must be stored in suitable compatible containers, identified and secured against damage or unauthorised access. Where a leak could pollute land or drains, appropriate secondary containment is also needed; simply putting a container out of traffic is not enough.

C.text: Transparency does not establish compatibility, labelling, security or secondary containment for a hazardous liquid.

D.text: The nearest container may be incompatible, unlabelled or damaged and cannot be chosen merely for convenience.

questions.prompt: From an environmental point of view, why should materials be reused, where possible?

options.C: A lot of energy and raw materials go into making most construction products
options.D: It makes less mess on site

questions.explanation: Reference: Although reducing the amount of waste is the first priority, the re-use of materials can also contribute to effective waste management.

A.text: Reuse is not justified by a blanket European-law requirement; its benefit comes from conserving resources and energy.

B.text: Client savings may follow, but cost alone is not the environmental reason for retaining useful material.

C.text: Reference: Although reducing the amount of waste is the first priority, the re-use of materials can also contribute to effective waste management.

D.text: Less mess is useful housekeeping, but it does not explain the upstream environmental cost avoided by reuse.

questions.prompt: If you have unused material left, what should you do before you consider putting non-hazardous waste items into a skip?

options.A: Put it in a plastic bag and put it in a skip
options.C: Make sure there is a label on it
options.D: Check whether someone else on your team can make use of it

questions.explanation: Reference: Although reducing the amount of waste is the first priority, the reuse of waste materials is much better than disposal, which is the most expensive option and which should be the last resort. Reuse is a better waste management option than recovery.

A.text: Discarding a usable remainder creates avoidable waste before reuse by the team has been considered.

B.text: Weight may affect handling or waste records but does not determine whether another worker can use the material.

C.text: Labelling helps identify material but does not itself prevent a useful item from entering the waste stream.

D.text: Reference: Although reducing the amount of waste is the first priority, the reuse of waste materials is much better than disposal, which is the most expensive option and which should be the last resort. Reuse is a better waste management option than recovery.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a suitable means of isolating a circuit?

options.A: Fitting a padlocked circuit breaker lockout
options.B: Removing a fuse and locking the distribution board
options.D: Putting insulating tape over the circuit breaker instead of applying a secure lock-off device

questions.explanation: Tape does not secure an isolating device against inadvertent or unauthorised operation. HSE construction guidance explicitly contrasts tape over a circuit-breaker with a proper lock-off device, personal lock and safety notice.

A.text: A correctly fitted lockout prevents circuit-breaker operation and is a recognised way to secure isolation.

B.text: Removing the fuse and controlling access can provide secure isolation when implemented under the safe system.

C.text: A suitable padlocked isolator provides positive security against inadvertent reconnection by another person.

D.text: Tape does not secure an isolating device against inadvertent or unauthorised operation. HSE construction guidance explicitly contrasts tape over a circuit-breaker with a proper lock-off device, personal lock and safety notice.

questions.prompt: What colour cable USUALLY signifies 110 volt power supply on site?
questions.explanation: Reference: Yellow is the usual colour of cables, socket outlets, plugs and transformers etc which are used with a 110 volt supply.

A.text: Red is associated with 400 V three-phase supplies, not the ordinary 110 V site-tool system.

B.text: Blue is associated with the 230 V range and would risk connecting equipment to the wrong nominal supply.

C.text: Black is not the recognised site connector and cable identification for the 110 V reduced-low-voltage system.

D.text: Reference: Yellow is the usual colour of cables, socket outlets, plugs and transformers etc which are used with a 110 volt supply.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is true with regard to the dangers of electricity?

options.A: Electricity is only dangerous if you are not wearing wellington boots
options.B: Electricity is dangerous at any time because you cannot tell by looking at a cable whether or not it is live
options.C: Electricity is only dangerous in wet weather
options.D: Electricity is perfectly safe so long as you wear cotton gloves

questions.explanation: Reference: The features which make electricity so dangerous are that you cannot see, hear or smell it. It can give you a very unpleasant surprise. Always assume that cables are live.

A.text: Wellington boots are not a universal electrical safeguard and may be wet, damaged or unsuitable for the voltage.

B.text: Reference: The features which make electricity so dangerous are that you cannot see, hear or smell it. It can give you a very unpleasant surprise. Always assume that cables are live.

C.text: Dry weather does not prove a conductor dead or remove the possibility of a fatal current path.

D.text: Cotton gloves have no electrical insulating rating and do not make contact with energised parts safe.

questions.prompt: Test instruments used for working on electrical systems should:
questions.explanation: Reference: To protect the user from electric shock whilst using the instrument, i.e. handling the probes.

A.text: Age does not demonstrate electrical condition or suitability; instruments require appropriate design, maintenance and checks.

B.text: Yellow colour has no protective function and cannot establish voltage rating or finger-safe construction.

C.text: Reference: To protect the user from electric shock whilst using the instrument, i.e. handling the probes.

D.text: Bare probes increase the chance of bridging conductors or touching live metal and conflict with safe test-lead guidance.

questions.prompt: Under Regulation 14 of the Electricity at Work Regulations 1989, when may work on or near a live conductor that may give rise to danger proceed?

options.A: Only when it is unreasonable in all the circumstances for the conductor to be dead, it is reasonable to work live, and suitable precautions are taken to prevent injury
options.B: When the person carrying out the work is a competent person
options.C: When the person working on the equipment is wearing rubber gloves
options.D: When the means of isolation cannot be identified

questions.explanation: All three Regulation 14 conditions must be satisfied. Live work must be justified because making dead is unreasonable, carrying it out live must itself be reasonable, and suitable precautions, including suitable protective equipment where necessary, must prevent injury.

A.text: All three Regulation 14 conditions must be satisfied. Live work must be justified because making dead is unreasonable, carrying it out live must itself be reasonable, and suitable precautions, including suitable protective equipment where necessary, must prevent injury.

B.text: Competence is necessary for dangerous electrical work, but competence alone does not justify leaving the conductor live.

C.text: Rubber gloves are only one possible precaution and cannot replace the three legal conditions for live work.

D.text: Difficulty identifying isolation does not satisfy the statutory tests; the supply must be traced and the work properly planned.

questions.prompt: The lowest level of electrical current which can harm the human body is normally measured in:
questions.explanation: Reference: Research has shown that a person is in serious danger of a fatal electric shock at, or above, approximately 30 milliamps.

A.text: Whole amperes are far above the range where shock can already disrupt breathing or heart rhythm.

B.text: Microamperes are one-thousandth of a milliampere and are generally below the ordinary harmful-shock thresholds discussed.

C.text: Reference: Research has shown that a person is in serious danger of a fatal electric shock at, or above, approximately 30 milliamps.

D.text: Kiloamperes describe fault-current magnitudes, not the small body current capable of causing physiological injury.

questions.prompt: What must be considered first when planning to carry out work in a confined space?

options.B: Can the work be done from the outside
options.C: Has the job been priced properly
options.D: Have the correct tools been arranged

questions.explanation: Reference: Working outside will remove the risks of working in the confined space.

A.text: Staffing is considered only after establishing that entry is unavoidable and assessing the confined-space hazards.

B.text: Reference: Working outside will remove the risks of working in the confined space.

C.text: Commercial pricing cannot determine whether a worker should be exposed to a dangerous enclosed atmosphere.

D.text: Tool selection follows the safe method; arranging tools first assumes entry before avoidance has been considered.

questions.prompt: While digging a trench, you uncover a length of yellow marker tape at a depth of about 150mm. What does the presence of the marker tape mean?

options.A: There is contaminated soil below the level of the marker tape and all excavation must stop
options.B: The area has a high water-table and precautions must be taken to prevent an in-rush of water
options.C: There is a buried electrical cable and further excavation must be carried out with care
options.D: The excavation has reached a depth where the sides must now be supported

questions.explanation: Reference: The coloured tape indicates that there are buried services below the route of the tape.

A.text: Contaminated land requires separate evidence and controls; yellow service tape is not a soil-contamination marker.

B.text: Electrical warning tape identifies a service route, not groundwater conditions or a need to dewater the excavation.

C.text: Reference: The coloured tape indicates that there are buried services below the route of the tape.

D.text: Support requirements depend on ground and excavation risk, not on the colour of buried service marker tape.

questions.prompt: When do special precautions need to be taken when working near overhead electric power lines?

options.A: Only if plant has to pass under the lines
options.B: Only if cranes etc. are being used
options.C: Only if someone could touch a line with their bare hands
options.D: Whenever work areas will be near or beneath the lines

questions.explanation: Reference: Actual contact with a power line is not necessary to result in an electric shock as a close approach may allow 'flashover' to occur. HSE publication GS6 gives advice on procedures to avoid such danger.

A.text: People, loads and equipment can approach a line even without passing directly underneath it.

B.text: Cranes are one concern, but ladders, scaffold tubes, tipping bodies and MEWPs can also reach overhead conductors.

C.text: Electricity can arc across an air gap, so bare-hand contact is not required for serious injury.

D.text: Reference: Actual contact with a power line is not necessary to result in an electric shock as a close approach may allow 'flashover' to occur. HSE publication GS6 gives advice on procedures to avoid such danger.

questions.prompt: What is the preferred nominal voltage for portable hand tools on construction sites?
questions.explanation: Reference: 110 volt reduced low voltage systems are strongly preferred for the supply to such equipment.

A.text: Portable 230 V tools create a greater shock risk and are not the preferred general construction-site arrangement.

B.text: Twelve volts may suit specialist very-high-risk conditions, but it is not the standard nominal site-tool supply.

C.text: Reference: 110 volt reduced low voltage systems are strongly preferred for the supply to such equipment.

D.text: Twenty-four volts can be used for particular equipment, but UK site power tools normally use 110 V centre-tapped-to-earth.

questions.prompt: Who should operate plant and equipment on site?

options.C: An employee holding a full driving license
options.D: Only people over 18 years of age

questions.explanation: Reference: Never operate plant or equipment unless you have been trained and are authorised to do so.

A.text: General experience does not demonstrate training on the particular machine or formal authority to use it.

B.text: Reference: Never operate plant or equipment unless you have been trained and are authorised to do so.

C.text: A road driving licence does not cover construction plant controls, stability, attachments or site-specific hazards.

D.text: Age alone cannot establish competence, and trained authorised younger workers may use some equipment under suitable controls.

questions.prompt: The electric drill you are about to use has a faulty on/off switch. What action should you take?

options.A: Find another machine and carry on working
options.B: Tape the switch on to keep it running and carry on working
options.C: Stop work and inform your supervisor

questions.explanation: Reference: It is essential that supervisors are aware of faulty or damaged equipment.

A.text: Using another drill may keep the task moving, but the defective tool remains unreported and available to others.

B.text: Taping a switch on removes control of the tool and can cause unexpected starting or inability to stop it.

C.text: Reference: It is essential that supervisors are aware of faulty or damaged equipment.

D.text: Untrained repair can expose live parts or defeat safety features; the fault requires competent attention.

questions.prompt: What precaution should you take before adjusting an electrical tool?

options.A: Wear the correct personal protective equipment
options.B: Check the lead is not twisted or knotted
options.D: Wear safety footwear with steel toecaps

questions.explanation: Reference: Do not adjust tools which could still be live or operate.

A.text: PPE may remain necessary, but it does not prevent the tool from starting while hands are at the adjustment point.

B.text: Lead condition matters for use, yet an untwisted lead does not isolate the tool from electrical power.

C.text: Reference: Do not adjust tools which could still be live or operate.

D.text: Toe protection cannot control unexpected rotation, cutting or electric shock during adjustment.

questions.prompt: When can you work from a ladder?

options.A: When not being used for access
options.B: For short periods and then only if it is safe to do so

questions.explanation: Reference: Ladders are primarily means of access, not workplaces. They can be worked from, but only if the use of other, more suitable, work equipment is not appropriate and the task is of low risk and of short duration.

A.text: A ladder used as access does not become a suitable workplace merely when nobody is climbing through it.

B.text: Reference: Ladders are primarily means of access, not workplaces. They can be worked from, but only if the use of other, more suitable, work equipment is not appropriate and the task is of low risk and of short duration.

C.text: Availability is not a risk assessment; a safer platform may be required even when a ladder is close at hand.

D.text: Sufficient length addresses reach only and says nothing about duration, task risk, stability or maintaining handhold.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum height of the top guard-rail of a scaffold above the edge from which someone is liable to fall?
questions.explanation: Reference: This is a requirement of the Work at Height Regulations 2005.

A.text: Two metres is not the minimum top-rail height and would be an unnecessarily high dimension for this requirement.

B.text: Nine hundred and ten millimetres reflects older figures and falls below the current 950 mm minimum for construction work.

C.text: Four hundred and seventy millimetres relates to limiting gaps and intermediate protection, not the top guard-rail height.

D.text: Reference: This is a requirement of the Work at Height Regulations 2005.

questions.prompt: If work at height cannot be avoided and collective fall-prevention equipment is not reasonably practicable, which listed approach is required before the work proceeds?

options.A: Use a properly selected work-restraint or fall-arrest system connected to a suitable anchor, with competent users and planned rescue arrangements
options.B: Work without fall protection at all times when no one else is about
options.C: Work without fall protection, provided you have a mate with you
options.D: Work without fall protection, provided the weather is not too windy

questions.explanation: Personal fall protection comes below collective prevention in the work-at-height hierarchy. A harness alone is not protection: the system, lanyard and anchorage must suit the task, users must be competent, and foreseeable rescue must be planned.

A.text: Personal fall protection comes below collective prevention in the work-at-height hierarchy. A harness alone is not protection: the system, lanyard and anchorage must suit the task, users must be competent, and foreseeable rescue must be planned.

B.text: Working alone increases the consequences of a fall and never makes absence of fall protection acceptable.

C.text: A companion cannot reliably arrest a fall or perform a suspended rescue without a designed system and plan.

D.text: Low wind removes only one factor; gravity, edges, slips and structural failure still create a fall risk.

questions.prompt: Half the deaths on construction sites are caused by which one of the following?
questions.explanation: Falls from height are the single biggest cause of fatal accidents in construction, accounting for around half of deaths. This is why work at height must be properly planned with guarding, secure access and fall protection rather than improvised access.

A.text: Plant misuse causes fatal incidents, but the cited construction data attributes the largest share to falls from height.

B.text: Trenches and confined spaces require strong controls, yet they account for a smaller share of deaths than falls.

C.text: Electrical danger can be fatal, but it is not the category responsible for roughly half of the cited deaths.

D.text: Falls from height are the single biggest cause of fatal accidents in construction, accounting for around half of deaths. This is why work at height must be properly planned with guarding, secure access and fall protection rather than improvised access.

questions.prompt: What is the ideal angle for a ladder against a wall and floor?

options.A: One metre up for every metre out from the wall
options.B: Two metres up for every metre out from the wall
options.C: Four metres up for every metre out from the wall
options.D: One metre up for every two metres out from the wall

questions.explanation: Reference: The correct angle for a ladder is 75 degrees, which an be judged using the angle indicator marked on the stiles of some ladders or using the 1 in 4 rule.

A.text: A one-to-one slope is about 45 degrees, far shallower and less stable than the recommended 75-degree angle.

B.text: A two-to-one slope is about 63 degrees, still too shallow compared with the one-in-four setup rule.

C.text: Reference: The correct angle for a ladder is 75 degrees, which an be judged using the angle indicator marked on the stiles of some ladders or using the 1 in 4 rule.

D.text: One metre up for two metres out is about 27 degrees, making the ladder dangerously close to horizontal.

questions.prompt: Once the casualty is away from the hot metal and there is no immediate life-threatening danger, what should you do first for the hand burn?

options.A: Warn other people about the piece of hot metal
options.B: Cover the burn with something dry
options.C: Cool the burn under cool running water for at least 20 minutes while keeping the casualty warm
options.D: Rub some cream or Vaseline into the burn

questions.explanation: Current NHS burns guidance is to stop the burning process and cool the affected area with cool running water for at least 20 minutes. Ice, very cold water, creams and grease can worsen injury or interfere with assessment.

A.text: Warning others is useful once urgent care is under way, but it does not limit continuing tissue damage in the casualty.

B.text: A dry covering comes after adequate cooling; covering first traps heat in the burned tissue.

C.text: Current NHS burns guidance is to stop the burning process and cool the affected area with cool running water for at least 20 minutes. Ice, very cold water, creams and grease can worsen injury or interfere with assessment.

D.text: Cream or petroleum products retain heat and complicate clinical assessment, so they should not be rubbed into a fresh burn.

questions.prompt: In an on-site emergency, which of the following must a first-aider NOT do?

options.C: Give medicines to patients without authorization

questions.explanation: Reference: First-aid is concerned with preserving life and limb, and first-aiders are not trained to dispense medical treatments.

A.text: An unconscious casualty requires assessment and appropriate care; unconsciousness is not a reason to avoid treatment.

B.text: Resuscitation is a core emergency skill and must not be withheld when a casualty is not breathing normally.

C.text: Reference: First-aid is concerned with preserving life and limb, and first-aiders are not trained to dispense medical treatments.

D.text: Controlling severe bleeding with appropriate first-aid measures is within the trained first-aider's role.

questions.prompt: What action should you take if you discover a fire?

options.A: Leave it because you will get the blame
options.C: Extinguish the fire without raising the alarm
options.D: Carry on working if it is safe to do so

questions.explanation: Reference: Raising the alarm will reduce the risk to others, particularly if the fire spreads.

A.text: Fear of blame cannot justify leaving others unaware of a fire that may spread rapidly.

B.text: Reference: Raising the alarm will reduce the risk to others, particularly if the fire spreads.

C.text: Attempting extinction without warning people can delay evacuation and leave the worker trapped if the fire grows.

D.text: Continuing work ignores an escalating emergency and prevents the site's fire procedure from starting.

questions.prompt: Which of the following animals can carry Weil's disease?
questions.explanation: Reference: Weil's disease is a serious and sometimes fatal infection that can be transmitted to humans by contact with infected rats. Another form of Leptospirosis infection can be transmitted from cattle to humans.

A.text: Sheep are associated with different occupational infections; they are not the expected reservoir in this question.

B.text: Pigs can carry other zoonoses, but rats and their urine are the classic construction-site source of Weil's disease.

C.text: Reference: Weil's disease is a serious and sometimes fatal infection that can be transmitted to humans by contact with infected rats. Another form of Leptospirosis infection can be transmitted from cattle to humans.

D.text: Snake exposure is unrelated to leptospiral infection from urine-contaminated water or wet ground.

questions.prompt: While working you discover material you think could be asbestos. What should you do?

options.B: Clear any dust and fragments, put them in a bin then carry on working
options.C: Dampen the material to prevent further dust being created, then carry on working
options.D: Stop working immediately and report your suspicions to your supervisor

questions.explanation: Reference: It is essential to stop work if asbestos is found or suspected, and await competent advice on what to do next.

A.text: A nurse may later advise on exposure, but the work area first needs to be stopped and controlled through supervision.

B.text: Sweeping and binning fragments can release fibres and creates unlicensed, uncontained asbestos waste.

C.text: Damping alone does not identify the material or authorise continued disturbance under an assessed method.

D.text: Reference: It is essential to stop work if asbestos is found or suspected, and await competent advice on what to do next.

questions.prompt: If you have been handling lead, how is it most likely to get into your blood stream?

options.A: By not reporting the matter to the HSE
options.B: By not using the correct safety footwear
options.C: By not washing your hands before eating

questions.explanation: Reference: The route into the body is ingestion, normally from lead contamination on the hands.

A.text: Failure to notify HSE does not itself put lead into the bloodstream; exposure occurs through physical routes into the body.

B.text: Safety footwear protects the feet but does not stop contaminated hands transferring lead to food or the mouth.

C.text: Reference: The route into the body is ingestion, normally from lead contamination on the hands.

D.text: Goggles protect the eyes; they do not control ingestion from eating with lead-contaminated hands.

questions.prompt: Which listed requirement must apply to a safety helmet supplied as PPE for work in Great Britain?

options.A: It is less than 1 year old
options.B: It must meet the applicable PPE product-safety requirements and bear a recognised conformity marking such as CE or UKCA
options.C: It is less than 2 years old
options.D: It is less than 5 years old

questions.explanation: A helmet's suitability is not established by a generic age limit. PPE placed on the Great Britain market must meet the applicable essential safety requirements and carry an accepted conformity marking; current law recognises both CE and UKCA routes, so CE-only wording was incomplete.

A.text: A one-year age limit is not a general conformity requirement and says nothing about the helmet's standard or condition.

B.text: A helmet's suitability is not established by a generic age limit. PPE placed on the Great Britain market must meet the applicable essential safety requirements and carry an accepted conformity marking; current law recognises both CE and UKCA routes, so CE-only wording was incomplete.

C.text: Two years is not a universal expiry period; service life depends on the maker's instructions, use and damage.

D.text: Five years is neither an automatic acceptance nor rejection rule and cannot replace conformity and pre-use checks.

questions.prompt: Why should a high visibility vest be worn when working on roads?

options.A: So road users and plant operators can see you
options.B: So that your mates can see you
options.C: Because you were told to do so
options.D: Because it will keep you warm

questions.explanation: Reference: Many workers are struck and injured, often seriously, by moving vehicles.

A.text: Reference: Many workers are struck and injured, often seriously, by moving vehicles.

B.text: Colleague recognition is secondary; the critical need is early detection by approaching drivers and mobile-plant operators.

C.text: Following an instruction is required, but it does not explain the road-traffic hazard that the garment controls.

D.text: A high-visibility vest is not thermal clothing and may provide little insulation in cold conditions.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following should you do if your personal protective equipment (PPE) is damaged?

options.C: Reduce the amount of time you use it
options.D: Report to your Supervisor without delay

questions.explanation: Reference: Employees are required to report any defective PPE to their employer (PPE at Work Regulations 1992, Regulation 7)

A.text: Continuing with damaged PPE leaves the identified hazard uncontrolled exactly when protection may be needed.

B.text: Waiting for a convenient replacement exposes the worker in the meantime; use should stop and the defect be reported.

C.text: Shorter exposure does not restore the equipment's protection or make an unknown failure mode predictable.

D.text: Reference: Employees are required to report any defective PPE to their employer (PPE at Work Regulations 1992, Regulation 7)

questions.prompt: Which of the following must your safety helmet comply with to meet with the requirements of the Personal Protective Equipment at Work Regulations?

options.A: It is a good visible colour
options.B: It has a label with your name on it
options.C: It can be adjusted to suit your head size
options.D: It is less than 1 year old

questions.explanation: Reference: An assessment of the suitability of head protection would include consideration of whether it can be adjusted to suit the individual who is to wear it, that it is compatible with the work to be done and that it is comfortable to wear.

A.text: Visibility may be useful for some tasks, but colour alone does not make a helmet fit and remain secure on its wearer.

B.text: A name label assists identification but contributes no impact protection, fit or compatibility with the user's head.

C.text: Reference: An assessment of the suitability of head protection would include consideration of whether it can be adjusted to suit the individual who is to wear it, that it is compatible with the work to be done and that it is comfortable to wear.

D.text: Being less than a year old cannot compensate for poor fit, damage or use contrary to the manufacturer's instructions.

questions.prompt: Under which of the following circumstances should an accident be recorded in the site's accident book?

options.A: When an accident causes damage to plant or equipment
options.B: When the injury is serious enough for first aid to be needed.
options.C: When an accident causes injury to an employee while at work
options.D: Only when a person is injured and will be off work for more than seven days

questions.explanation: Reference: An accident causing an injury to an employee at work should be recorded in the accident book (BI 510).

A.text: Plant damage without personal injury belongs in maintenance or incident records, not necessarily the statutory accident book.

B.text: The recording duty is not triggered only when first aid is needed; even a minor work injury should be recorded.

C.text: Reference: An accident causing an injury to an employee at work should be recorded in the accident book (BI 510).

D.text: Seven-day incapacity is a separate RIDDOR reporting threshold and is not the threshold for an accident-book entry.

questions.prompt: When judging "individual capability" for manual handling, you should assume:
questions.explanation: Reference: Assessing ability for manual handling must be done on an individual basis.

A.text: Treating all women as identical ignores the individual factors that a manual-handling assessment must consider.

B.text: Reference: Assessing ability for manual handling must be done on an individual basis.

C.text: Sex does not make all men equally capable; health, size, training, fatigue and the task all affect capacity.

D.text: Age and sex stereotypes are not an assessment of the actual worker's physical capability for the task.

questions.prompt: Why should a serious accident be reported to the enforcing authority?

options.A: So that the site manager can see who is to blame
options.B: So that the company will be held responsible
options.C: It helps the site find out what caused it

questions.explanation: Reference: Serious accidents (specified injuries or those resulting in an absence of over 7 days) must be reported to the enforcing authority under the Reporting of Injuries, Diseases and Dangerous Occurrences Regulations (RIDDOR).

A.text: The purpose is not to identify someone to blame, but to notify the legally specified event to the regulator.

B.text: A report does not automatically assign company liability; it supplies the facts required by the reporting regime.

C.text: Finding the cause is useful, but reporting to the enforcing authority is triggered by law rather than that local benefit.

D.text: Reference: Serious accidents (specified injuries or those resulting in an absence of over 7 days) must be reported to the enforcing authority under the Reporting of Injuries, Diseases and Dangerous Occurrences Regulations (RIDDOR).

questions.prompt: Under RIDDOR, which one of the following must be reported to the enforcing authority?

options.A: Fracture other than to fingers, thumbs or toes
options.B: All 'near misses' even if no one is hurt
options.D: Accidents where the injured person wishes to make a claim

questions.explanation: Reference: This is one of a number of reportable 'specified injuries' and must be reported to the enforcing authority under the Reporting of Injuries, Diseases and Dangerous Occurrences Regulations (RIDDOR).

A.text: Reference: This is one of a number of reportable 'specified injuries' and must be reported to the enforcing authority under the Reporting of Injuries, Diseases and Dangerous Occurrences Regulations (RIDDOR).

B.text: Near misses are valuable internally, but only listed dangerous occurrences require notification when nobody is hurt.

C.text: Minor injuries belong in workplace records but are not all reportable to the enforcing authority.

D.text: A possible civil claim does not determine RIDDOR status; the event and injury category do.

questions.prompt: What is the most common type of injury resulting from lifting loads from the floor?
questions.explanation: Lifting from floor level forces you to bend and put strain on the spine, so the back is by far the most commonly injured area. Poor technique and twisting under load make muscle and disc damage very likely.

A.text: Knee grazes may occur, but floor-level lifting more commonly overloads the lower back through poor posture and leverage.

B.text: Vibration white finger results from prolonged vibration exposure, not from a single floor-lifting movement.

C.text: A head injury is not the characteristic manual-handling outcome unless a separate falling-object event occurs.

D.text: Lifting from floor level forces you to bend and put strain on the spine, so the back is by far the most commonly injured area. Poor technique and twisting under load make muscle and disc damage very likely.

questions.prompt: In HSE's simple lifting-and-lowering risk filter, what guideline figure applies for a man handling an easily grasped load close to the body at about knuckle height?

options.A: 25 kg, as a risk-filter value rather than a guaranteed safe limit

questions.explanation: The HSE chart uses 25 kg in this limited posture and handling zone to screen for low-risk tasks. It is not a safe limit and does not remove the need to consider frequency, twisting, travel, grip, individual capability and other adverse factors.

A.text: The HSE chart uses 25 kg in this limited posture and handling zone to screen for low-risk tasks. It is not a safe limit and does not remove the need to consider frequency, twisting, travel, grip, individual capability and other adverse factors.

B.text: Twenty kilograms is below the chart's 25 kg figure for this precise zone and therefore is not the published filter value.

C.text: Forty kilograms substantially exceeds the filter value and would require a more detailed assessment.

D.text: Fifty kilograms is double the chart figure and must never be treated as a simple low-risk screening weight.

questions.prompt: If moving a load may cause injury, what should you do before proceeding?

options.A: Stop and tell the supervisor or responsible person so the operation can be avoided where possible or properly assessed and controlled
options.D: Getting someone to assist you over the distance

questions.explanation: The correct response is not simply to carry, drag or recruit someone informally. Hazardous handling should first be avoided where reasonably practicable; otherwise the task needs assessment and controls such as redesign, an aid or a planned team lift.

A.text: The correct response is not simply to carry, drag or recruit someone informally. Hazardous handling should first be avoided where reasonably practicable; otherwise the task needs assessment and controls such as redesign, an aid or a planned team lift.

B.text: Proceeding despite a known injury risk bypasses both the duty to avoid the handling and the need for assessment.

C.text: Dragging can add high force, poor posture and damage and is not automatically safer than carrying.

D.text: Informally adding a helper can create coordination hazards; a team lift must follow an assessed plan where appropriate.

questions.prompt: The Health and Safety (Safety Signs and Signals) Regulations require the colour coding of safety signs. What colours are used on a sign indicating a mandatory activity, for example "Safety helmets must be worn"?
questions.explanation: Mandatory signs that tell you what you must do, like wearing a helmet, are a blue circle with a white symbol. Red means prohibition or fire, yellow with black warns of a hazard, and green indicates safe conditions or escape routes.

A.text: Mandatory signs that tell you what you must do, like wearing a helmet, are a blue circle with a white symbol. Red means prohibition or fire, yellow with black warns of a hazard, and green indicates safe conditions or escape routes.

B.text: Green and white marks safe conditions and emergency facilities, not an instruction that must be followed.

C.text: Red, black and white prohibits an activity; it is not used for a positive helmet-wearing command.

D.text: Yellow and black warns of a hazard but does not prescribe the action that the viewer must take.

questions.prompt: Why should regular inspections of the workplace take place?

options.A: To check that all employees are present
options.B: To check that everyone is doing their job
options.C: To check whether the working environment is safe
options.D: To prepare for a visit from an HSE Inspector

questions.explanation: Reference: The Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations require that routine inspections of workplaces are carried out to ensure that preventative and protective measures are in place and effective.

A.text: Attendance is an administrative check and gives no assurance that access, guarding or housekeeping remains safe.

B.text: Performance supervision may be needed, but a workplace inspection looks for hazards and control failures, not productivity.

C.text: Reference: The Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations require that routine inspections of workplaces are carried out to ensure that preventative and protective measures are in place and effective.

D.text: Inspections should find and correct risks routinely, rather than being cosmetic preparation for a regulator's visit.

questions.prompt: For relevant Health and Safety at Work etc. Act offences tried on indictment, which listed maximum penalties can a Crown Court impose on an individual?

options.B: An unlimited fine and up to two years' imprisonment

questions.explanation: For relevant offences tried on indictment, the available maximum is an unlimited fine and, for an individual, imprisonment up to two years, or both. The original term 'Higher Court' was imprecise and not every offence or defendant attracts identical sentencing powers.

A.text: This limited fine and six-month term understates the sentencing powers available for relevant offences tried on indictment.

B.text: For relevant offences tried on indictment, the available maximum is an unlimited fine and, for an individual, imprisonment up to two years, or both. The original term 'Higher Court' was imprecise and not every offence or defendant attracts identical sentencing powers.

C.text: Three years exceeds the stated maximum imprisonment, while the monetary figure is not the unlimited Crown Court fine.

D.text: Although two years is the relevant imprisonment maximum, the Crown Court fine is not capped at £20,000.

questions.prompt: Regulations that govern health and safety on construction sites:

options.A: Do not apply during 'out of hours' working

questions.explanation: Reference: The requirements of health and safety law are mandatory, and failure to follow them can lead to prosecutions.

A.text: Legal duties continue outside ordinary hours; the time of day does not suspend the Regulations.

B.text: Reference: The requirements of health and safety law are mandatory, and failure to follow them can lead to prosecutions.

C.text: Small employers and small projects remain subject to construction health and safety law.

D.text: Health and safety duties apply according to work and risk, not according to whether a worker is inexperienced.

questions.prompt: What is a HAZARD?

options.B: The likelihood of something going wrong
options.C: Something with the potential to cause harm
options.D: Where an accident is likely to happen

questions.explanation: Reference: Examples of hazards include: a drum of acid, breeze blocks on an elevated plank; cables running across a floor.

A.text: The phrase predicts an event but does not identify the thing or condition that has potential to cause harm.

B.text: Likelihood is part of risk; a hazard exists because it can cause harm regardless of how likely exposure is.

C.text: Reference: Examples of hazards include: a drum of acid, breeze blocks on an elevated plank; cables running across a floor.

D.text: A place can contain hazards, but location alone is not the definition of the harmful agent or condition.

questions.prompt: What does a prohibition notice that takes immediate effect require?

options.A: When you finish the work you must not start again
options.B: The activity specified in the notice must stop immediately and cannot resume until the serious-risk matters have been remedied
options.C: Work may continue until the end of the day
options.D: Work is to stop for that day only

questions.explanation: An immediate prohibition notice stops the specified activity at once because an imminent risk of serious personal injury exists. The correction distinguishes this from a deferred prohibition notice, which takes effect at the time stated on it.

A.text: An immediate notice does not allow the current work to be finished before the statutory stop takes effect.

B.text: An immediate prohibition notice stops the specified activity at once because an imminent risk of serious personal injury exists. The correction distinguishes this from a deferred prohibition notice, which takes effect at the time stated on it.

C.text: Work cannot continue until the end of the day when the notice identifies an imminent risk requiring immediate cessation.

D.text: The activity remains prohibited beyond that day until the matters giving rise to the serious risk are remedied.

questions.prompt: The Electricity at Work Regulations require that:

options.A: A training course is necessary before anyone can work with electricity
options.B: Anyone supervised can work with electricity
options.C: Only electricians can work with electricity
options.D: People must have adequate knowledge or experience, or be under an appropriate degree of supervision, to prevent danger and injury

questions.explanation: Regulation 16 permits work where technical knowledge or experience is necessary only when the person has that competence or is under an appropriate degree of supervision. It does not require every worker to already possess the same unsupervised competence.

A.text: A course may contribute to competence, but the Regulation focuses on effective knowledge, experience or supervision.

B.text: Supervision must be appropriate to prevent danger; the mere presence of any supervisor is not enough.

C.text: Job title is not the legal test, and non-electricians may do limited work when competence or supervision is adequate.

D.text: Regulation 16 permits work where technical knowledge or experience is necessary only when the person has that competence or is under an appropriate degree of supervision. It does not require every worker to already possess the same unsupervised competence.

questions.prompt: The Electricity at Work Regulations apply to:
questions.explanation: The EAW Regulations cover the safe use of electricity in work activities, irrespective of voltage.

A.text: The EAW Regulations cover the safe use of electricity in work activities, irrespective of voltage.

B.text: Extra-low voltage can still create electrical danger in some environments and is not excluded as a class.

C.text: High-voltage systems are covered, but the Regulations are not restricted to them.

D.text: Low-voltage systems are covered, but the statutory scope also reaches other voltage ranges where electrical danger arises.

questions.prompt: Which of the following should be used to prove a circuit or equipment is dead after isolation?

options.A: A lamp holder with a length of flex attached
options.C: A proprietary test lamp or two-pole voltage detector

questions.explanation: Accident history has shown that using incorrectly set multimeters or makeshift devices for voltage detection has often caused accidents. The use of non-contact voltage indicators (voltage sticks) is also not advised as the sole means of proving dead.

A.text: A makeshift lamp and flex lacks protected probe tips, appropriate ratings and a controlled indication of voltage.

B.text: A multimeter can be mis-set or give a misleading reading and is not the preferred device for proving dead.

C.text: Accident history has shown that using incorrectly set multimeters or makeshift devices for voltage detection has often caused accidents. The use of non-contact voltage indicators (voltage sticks) is also not advised as the sole means of proving dead.

D.text: A non-contact voltage stick can miss screened or poorly coupled conductors and cannot prove absence of voltage.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a suitable means of isolating a circuit?

options.A: Fitting a padlocked circuit breaker lockout
options.C: Removing a fuse and securing the distribution board against access
options.D: Putting insulating tape over the circuit breaker instead of applying a secure lock-off device

questions.explanation: Tape does not secure an isolating device against inadvertent or unauthorised operation. HSE construction guidance explicitly contrasts tape over a circuit-breaker with a proper lock-off device, personal lock and safety notice.
