questions.prompt: Which of the following animals can carry Weil's disease?
questions.explanation: Weil's disease is a serious and sometimes fatal infection that can be transmitted to humans by contact with infected rats. Another form of Leptospirosis infection can be transmitted from cattle to humans.

questions.prompt: While working you discover material you think could be asbestos. What should you do?

options.A: Clear any dust and fragments, put them in a bin then carry on working
options.B: Dampen the material to prevent further dust being created, then carry on working
options.D: Stop working immediately and report your suspicions to your supervisor

questions.explanation: It is essential to stop work if asbestos is found or suspected, and await competent advice on what to do next.

D.text: It is essential to stop work if asbestos is found or suspected, and await competent advice on what to do next.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is TRUE when an employer issues personal protective equipment (PPE)?

options.A: The employer can charge you for the full cost of it

questions.prompt: Who has a duty to provide PPE (Personal Protective Equipment) for use by an employee?
questions.explanation: This is a requirement of the PPE at Work Regulations 1992(Regulation 4).

B.text: Employees must wear and look after issued equipment, but they are not responsible for funding statutory PPE.

D.text: The principal contractor coordinates the construction phase, while the worker's own employer still supplies required PPE.

questions.prompt: In normal use, what item of PPE is NOT essential for the operator of a cartridge-operated tool, such as a nail gun?

questions.prompt: Which of the following must your safety helmet comply with to meet with the requirements of the Personal Protective Equipment at Work Regulations?

options.A: It can be adjusted to suit your head size
options.B: It has a label with your name on it

questions.explanation: An assessment of the suitability of head protection would include consideration of whether it can be adjusted to suit the individual who is to wear it, that it is compatible with the work to be done and that it is comfortable to wear.

A.text: An assessment of the suitability of head protection would include consideration of whether it can be adjusted to suit the individual who is to wear it, that it is compatible with the work to be done and that it is comfortable to wear.

questions.prompt: Could making an entry in the accident book help you if you later make a claim for compensation?

options.B: Only if it is a serious injury

D.text: A timely accident-book entry creates a dated, factual record of what happened and any injury, which supports a later compensation claim. Without that documented evidence it becomes far harder to prove the incident occurred at work and how it arose.

questions.prompt: At work who would you report a dangerous occurrence to?
questions.explanation: Under RIDDOR, an employer has a legal duty to report certain work-related accidents, but to do this they will need to know that an accident has occurred.

questions.prompt: When an article has to be moved for a long distance, you should:

options.C: Get someone else to do it for you

questions.explanation: Using a barrow or trolley for a long-distance move lets the wheels carry the weight instead of your spine, reducing the risk of musculoskeletal injury. Mechanical aids are the preferred control under manual handling principles whenever a load must travel any real distance.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following has the power to examine an accident record?
questions.explanation: HSE inspectors hold statutory powers to inspect and take copies of accident records and other safety documents when investigating or checking compliance. This access lets them verify that incidents are being reported and managed as the law requires.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is advisable when lifting a load manually?

options.A: Use a stable stance, keep the load close and use slight bending of the back, hips and knees while avoiding twist and further back flexion
options.B: Bend the knees, keep the back straight, use power of back
options.C: Keep legs and back straight, use power of legs
options.D: Keep legs straight, bend back, use power of legs

questions.explanation: Current HSE technique favours a stable posture and slight coordinated bending, not a rigidly straight back or a deep squat. Keep the heaviest side close, secure the load, move smoothly and turn with the feet instead of twisting.

A.text: Current HSE technique favours a stable posture and slight coordinated bending, not a rigidly straight back or a deep squat. Keep the heaviest side close, secure the load, move smoothly and turn with the feet instead of twisting.

B.text: The back is not the power source for the lift, and forcing it rigidly straight is not current HSE technique.

C.text: Keeping both legs and back straight forces reaching and spinal bending and prevents a stable, close hold.

questions.prompt: Which listed answer best describes using good manual-handling technique after hazardous handling has first been avoided or reduced as far as reasonably practicable?

options.A: Getting a friend to help you with the load
options.B: Handling the load in a controlled and efficient way using a stable posture, secure hold, close load position and smooth movement

options.D: Using a forklift truck or pallet truck

questions.explanation: 'Kinetic lifting' is dated shorthand and must not imply that technique makes an otherwise hazardous lift safe. Good handling technique supplements task redesign and lifting aids; it uses balance, a close load, controlled movement and avoids twisting or sudden force.

questions.prompt: What is the main colour on a safety sign stating that you must NOT do something?

questions.prompt: What should you do if your supervisor asks you to move something that you find is too heavy to lift?

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: All employees must take reasonable care, not only to protect themselves but also their colleagues

options.C: Only the client is responsible for safety on site

questions.prompt: What is a HAZARD?

options.B: Something with the potential to cause harm

questions.prompt: What does a prohibition notice that takes immediate effect require?

questions.prompt: What is an "Improvement Notice"?

questions.prompt: What do the letters HSE stand for?

questions.prompt: What are fire-stops designed to do?

questions.prompt: If you have unused material left, what should you do before you consider putting non-hazardous waste items into a skip?

questions.prompt: The Electricity at Work Regulations apply to:

questions.prompt: Which of the following should be disposed of as hazardous/special waste?

questions.prompt: A residual current device is designed to operate in the event of one of the following:

questions.prompt: Which listed value is the conventional upper boundary of extra-low voltage for AC and the level above which HSE warns that contact can cause shock injury?

questions.prompt: Your job involves you working near to hanging electrical cables which have bare ends. What should you do?

questions.prompt: A mobile plant operator can let you ride in the machine:

options.D: If you have a long way to go

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a requirement of low voltage safe isolation practice?

questions.prompt: Where mains voltage is used to supply portable equipment on a construction site, what additional protection is required?

questions.prompt: After plans and a suitable locating device have identified an underground power cable, which listed approach should be used for trial holes and final exposure?

questions.prompt: When working alone:

questions.prompt: Which listed approach is safest when portable lighting is needed in a confined or damp location?

questions.prompt: The power hand tool you are about to use has burn marks visible on the cable. What should you do?

questions.explanation: It is essential that supervisors are aware of faulty or damaged equipment.

questions.prompt: Your supervisor asks you to use a powered hand-tool which has a rotating blade. You notice that the guard is missing from the blade. What do you do?

questions.prompt: An electric drill is to be used. Before use, who should carry out a check on the tool?

questions.prompt: What is the minimum height of the top guard-rail of a scaffold above the edge from which someone is liable to fall?

questions.prompt: After checking that approaching the casualty will not expose you or them to immediate danger, what should you do first on finding an injured person on site?

questions.prompt: What should you do if you hear the fire alarm?

questions.prompt: Can you tell by the smell of a product whether it is likely to cause harm?

questions.prompt: Why is personal hygiene so important?

questions.prompt: Which listed statement best describes the role of personal protective equipment at work?

options.B: Personal protective equipment (PPE) need only be provided if it is not too expensive

questions.prompt: When should a safety helmet be worn on site?

questions.prompt: Can you opt out of wearing personal protective equipment (PPE)?

questions.prompt: Which of the following can you learn from an accident?

questions.prompt: Which of the following should be recorded in the accident book following an accident?

options.A: The date and time the accident occurred

questions.explanation: The information to be entered in an accident book (BI510) includes when and where the accident happened, the name, address and occupation of the person who had the accident and details of how the accident happened and the injuries suffered. The weather conditions would only be included if they contributed to the accident

A.text: The information to be entered in an accident book (BI510) includes when and where the accident happened, the name, address and occupation of the person who had the accident and details of how the accident happened and the injuries suffered. The weather conditions would only be included if they contributed to the accident

B.text: Weather is relevant only when it contributed; the date and time are core facts for every accident record.

C.text: Date of birth is not required in the standard accident particulars, unlike the time and date of the event.

D.text: A National Insurance number does not establish the circumstances of the workplace incident and is not a standard BI510 field.

questions.prompt: When moving a load fitted with wheels which of the following is generally true?

options.A: It is safer to pick it up and carry it
options.C: Pushing and pulling are equally risky

questions.explanation: The operator should try to push rather than pull when moving a load, provided they can see over it and control steering and stopping.

A.text: Lifting discards the mechanical advantage of the wheels and adds unnecessary support of the full weight.

B.text: Pulling can twist the body and leaves less control if the load rolls toward the handler; pushing is generally preferred when visibility is good.

C.text: The postures and control differ: pushing normally permits a more stable body position than pulling.

D.text: The operator should try to push rather than pull when moving a load, provided they can see over it and control steering and stopping.

questions.prompt: What is the most common type of injury resulting from lifting loads from the floor?
questions.explanation: Lifting from floor level forces the body to bend and take strain through the spine, so back injuries are by far the most common outcome of poor manual handling. Correct technique and assessing the load first are key to avoiding them.

A.text: Lifting from floor level forces the body to bend and take strain through the spine, so back injuries are by far the most common outcome of poor manual handling. Correct technique and assessing the load first are key to avoiding them.

B.text: Knee grazes may occur, but floor-level lifting more commonly overloads the lower back through poor posture and leverage.

C.text: A head injury is not the characteristic manual-handling outcome unless a separate falling-object event occurs.

D.text: Vibration white finger results from prolonged vibration exposure, not from a single floor-lifting movement.

questions.prompt: What should be the first consideration when you are about to lift a load on your own?

options.A: Assess whether it is safe to lift it on your own
options.B: Ensure you lift with a bent back

questions.explanation: Employees should assess whether there is a risk of injury before lifting. If they are not sure they should seek advice from their supervisor.

A.text: Employees should assess whether there is a risk of injury before lifting. If they are not sure they should seek advice from their supervisor.

B.text: Starting with a bent back increases leverage on the spine and ignores whether the task should be attempted at all.

C.text: PPE may control a specific residual hazard, but it cannot make an excessive weight or unstable load safe to lift alone.

D.text: Gloves can improve grip yet do not answer whether the weight, shape, route and worker capability require help.

questions.prompt: What do the blue and white health and safety signs tell you?

options.D: Where the nearest fire exit is

questions.explanation: Blue and white signs are mandatory signs telling you actions you must take, such as wearing eye protection or a hard hat. The blue circle distinguishes them from red prohibition signs, yellow warnings and green safe-condition signs.

A.text: Hazard warnings use yellow and black, not the blue circular mandatory-sign format.

B.text: Blue and white signs are mandatory signs telling you actions you must take, such as wearing eye protection or a hard hat. The blue circle distinguishes them from red prohibition signs, yellow warnings and green safe-condition signs.

C.text: Prohibitions use red edging and a diagonal bar to show an action that must not be taken.

D.text: Safe-condition signs such as emergency exits use green and white rather than blue and white.

questions.prompt: What colours are fire exit signs?
questions.explanation: The colours are prescribed in the Health and Safety (Safety Signs and Signals) Regulations.

A.text: Blue and white indicates a mandatory action, not a safe escape route.

B.text: The colours are prescribed in the Health and Safety (Safety Signs and Signals) Regulations.

C.text: Red and white identifies fire-fighting equipment or prohibition features, not the direction of escape.

D.text: Red and yellow does not represent the standard safe-condition colour scheme for an emergency exit.

questions.prompt: Why should regular inspections of the workplace take place?

options.A: To check that all employees are present
options.B: To check that everyone is doing their job
options.C: To check whether the working environment is safe
options.D: To prepare for a visit from an HSE Inspector

questions.explanation: The Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations require that routine inspections of workplaces are carried out to ensure that preventative and protective measures are in place and effective.

A.text: Attendance is an administrative check and gives no assurance that access, guarding or housekeeping remains safe.

B.text: Performance supervision may be needed, but a workplace inspection looks for hazards and control failures, not productivity.

C.text: The Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations require that routine inspections of workplaces are carried out to ensure that preventative and protective measures are in place and effective.

D.text: Inspections should find and correct risks routinely, rather than being cosmetic preparation for a regulator's visit.

questions.prompt: Who would you expect to carry out a risk assessment on your working site?
questions.explanation: Risk assessments must be carried out by a competent person who has the training, knowledge and experience to recognise the hazards and judge the controls needed. The legal duty to assess risks rests with the employer through such competent individuals.

A.text: Risk assessments must be carried out by a competent person who has the training, knowledge and experience to recognise the hazards and judge the controls needed. The legal duty to assess risks rests with the employer through such competent individuals.

B.text: An inspector checks whether the duty holder has assessed risk; the inspector does not write the site's assessment for it.

C.text: The former CDM co-ordinator role no longer exists under CDM 2015 and never replaced the employer's competent assessment process.

D.text: A designer assesses design risks, but does not automatically understand the contractor's people, tools and live site conditions.

questions.prompt: In what circumstances can an HSE Improvement Notice be issued?

options.B: If there is a breach of legal requirements
options.C: Only between Monday and Friday on site

questions.explanation: Improvement notices require action to achieve standards which meet health and safety law.

A.text: An appointed inspector serves an improvement notice under statutory powers without first obtaining a police warrant.

B.text: Improvement notices require action to achieve standards which meet health and safety law.

C.text: Enforcement powers are not restricted to weekdays; the issue is the legal breach, not the day of inspection.

D.text: Prosecution is a separate enforcement route and is not the office through which an improvement notice is issued.

questions.prompt: Companies employing five or more people must have a written Health and Safety Policy because:

options.B: The principal contractor gives them work on site
options.C: The Social Security Act requires it

questions.explanation: The Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 requires employers with five or more staff to set out their safety arrangements in a written policy. This ensures responsibilities and procedures are documented and made known to everyone affected.

A.text: The Health and Safety at Work etc. Act 1974 requires employers with five or more staff to set out their safety arrangements in a written policy. This ensures responsibilities and procedures are documented and made known to everyone affected.

B.text: A principal contractor may require site documents, but the employer's written-policy duty exists independently of winning that work.

C.text: Social-security law deals with benefits and records, not the employer threshold for a written safety policy.

D.text: Trade unions can press for strong arrangements, yet the written-policy requirement comes from statute rather than union rules.

questions.prompt: If you discover a hole or gap in a fire rated wall or floor that has not been fire-stopped, what should you do?

options.A: Cover the hole or gap with insulating tape
options.B: Ignore it unless it is causing a draught
options.C: Report it to your supervisor without delay
options.D: Use decorators' sealant to fill the gap

questions.explanation: Supervisors need to be made aware of any observed inadequacies in fire-stopping - which can undermine fire precautions catastrophically during the construction of buildings and on their completion. Only a limited range of products are suitable and they must be correctly applied to provide the required degree of fire-stopping.

A.text: Insulating tape has no tested fire-resistance rating and cannot reinstate a breached fire compartment.

B.text: A draught is irrelevant: any unsealed penetration can let smoke and flame bypass the fire-rated barrier.

C.text: Supervisors need to be made aware of any observed inadequacies in fire-stopping - which can undermine fire precautions catastrophically during the construction of buildings and on their completion. Only a limited range of products are suitable and they must be correctly applied to provide the required degree of fire-stopping.

D.text: Ordinary decorators' sealant is not a certified fire-stopping system matched to the wall or floor construction.

questions.prompt: Who needs to understand relevant environmental risks on a construction site?

options.B: Only the environmental clerk of works

questions.explanation: The actions of everyone on site determine how well the risks to the environment (such as water pollution, or creating a local nuisance) are controlled.

A.text: The actions of everyone on site determine how well the risks to the environment (such as water pollution, or creating a local nuisance) are controlled.

B.text: A specialist can coordinate environmental controls but cannot prevent pollution caused by uninformed workers across the site.

C.text: The principal contractor manages overall arrangements, while each person must follow controls relevant to their own activity.

D.text: Employees and other contractors can also spill, waste or release pollutants, so understanding cannot be limited to subcontractors.

questions.prompt: Which of the following should you do on site in the interest of sustainability?

options.B: Comply with site instructions on handling waste materials
options.C: Pour waste liquids down a drain off-site
options.D: Run plant and equipment when they are not needed

questions.explanation: Your actions will help your company, and others working on site, to achieve more sustainable work practices, such as waste recovery.

A.text: Burying waste evades authorised disposal and risks long-term contamination of land and groundwater.

B.text: Your actions will help your company, and others working on site, to achieve more sustainable work practices, such as waste recovery.

C.text: Moving off site does not make drain disposal lawful; liquids still need classification and an authorised waste route.

D.text: Unneeded running wastes fuel, creates emissions and adds noise and maintenance without productive work.

questions.prompt: Do individuals have any responsibility for minimising the amount of waste created on site?

options.A: No, it's the responsibility of the client
options.B: Only during site clean-up, at the end of the project
options.C: Only if asbestos removal is being carried out
options.D: Yes, everyone on site has this responsibility

questions.explanation: Your actions will help your company, and others on site, to procure sensibly and to organise the job so that materials and substances are not wasted. Waste reduction is the best option when trying to manage site waste.

A.text: The client influences procurement, but every worker can prevent damage, use only what is needed and sort remaining waste.

B.text: Waste is best prevented throughout delivery and installation; end-of-project clean-up is too late to recover wasted material.

C.text: Waste minimisation applies to ordinary packaging, off-cuts and surplus as well as specially controlled asbestos waste.

D.text: Your actions will help your company, and others on site, to procure sensibly and to organise the job so that materials and substances are not wasted. Waste reduction is the best option when trying to manage site waste.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a suitable means of isolating a circuit?

options.A: Fitting a padlocked circuit breaker lockout
options.C: Removing a fuse and securing the distribution board against access
options.D: Putting insulating tape over the circuit breaker instead of applying a secure lock-off device

questions.explanation: Tape does not secure an isolating device against inadvertent or unauthorised operation. HSE construction guidance explicitly contrasts tape over a circuit-breaker with a proper lock-off device, personal lock and safety notice.

A.text: A purpose-made circuit-breaker lockout and padlock secure the device against inadvertent operation.

B.text: Padlocking a suitable isolating switch provides the positive security that a safe isolation needs.

C.text: Removing the fuse and securing access can disconnect the circuit and prevent unauthorised replacement under the procedure.

D.text: Tape does not secure an isolating device against inadvertent or unauthorised operation. HSE construction guidance explicitly contrasts tape over a circuit-breaker with a proper lock-off device, personal lock and safety notice.

questions.prompt: The use of a multi-lock hasp with the appropriate number of padlocks is a recommended method of safe isolation where:

options.A: Individual circuit breaker locking off devices are not available
options.B: Individual circuit breakers are not identified at the distribution board
options.C: More than one person will be working on circuits supplied from the same distribution board
options.D: You know the health and safety inspector is in the area

questions.explanation: A multi-lock hasp can be used to prevent operation of the isolator until such time that all persons working on the electrical installation have completed their work and removed their padlocks from the hasp.

A.text: The need for a hasp comes from multiple personal locks, not from the absence of a device for one circuit-breaker.

B.text: Unidentified circuits must be traced and labelled; a multi-lock hasp cannot correct uncertainty about the isolation point.

C.text: A multi-lock hasp can be used to prevent operation of the isolator until such time that all persons working on the electrical installation have completed their work and removed their padlocks from the hasp.

D.text: Isolation arrangements are based on people exposed to reconnection risk, not on whether an inspector is nearby.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is true with regard to the dangers of electricity?

options.A: Electricity is dangerous at any time because you cannot tell by looking at a cable whether or not it is live
options.B: Electricity is only dangerous if you are not wearing wellington boots
options.C: Electricity is only dangerous in wet weather
options.D: Electricity is perfectly safe so long as you wear cotton gloves

questions.explanation: The features which make electricity so dangerous are that you cannot see, hear or smell it. It can give you a very unpleasant surprise. Always assume that cables are live.

A.text: The features which make electricity so dangerous are that you cannot see, hear or smell it. It can give you a very unpleasant surprise. Always assume that cables are live.

B.text: Wellington boots are not a universal electrical safeguard and may be wet, damaged or unsuitable for the voltage.

C.text: Dry weather does not prove a conductor dead or remove the possibility of a fatal current path.

D.text: Cotton gloves have no electrical insulating rating and do not make contact with energised parts safe.

questions.prompt: What is the most serious effect that electric shock can have if you come into contact with a live part?

options.A: The electric current can cause a slight tingling in the fingers
options.B: The electric current can cause burn marks on the fingers
options.C: The electric current can cause the finger muscles to twitch
options.D: The electric current can cause the heart to stop, resulting in death

questions.explanation: Contact with live electrical parts can be fatal. If you do not know otherwise, always assume that electrical parts are live.

A.text: Tingling is an early shock effect, but it is less severe than a current path that stops the heart.

B.text: Burns can be serious and deep, yet cardiac arrest presents the more immediate fatal consequence listed.

C.text: Muscle twitching shows physiological stimulation, but it is not the most severe outcome among these choices.

D.text: Contact with live electrical parts can be fatal. If you do not know otherwise, always assume that electrical parts are live.

questions.prompt: An electrical Permit to Work is primarily a statement that:

options.A: Certain instructions need to be followed
options.B: Someone else has taken responsibility for the work
options.C: The circuit or equipment has been isolated and is safe to work on
options.D: The circuit or equipment is live

questions.explanation: Permits to work describe the procedures that prevent a major hazard, such as electricity or moving machinery, from causing harm, usually by isolation to effectively ensure (in the case of electricity) 'dead' working with no chance of it going 'live'.

A.text: A permit contains instructions, but its central assurance is the defined equipment state and boundary released for work.

B.text: Issuing a permit coordinates responsibilities; it does not transfer all responsibility away from the people doing the work.

C.text: Permits to work describe the procedures that prevent a major hazard, such as electricity or moving machinery, from causing harm, usually by isolation to effectively ensure (in the case of electricity) 'dead' working with no chance of it going 'live'.

D.text: A permit-to-work for dead work is not authority to treat the circuit as live or to bypass isolation.

questions.prompt: To prove a circuit or equipment is dead after isolation what is the FIRST activity in the sequence of events?

options.C: Check that the voltage detector is working on a proving device, known live source or in- built test feature
options.D: Make sure equipment is not working

questions.explanation: This will prove that that the voltage detector (such as a two-pole voltage detector or proprietary test lamp) is working, i.e. indicating voltage.

A.text: Testing line to earth is part of proving dead, but the detector must first be proved functional.

B.text: A line-neutral test can falsely reassure if the detector has failed; pre-use proving must precede circuit measurements.

C.text: This will prove that that the voltage detector (such as a two-pole voltage detector or proprietary test lamp) is working, i.e. indicating voltage.

D.text: Equipment not operating may result from a control fault and does not prove every conductor is dead.

questions.prompt: Where mains voltage is used to supply portable equipment on a construction site, what additional protection is required?
questions.explanation: Reduced low voltage systems (e.g. 110 volt centre point earthed) are strongly preferred in such circumstances. Where only mains voltage (230 V) equipment is available, however, a 30 mA RCD will give additional protection against fatal electric shock.

A.text: A cable locator prevents excavation strikes and provides no automatic disconnection for a shock from portable equipment.

B.text: Reduced low voltage systems (e.g. 110 volt centre point earthed) are strongly preferred in such circumstances. Where only mains voltage (230 V) equipment is available, however, a 30 mA RCD will give additional protection against fatal electric shock.

C.text: A generator is a source, not additional personal shock protection for a 230 V portable appliance.

D.text: A step-down transformer would change the equipment voltage and cannot supply a tool designed solely for 230 V at its rated operation.

questions.prompt: What must be considered first when planning to carry out work in a confined space?

options.A: Can the work be done from the outside
options.C: Has the job been priced properly
options.D: Have the correct tools been arranged

questions.explanation: Working outside will remove the risks of working in the confined space.

A.text: Working outside will remove the risks of working in the confined space.

B.text: Staffing is considered only after establishing that entry is unavoidable and assessing the confined-space hazards.

C.text: Commercial pricing cannot determine whether a worker should be exposed to a dangerous enclosed atmosphere.

D.text: Tool selection follows the safe method; arranging tools first assumes entry before avoidance has been considered.

questions.prompt: After plans and a suitable locating device have identified an underground power cable, which listed approach should be used for trial holes and final exposure?

options.A: A 360 degree excavator with rubber tyres
options.D: Careful safe digging with suitable hand tools, using insulated tools near the cable and exposing it from the side where practicable

questions.explanation: HSE requires planning, cable plans, trained use of locating devices and safe excavation. Trial holes and final exposure normally use carefully controlled suitable hand tools, with insulated tools near electricity cables; 'hand digging' alone was too vague to describe the safe system.

A.text: Rubber tyres do not prevent a bucket tooth cutting a live cable or protect people from arc-flash energy.

B.text: A powered breaker can penetrate cable protection before the operator detects it and is unsuitable for final exposure.

C.text: A pickaxe concentrates uncontrolled impact at its point and can pierce a cable with little warning.

D.text: HSE requires planning, cable plans, trained use of locating devices and safe excavation. Trial holes and final exposure normally use carefully controlled suitable hand tools, with insulated tools near electricity cables; 'hand digging' alone was too vague to describe the safe system.

questions.prompt: If an extension cable is to be run across a site road, what action should you take?

options.A: Don't do anything to protect the cable
options.B: Lay the cable over wooden boards
options.C: Place a rubber protection ramp over it and put up a sign stating 'Ramp Ahead'

questions.explanation: It is essential that the cable is protected from damage caused by passing traffic. A sign will warn road traffic of the ramp.

A.text: An unprotected cable can be crushed or cut by traffic, exposing live conductors and interrupting the supply.

B.text: Loose boards can shift, split or create a vehicle hazard and do not provide a designed cable-crossing system.

C.text: It is essential that the cable is protected from damage caused by passing traffic. A sign will warn road traffic of the ramp.

D.text: Casually thrown boards provide neither reliable mechanical protection nor adequate warning to approaching drivers.

questions.prompt: Before moving a mobile tower scaffold, to what maximum height should the tower be reduced under current HSE guidance?
questions.explanation: HSE says to reduce a tower to a maximum height of 4 m before moving it. The route must also be checked for overhead lines and obstructions, the ground must be firm and level, and no person or material should remain on the tower while it moves.

A.text: Reducing below 4 m may be prudent for a particular route, but 2 m is not HSE's stated general maximum before moving.

B.text: Three metres is conservative but does not state the published 4 m maximum that this factual question asks for.

C.text: HSE says to reduce a tower to a maximum height of 4 m before moving it. The route must also be checked for overhead lines and obstructions, the ground must be firm and level, and no person or material should remain on the tower while it moves.

D.text: Five metres exceeds HSE's maximum reduced height and increases overturning risk while the tower is moved.

questions.prompt: Who should operate plant and equipment on site?

options.A: An employee holding a full driving license
options.C: Only people over 18 years of age

questions.explanation: Never operate plant or equipment unless you have been trained and are authorised to do so.

A.text: A road driving licence does not cover construction plant controls, stability, attachments or site-specific hazards.

B.text: General experience does not demonstrate training on the particular machine or formal authority to use it.

C.text: Age alone cannot establish competence, and trained authorised younger workers may use some equipment under suitable controls.

D.text: Never operate plant or equipment unless you have been trained and are authorised to do so.

questions.prompt: What must you do when work equipment is found damaged?

options.B: Locked up so no one can use it
options.C: Take it out of use and report the defect to your supervisor or other responsible person

questions.explanation: Damaged equipment must not remain available for use. Remove it from service and report or label it through the site procedure so a competent person can assess, repair or replace it before it is used again.

A.text: A label alone is incomplete unless the equipment is also removed from availability and the defect is reported.

B.text: Locking equipment away controls immediate use but does not communicate the defect for assessment, repair or replacement.

C.text: Damaged equipment must not remain available for use. Remove it from service and report or label it through the site procedure so a competent person can assess, repair or replace it before it is used again.

D.text: Immediate disposal may be wasteful or unsafe; a competent person should determine whether repair or replacement is appropriate.

questions.prompt: Hand and power tools must be:

options.C: Suitable for the task and regularly inspected
options.D: The best that you can buy

questions.explanation: Tools must not create a risk to the user or others. This means they must be suitable and kept in good condition. This requires inspection before use.

A.text: Corporate colour has no bearing on guarding, electrical integrity or suitability for the material and operation.

B.text: Availability helps scheduling but cannot justify using an unsuitable, damaged or unmaintained tool.

C.text: Tools must not create a risk to the user or others. This means they must be suitable and kept in good condition. This requires inspection before use.

D.text: Price or marketing quality does not replace task suitability, correct safety features and maintained condition.

questions.prompt: Ladders should not be painted because:

options.B: The paint may cover a defect or damaged part of the ladder
options.C: The paint may not be suitable on metal parts of the ladder
options.D: The paint will make them slippery to use

questions.explanation: Painting a ladder can hide cracks, splits or other damage that would otherwise be visible during pre-use checks. Because such hidden defects could cause the ladder to fail under load, only clear preservatives that allow inspection should be used.

A.text: Future repainting is a maintenance inconvenience, not the safety reason for keeping the ladder surface visible.

B.text: Painting a ladder can hide cracks, splits or other damage that would otherwise be visible during pre-use checks. Because such hidden defects could cause the ladder to fail under load, only clear preservatives that allow inspection should be used.

C.text: Material compatibility can matter, but the principal danger is paint concealing cracks, splits or corrosion.

D.text: Suitable dry paint need not make every rung slippery; hidden structural damage is the more fundamental concern.

questions.prompt: What is the minimum height of the top guard-rail of a scaffold above the edge from which someone is liable to fall?
questions.explanation: Work at height rules require the top guard-rail to be at least 950mm above any edge where a person could fall, giving enough height to stop someone toppling over it. Lower rails would fail to provide effective edge protection.

A.text: Two metres is not the minimum top-rail height and would be an unnecessarily high dimension for this requirement.

B.text: Four hundred and seventy millimetres relates to limiting gaps and intermediate protection, not the top guard-rail height.

C.text: Nine hundred and ten millimetres reflects older figures and falls below the current 950 mm minimum for construction work.

D.text: Work at height rules require the top guard-rail to be at least 950mm above any edge where a person could fall, giving enough height to stop someone toppling over it. Lower rails would fail to provide effective edge protection.

questions.prompt: If work on or near a fragile roof cannot be avoided, which listed measure is part of the required fall-protection approach?

options.A: As long as you avoid any fragile areas it is safe
options.B: Use suitable stagings or platforms and combine them with appropriate edge protection and measures that prevent or mitigate a fall
options.C: It is safe to walk on the purlins
options.D: Walk straight across the roof to where you need to get to

questions.explanation: HSE's first requirement is to avoid work on or near a fragile surface where possible. Where access is unavoidable, a planned combination of stagings or platforms, guardrails, coverings, restraint or arrest and safety nets is normally needed; a crawling board by itself is not a complete control system.

A.text: Fragile areas may be hidden or poorly marked, and simply intending to avoid them provides no fall prevention.

B.text: HSE's first requirement is to avoid work on or near a fragile surface where possible. Where access is unavoidable, a planned combination of stagings or platforms, guardrails, coverings, restraint or arrest and safety nets is normally needed; a crawling board by itself is not a complete control system.

C.text: Purlins are not designed as access routes and a slip can put the worker directly onto a fragile sheet.

D.text: Crossing directly gives no protection against misidentified panels, loss of balance or a surface failing unexpectedly.

questions.prompt: Under what circumstances do the Work at Height Regulations permit a stepladder to be used on site?

options.C: Only when a risk assessment shows that safer alternatives have been ruled out and the task is of low risk and of short duration
options.D: Provided you can't fall 2 metres or more

questions.explanation: The WAH Regulations have not banned the use of ladders or stepladders, but they should be used sensibly.

A.text: Stepladders are not a default work platform; their use must be justified by task-specific risk and duration.

B.text: They are not banned and remain appropriate for some low-risk, short-duration work after assessment.

C.text: The WAH Regulations have not banned the use of ladders or stepladders, but they should be used sensibly.

D.text: The Regulations apply wherever a fall could injure, so a two-metre threshold does not determine permission.

questions.prompt: Which of the following items should not be in a first- aid box?
questions.explanation: Drugs must not be kept in a first aid box (Health and Safety guidance note INDG 214).

A.text: Disposable gloves protect both casualty and first-aider from blood and body-fluid contact and belong in the kit.

B.text: Drugs must not be kept in a first aid box (Health and Safety guidance note INDG 214).

C.text: Safety pins can secure triangular bandages and are a recognised non-medicinal first-aid item.

D.text: Triangular bandages support limbs and secure dressings and are standard first-aid supplies.

questions.prompt: After checking that it is safe to approach, what should you do when a worker who has fallen is unresponsive?

options.A: Find out if there were any witnesses
options.B: Put them in the recovery position
options.C: Call 999 immediately and send for the first-aider and an AED while assessing breathing and following the call handler's instructions
options.D: Try to protect them from any further injury

questions.explanation: Current Resuscitation Council UK guidance says to call 999 as soon as a person is found unresponsive, then assess breathing while the call is being connected. Summon the first-aider and AED too, and start CPR promptly if breathing is not normal.

A.text: Witness evidence can be gathered later; it must not delay emergency response to an unresponsive casualty.

B.text: Recovery position is appropriate only after breathing is assessed as normal and spinal concerns are considered.

C.text: Current Resuscitation Council UK guidance says to call 999 as soon as a person is found unresponsive, then assess breathing while the call is being connected. Summon the first-aider and AED too, and start CPR promptly if breathing is not normal.

D.text: Preventing further harm is important, but emergency help and breathing assessment cannot be postponed.

questions.prompt: In an on-site emergency, which of the following must a first-aider NOT do?

options.B: Give medicines to patients without authorization

questions.explanation: First-aid is concerned with preserving life and limb, and first-aiders are not trained to dispense medical treatments.

A.text: Controlling severe bleeding with appropriate first-aid measures is within the trained first-aider's role.

B.text: First-aid is concerned with preserving life and limb, and first-aiders are not trained to dispense medical treatments.

C.text: Resuscitation is a core emergency skill and must not be withheld when a casualty is not breathing normally.

D.text: An unconscious casualty requires assessment and appropriate care; unconsciousness is not a reason to avoid treatment.

questions.prompt: Modern portable fire extinguishers are predominantly red. How is the extinguishing medium additionally identified?

options.A: By the extinguisher's wording and a permitted colour-coded panel or band on the red body
options.B: During site induction, you will be told where the different types of extinguishers are
options.C: The type of extinguisher is written on a sign next to it
options.D: The weight and shape of the extinguisher

questions.explanation: The extinguisher label names the medium and a limited colour-coded area helps rapid identification, while the body is predominantly red. Location and shape alone are not reliable ways to choose the correct extinguisher for a fire.

A.text: The extinguisher label names the medium and a limited colour-coded area helps rapid identification, while the body is predominantly red. Location and shape alone are not reliable ways to choose the correct extinguisher for a fire.

B.text: Induction may explain locations, but memory of location does not identify an unfamiliar extinguisher in an emergency.

C.text: A nearby wall sign can be missing or obscured; identification must be carried on the extinguisher itself.

D.text: Different media can use similar cylinders, so weight and shape are not the standard identification system.

questions.prompt: A black-labelled fire extinguisher contains:

questions.prompt: When discharging carbon dioxide fire extinguishers, the nozzle:

questions.prompt: For fires involving spilled petrol, which types of fire extinguisher could you use?

options.A: Foam, carbon dioxide or dry powder
options.B: Water, carbon dioxide or dry powder

questions.explanation: Petrol is a flammable liquid, so the fire must be smothered or its chemical reaction interrupted rather than doused with water. Foam, carbon dioxide and dry powder all achieve this safely, whereas water would simply spread the burning fuel.

A.text: Petrol is a flammable liquid, so the fire must be smothered or its chemical reaction interrupted rather than doused with water. Foam, carbon dioxide and dry powder all achieve this safely, whereas water would simply spread the burning fuel.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is one of the recommended means of protecting your hearing?
questions.explanation: The others are not considered to be suitable types of hearing protection.

D.text: Cloth pads do not seal the ear or provide a rated reduction across hazardous frequencies.

questions.prompt: How would you recognise a hazardous substance?

options.A: By the hazard pictograms and other warning information on its label and safety data sheet
options.C: It will be in a suitable container
options.D: The colour of the label on the container

questions.explanation: Hazardous chemicals are identified from their classified label information, including pictograms, signal words and hazard statements, supported by the safety data sheet. Smell, container appearance or label colour alone is not a reliable test.

A.text: Hazardous chemicals are identified from their classified label information, including pictograms, signal words and hazard statements, supported by the safety data sheet. Smell, container appearance or label colour alone is not a reliable test.

B.text: Odour is subjective, may be absent and can occur only above a harmful exposure concentration.

questions.prompt: If you have been handling lead, how is it most likely to get into your blood stream?

options.A: By not reporting the matter to the HSE

options.C: By not washing your hands before eating

C.text: The route into the body is ingestion, normally from lead contamination on the hands.

D.text: Goggles protect the eyes; they do not control ingestion from eating with lead-contaminated hands.

questions.prompt: When should you wear safety footwear on site?

options.A: Only if the site conditions are wet
options.D: When there is a risk of a foot injury

questions.explanation: Suitable safety footwear should be worn if there is a risk of injury from objects falling onto the foot or sharp objects, such as nails, penetrating the sole.

A.text: Wet ground may justify waterproof footwear, but crushing and puncture risks also occur in dry conditions.

B.text: Scaffold work can present foot hazards, yet materials, nails and plant create the same need at ground level.

C.text: Indoor construction areas still contain falling objects, sharp debris and moving loads that can injure feet.

D.text: Suitable safety footwear should be worn if there is a risk of injury from objects falling onto the foot or sharp objects, such as nails, penetrating the sole.

questions.prompt: Which listed requirement must apply to a safety helmet supplied as PPE for work in Great Britain?

options.A: It is less than 1 year old
options.B: It must meet the applicable PPE product-safety requirements and bear a recognised conformity marking such as CE or UKCA
options.C: It is less than 2 years old
options.D: It is less than 5 years old

questions.explanation: A helmet's suitability is not established by a generic age limit. PPE placed on the Great Britain market must meet the applicable essential safety requirements and carry an accepted conformity marking; current law recognises both CE and UKCA routes, so CE-only wording was incomplete.

A.text: A one-year age limit is not a general conformity requirement and says nothing about the helmet's standard or condition.

B.text: A helmet's suitability is not established by a generic age limit. PPE placed on the Great Britain market must meet the applicable essential safety requirements and carry an accepted conformity marking; current law recognises both CE and UKCA routes, so CE-only wording was incomplete.

D.text: Five years is neither an automatic acceptance nor rejection rule and cannot replace conformity and pre-use checks.

questions.prompt: What is the most important item of personal protective equipment (PPE) when working on or near a highway?
questions.explanation: Near a live carriageway the greatest danger is being struck by moving traffic, so being seen is the priority. High-visibility clothing makes you conspicuous to drivers and plant operators in all light conditions, addressing the dominant risk that the other items do not.

A.text: A hard hat protects the head after an impact but does little to help a driver notice the worker in time.

B.text: Near a live carriageway the greatest danger is being struck by moving traffic, so being seen is the priority. High-visibility clothing makes you conspicuous to drivers and plant operators in all light conditions, addressing the dominant risk that the other items do not.

C.text: Safety footwear controls foot injuries, not the dominant risk of a moving vehicle striking an unseen person.

D.text: Waterproof clothing keeps the wearer dry but is not necessarily conspicuous to approaching traffic.

questions.prompt: When must you wear all personal protective equipment (PPE) provided by your employer?
questions.explanation: Under the PPE at Work Regulations 1992, employees must wear PPE as instructed.

A.text: Under the PPE at Work Regulations 1992, employees must wear PPE as instructed.

B.text: PPE must fit before use, but an unsuitable fit must be reported and remedied rather than treated as a general exemption.

C.text: The employer's instruction and risk assessment define when protection is needed; personal judgement cannot simply override them.

D.text: PPE use is a safety control, not a matter of preference whenever the wearer feels like using it.

questions.prompt: Which of the following MUST be recorded in an accident book after you have had an accident?
questions.explanation: The information to be entered in an accident book (BI510) includes when and where the accident happened, the name, address and occupation of the person who had the accident and details of how the accident happened and the injuries suffered.

C.text: The information to be entered in an accident book (BI510) includes when and where the accident happened, the name, address and occupation of the person who had the accident and details of how the accident happened and the injuries suffered.

D.text: A phone number is not a required accident-description field in the standard BI510 record.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following accounts for most accidents each year on construction sites?
questions.explanation: HSE statistics show clearly that there are more slips, trips and falls than any other type of accident on site.

questions.prompt: Accidents causing any injury should always be recorded in:
questions.explanation: Your employer carries the legal duty to keep accident records and to report serious events under RIDDOR, so injuries must go into their recording system. This ensures the incident is investigated, trends are monitored, and any future claim or enforcement enquiry is properly supported.

A.text: A diary is an informal project log and may omit the personal-injury details and privacy controls of the employer's system.

B.text: An engineer's day book records technical activity, not the employer's official injury record.

C.text: Your employer carries the legal duty to keep accident records and to report serious events under RIDDOR, so injuries must go into their recording system. This ensures the incident is investigated, trends are monitored, and any future claim or enforcement enquiry is properly supported.

D.text: A personal note can support memory, but it is not accessible or managed as the workplace's recognised accident record.

questions.prompt: Which option describes a manual-handling operation under the Manual Handling Operations Regulations?

options.B: Transporting or supporting a load by hand or bodily force, including lifting, putting down, pushing, pulling, carrying or moving it

questions.explanation: Manual handling is defined by the use of hand or bodily force to transport or support a load. It includes lifting and carrying but also putting down, pushing, pulling and moving a person, animal or object.

A.text: A fully automated movement uses machine power rather than hand or bodily force, so it is outside the definition.

B.text: Manual handling is defined by the use of hand or bodily force to transport or support a load. It includes lifting and carrying but also putting down, pushing, pulling and moving a person, animal or object.

C.text: A task is not classified by a vague mixture of mechanisms; the regulated element is transporting or supporting by bodily force.

D.text: A machine moving a load without bodily force is mechanised handling, not manual handling.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is advisable when lifting a load manually?

options.A: Use a stable stance, keep the load close and use slight bending of the back, hips and knees while avoiding twist and further back flexion
options.B: Bend the knees, keep the back straight, use power of back
options.C: Keep legs and back straight, use power of legs
options.D: Keep legs straight, bend back, use power of legs

questions.explanation: Current HSE technique favours a stable posture and slight coordinated bending, not a rigidly straight back or a deep squat. Keep the heaviest side close, secure the load, move smoothly and turn with the feet instead of twisting.

A.text: Current HSE technique favours a stable posture and slight coordinated bending, not a rigidly straight back or a deep squat. Keep the heaviest side close, secure the load, move smoothly and turn with the feet instead of twisting.

B.text: The back is not the power source for the lift, and forcing it rigidly straight is not current HSE technique.

C.text: Keeping both legs and back straight forces reaching and spinal bending and prevents a stable, close hold.

D.text: Straight legs combined with a bent back places the load far from the body and increases spinal leverage.

questions.prompt: In HSE's simple lifting-and-lowering risk filter, what guideline figure applies for a man handling an easily grasped load close to the body at about knuckle height?

options.A: 25 kg, as a risk-filter value rather than a guaranteed safe limit

D.text: Fifty kilograms is double the chart value and would require redesign or assistance, not reliance on a guideline.

questions.prompt: If moving a load may cause injury, what should you do before proceeding?

questions.explanation: The correct response is not simply to carry, drag or recruit someone informally. Hazardous handling should first be avoided where reasonably practicable; otherwise the task needs assessment and controls such as redesign, an aid or a planned team lift.

questions.prompt: Who has the duty to manage risks arising from your employer's work and protect its workers, while coordinating with others who control the construction site?

D.text: Your employer retains duties to manage its undertaking and protect workers, even on a shared construction site. questions.prompt: In a health and safety risk assessment, what does the term risk describe?

options.B: Any work activity that can be described as dangerous
options.C: Something with the potential to cause injury
options.D: The chance that a hazard will cause harm, considered together with how serious that harm could be

questions.explanation: A hazard is something with the potential to cause harm. Risk concerns the chance that harm will occur and the possible severity of its consequences; it is not simply the unsafe thing or activity itself.

B.text: Calling work dangerous identifies concern but does not evaluate how likely harm is or how severe it could be.

C.text: Something with potential to cause harm defines a hazard; risk evaluates that potential in its circumstances.

D.text: A hazard is something with the potential to cause harm. Risk concerns the chance that harm will occur and the possible severity of its consequences; it is not simply the unsafe thing or activity itself.

questions.prompt: What must be done before any work begins?

questions.prompt: Employers have to produce a written Health and Safety Policy statement when:

questions.prompt: The Health and Safety at Work Act requires employers to provide what for their employees?

questions.prompt: If you discover a hole or gap in a fire rated wall or floor that has not been fire-stopped, what should you do?

options.B: Ignore it unless it is causing a draught

questions.prompt: Under environmental law, which statement is true?

options.A: Companies and individuals can be prosecuted if they do not follow the law
options.B: Companies can be prosecuted, but not individuals

questions.explanation: Most environmental law is enforced against companies, but the regulator in the relevant part of the UK (the Environment Agency, SEPA or NIEA) can also prosecute company officers and even have powers to prosecute employees if they wilfully contribute to environmental harm.

A.text: Most environmental law is enforced against companies, but the regulator in the relevant part of the UK (the Environment Agency, SEPA or NIEA) can also prosecute company officers and even have powers to prosecute employees if they wilfully contribute to environmental harm.

questions.prompt: Which action will help to minimise waste?

options.A: Always order much more than usually required - just in case you need it
options.B: Leave materials unprotected in the rain
options.C: Only take or open what you need and return or reseal anything left over

questions.explanation: The hierarchy for managing waste is to reduce/reuse/recover. Reducing the amount of waste is therefore the first priority.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is good environmental practice?

options.B: Leaving skips uncovered in wet weather

B.text: Rainwater can increase skip weight, spread contamination and make recoverable waste harder to sort.

D.text: This is good practice, since it will help with waste recovery. If the waste is classified as hazardous waste (special waste in Scotland) proper segregation is also a legal requirement.

questions.prompt: Why must a live or potentially live unterminated optical-fibre end never be viewed directly or pointed towards anyone's eyes?

options.A: The beam can bore a hole through the skin
options.B: The beam can damage the eyes
options.C: The beam can transfer a strong electric current
options.D: The colour of the beam is very hypnotic

questions.explanation: Active communications fibre can emit concentrated optical radiation, including wavelengths that are not visible. Viewing the end can focus that energy onto the retina and cause eye injury, so the link should be treated as active until proved otherwise.

A.text: Communications optical power can injure the retina but does not behave like a cutting beam boring through skin.

B.text: Active communications fibre can emit concentrated optical radiation, including wavelengths that are not visible. Viewing the end can focus that energy onto the retina and cause eye injury, so the link should be treated as active until proved otherwise.

D.text: Some hazardous wavelengths are invisible; hypnosis by colour is fictional and would miss the retinal exposure risk.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is true with regard to the dangers of electricity?

options.A: Electricity is dangerous at any time because you cannot tell by looking at a cable whether or not it is live
options.B: Electricity is only dangerous if you are not wearing wellington boots
options.C: Electricity is only dangerous in wet weather
options.D: Electricity is perfectly safe so long as you wear cotton gloves

questions.explanation: The features which make electricity so dangerous are that you cannot see, hear or smell it. It can give you a very unpleasant surprise. Always assume that cables are live.

B.text: Wellington boots are not a universal electrical safeguard and may be wet, damaged or unsuitable for the voltage.

C.text: Dry weather does not prove a conductor dead or remove the possibility of a fatal current path.

D.text: Cotton gloves have no electrical insulating rating and do not make contact with energised parts safe.

questions.prompt: The probes of voltage detectors and test instruments used on electrical systems should be:

options.D: Shaped or have barriers to prevent finger contact with the tips

D.text: In addition, to protect against damage by overcurrent whilst in use, the probes or instrument should incorporate suitable high breaking capacity (hbc) fuses with a low current rating (usually not exceeding 500 mA), or current-limiting resistors.

questions.prompt: In accordance with the Electricity at Work regulations, when considering whether to work live a responsible person should:
questions.explanation: To identify and assess the risks involved and the methods of controlling them.

C.text: Dead working is the normal approach, but the decision process still requires assessment of the actual circumstances.

questions.prompt: To prove a circuit or equipment is dead after isolation what is the FIRST activity in the sequence of events?

options.C: Check that the voltage detector is working on a proving device, known live source or in- built test feature
options.D: Make sure equipment is not working

questions.explanation: This will prove that that the voltage detector (such as a two-pole voltage detector or proprietary test lamp) is working, i.e. indicating voltage.

C.text: This will prove that that the voltage detector (such as a two-pole voltage detector or proprietary test lamp) is working, i.e. indicating voltage.

D.text: Equipment not operating may result from a control fault and does not prove every conductor is dead.

questions.prompt: Which listed device is specifically intended to provide additional protection against electric shock by rapidly disconnecting for some residual-current faults?

options.A: A 3 amp fuse should prevent a person receiving a fatal electric shock
options.B: A 30 mA Residual Current Device (RCD), although it does not make contact with live parts safe or guarantee survival
options.C: A 5 amp rewireable fuse should prevent a person receiving a fatal electric shock
options.D: A 6 amp circuit breaker should prevent a person receiving a fatal electric shock

questions.explanation: A 30 mA RCD can limit the energy in some electric shocks and can save life, but it detects only residual-current imbalance and is additional protection. questions.prompt: Why may young people be more at risk on site?

options.B: There is no specific legislation applying to them

B.text: Health and safety law includes specific protection for young people through assessment of their inexperience and maturity.

C.text: Health and Safety guidance lists young people as often being 'at particular risk', due to their lack of practical experience.

D.text: Leaving an inexperienced person alone would increase rather than explain or control their vulnerability.

questions.prompt: You are asked to enter a manhole where a toxic or oxygen-deficient atmosphere may be present, but no assessed safe system or suitable respiratory protection has been provided. What should you do?

options.D: Do not enter; report it so entry can be avoided or a competent risk-assessed system, atmosphere controls, training and rescue arrangements can be put in place

questions.prompt: You have to walk across a site several times a day, but have to dodge a lot of site traffic. The first thing you should do is:
