questions.explanation: Pedestrian routes should have been set up to keep people and vehicles apart, so inform your employer if the system is not working. Don't hitch rides on vehicles unless safe seating is provided.

A.text: Speaking informally to drivers does not redesign the route or place the traffic risk under site management control.

B.text: Riding on an undesigned part of a vehicle creates a crushing or fall risk and is not a safe alternative to walking.

C.text: Pedestrian routes should have been set up to keep people and vehicles apart, so inform your employer if the system is not working. Don't hitch rides on vehicles unless safe seating is provided.

D.text: Walking at the edge may introduce blind corners or reversing hazards and should not replace an assessed pedestrian route.

questions.prompt: How often should user (visual) checks be carried out on portable electrical equipment?
questions.explanation: All items of portable electrical equipment should be visually checked for safety by the user before being put into use.

A.text: An annual check can miss damage for many months on equipment that is handled and moved repeatedly.

B.text: Daily checking is too infrequent where the same item changes users or is used several times in one day.

C.text: All items of portable electrical equipment should be visually checked for safety by the user before being put into use.

D.text: Weekly inspection leaves each use dependent on conditions that may have changed since the previous check.

questions.prompt: To operate a powered hand tool you must be:
questions.explanation: There are no general age restrictions in legislation relating to the use of work equipment. Any person using work equipment, however, must be competent to do so, which will require initial and refresher training.

A.text: Reaching age sixteen does not demonstrate knowledge of the tool, its hazards or the controls for the task.

B.text: Being eighteen may remove some young-person restrictions, but age alone does not establish competence.

C.text: A twenty-one-year threshold is not the control; an older untrained person can still operate the tool dangerously.

D.text: There are no general age restrictions in legislation relating to the use of work equipment. Any person using work equipment, however, must be competent to do so, which will require initial and refresher training.

questions.prompt: Of the following, which is the poorest method of securing a ladder?

options.B: Securing the base of the ladder

questions.explanation: Footing a ladder is the last resort and should be avoided. Other more suitable access equipment should be used where practicable.

A.text: Footing a ladder is the last resort and should be avoided. Other more suitable access equipment should be used where practicable.

B.text: Securing the base is a physical restraint and is more reliable than depending on another person's attention and strength.

C.text: Tying the ladder near the top provides positive restraint and is preferred where a suitable point is available.

D.text: A suitable stability device controls movement mechanically and is preferable to relying on a person footing it.

questions.prompt: Before moving a mobile tower scaffold, to what maximum height should the tower be reduced under current HSE guidance?
questions.explanation: HSE says to reduce a tower to a maximum height of 4 m before moving it. The route must also be checked for overhead lines and obstructions, the ground must be firm and level, and no person or material should remain on the tower while it moves.

A.text: Reducing below 4 m may be prudent for a particular route, but 2 m is not HSE's stated general maximum before moving.

B.text: Three metres is conservative but does not state the published 4 m maximum that this factual question asks for.

C.text: HSE says to reduce a tower to a maximum height of 4 m before moving it. The route must also be checked for overhead lines and obstructions, the ground must be firm and level, and no person or material should remain on the tower while it moves.

D.text: Five metres exceeds HSE's maximum reduced height and increases overturning risk while the tower is moved.

questions.prompt: What do the letters SWL stand for?
questions.explanation: Machinery and accessories for lifting loads should be clearly marked to indicate their safe working loads.

A.text: SWL marks a permissible load, not a working height or level from which equipment may be used.

B.text: Machinery and accessories for lifting loads should be clearly marked to indicate their safe working loads.

C.text: The recognised term uses 'safe working', not 'satisfactory weight', because it defines an equipment loading limit.

D.text: 'Satisfactory working limit' is not the standard expansion shown on lifting equipment and accessories.

questions.prompt: Your supervisor asks you to use a powered hand-tool which has a rotating blade. You notice that the guard is missing from the blade. What do you do?

options.A: Contact the manufacturer of the tool
options.B: Inform your supervisor that the tool is unsafe and that the guard must be replaced before it is used
options.C: Try to make an improvised guard yourself
options.D: Use the tool anyway, you haven't had an accident with it before

questions.explanation: It is essential that supervisors are aware of faulty or damaged equipment.

A.text: Manufacturer contact may support repair, but the immediate action is to stop use and report the missing guard locally.

B.text: It is essential that supervisors are aware of faulty or damaged equipment.

C.text: An improvised guard may lack strength, clearance and secure fixing and can itself contact the rotating blade.

D.text: Past luck is no evidence of safety; one contact with an exposed blade can cause catastrophic injury.

questions.prompt: When can you work from a ladder?

options.A: For short periods and then only if it is safe to do so
options.D: When not being used for access

questions.explanation: Ladders are primarily means of access, not workplaces. They can be worked from, but only if the use of other, more suitable, work equipment is not appropriate and the task is of low risk and of short duration.

A.text: Ladders are primarily means of access, not workplaces. They can be worked from, but only if the use of other, more suitable, work equipment is not appropriate and the task is of low risk and of short duration.

B.text: Availability is not a risk assessment; a safer platform may be required even when a ladder is close at hand.

C.text: Sufficient length addresses reach only and says nothing about duration, task risk, stability or maintaining handhold.

D.text: A ladder used as access does not become a suitable workplace merely when nobody is climbing through it.

questions.prompt: You have been asked to operate a cherry-picker (mobile elevated work platform) when it is very windy. What should your FIRST consideration be?

options.A: Does the wind-speed make it unsafe to use the machine
options.B: Tie all light-weight objects to the hand-rails of the basket
options.C: Wear a safety harness and clip it to the structure that you are working on
options.D: Wear an extra layer of clothing to keep warm

questions.explanation: The priority in safety is eliminating risk at source - in this case by not working in dangerous conditions - rather than trying to stay safe by using protective equipment.

A.text: The priority in safety is eliminating risk at source - in this case by not working in dangerous conditions - rather than trying to stay safe by using protective equipment.

B.text: Securing loose items helps, but it does not establish whether wind can overturn or destabilise the MEWP itself.

C.text: Clipping to the external structure can create crushing or ejection hazards and does not make excessive wind safe.

D.text: Extra clothing addresses comfort only; it provides no control over the machine's wind-speed operating limit.

questions.prompt: A ladder giving access to a scaffold can generally be safely used, provided that:

options.A: Any broken rungs are clearly marked
options.B: It does not move when you climb up it
options.C: It is tied and extends at least 1 metre above the platform
options.D: The foot of the ladder is firmly wedged

questions.explanation: Access ladders should extend at least 1 metre above the landing point to provide a safe handhold.

A.text: Marking a broken rung does not restore its load capacity and leaves an obvious fall hazard in the access route.

B.text: A ladder may feel steady during one climb yet still lack positive restraint and safe handhold above the landing.

C.text: Access ladders should extend at least 1 metre above the landing point to provide a safe handhold.

D.text: Wedging only the foot may shift and does not provide the secure tying and extension needed at the platform edge.

questions.prompt: A red-labelled fire extinguisher should NOT be used:

options.D: Where there is a risk of electrocution

questions.explanation: Red denotes water. Liquids should not be used on electrical fires, since they can conduct electricity.

A.text: Water can cool burning clothing once electrical sources are excluded; electrocution is the distinctive prohibition here.

B.text: Water is suitable for many ordinary solid combustibles such as furniture when no electrical or liquid-fuel hazard exists.

C.text: Wood is a Class A fuel for which a water extinguisher is normally effective after electrical risks are ruled out.

D.text: Red denotes water. Liquids should not be used on electrical fires, since they can conduct electricity.

questions.prompt: A labourer gets an electric shock; looks a bit pale but says they are alright. What should you do?

options.A: Go and check the electrics so it cannot happen again
options.B: See if they want a drink or a cigarette
options.D: Tell them to report it to their supervisor

questions.explanation: An electric shock can cause delayed effects on the heart and the casualty may collapse even while appearing fine, so they should never be left unchecked. Summoning the first-aider ensures proper assessment and monitoring, and the incident can be escalated to emergency services if needed.

A.text: Investigating the equipment can expose another person and delays assessment of a casualty with possible internal effects.

B.text: Drink or smoking offers no treatment and may be unsafe if the casualty deteriorates or needs medical care.

C.text: An electric shock can cause delayed effects on the heart and the casualty may collapse even while appearing fine, so they should never be left unchecked. Summoning the first-aider ensures proper assessment and monitoring, and the incident can be escalated to emergency services if needed.

D.text: Reporting to a supervisor is necessary, but the pale casualty first needs a trained health assessment.

questions.prompt: Your workmate suddenly gets a foreign body in the eye. What should you do?

options.B: Take your workmate to the supervisor
options.C: Use a clean handkerchief to try and remove it
options.D: Wash your hands before touching your mate's face

questions.explanation: Attempting to remove a foreign body yourself risks scratching the cornea or driving the object deeper, causing lasting damage. A trained first-aider knows how to assess and treat eye injuries safely, so the correct response is to send for them immediately.

A.text: Attempting to remove a foreign body yourself risks scratching the cornea or driving the object deeper, causing lasting damage. A trained first-aider knows how to assess and treat eye injuries safely, so the correct response is to send for them immediately.

B.text: A supervisor is not necessarily trained to assess an eye injury, so this detour can delay appropriate first aid.

C.text: A handkerchief can scratch the cornea or push an embedded particle deeper into the eye.

D.text: Clean hands do not make untrained removal safe; the eye should be assessed by the first-aider.

questions.prompt: A workmate lifting a big box suddenly shouts "oh, my back" and drops the box. What should you do?

options.A: Find them somewhere comfortable to sit and rest
options.B: Help them to lift the box
options.D: Tell them to leave it for someone else to lift

questions.explanation: The priority for any back injury is to obtain first-aid advice, in order to prevent further damage.

A.text: Rest may feel helpful, but sudden back pain after lifting needs assessment before the casualty is moved or work resumes.

B.text: Continuing the lift can worsen the casualty's injury and expose the helper to the same uncontrolled load.

C.text: The priority for any back injury is to obtain first-aid advice, in order to prevent further damage.

D.text: Leaving the box addresses the task but not the injured person, who still needs competent first-aid assessment.

questions.prompt: A black-labelled fire extinguisher contains:
questions.explanation: Under the current colour-coding all extinguisher bodies are red with a coloured panel showing the contents, and the black panel denotes carbon dioxide. CO2 is non-conductive and leaves no residue, making it suitable for electrical and flammable-liquid fires.

A.text: Under the current colour-coding all extinguisher bodies are red with a coloured panel showing the contents, and the black panel denotes carbon dioxide. CO2 is non-conductive and leaves no residue, making it suitable for electrical and flammable-liquid fires.

B.text: Dry powder uses the blue identification panel, not the black panel associated with carbon dioxide.

C.text: Foam is identified by a cream panel and has different suitability from carbon dioxide on electrical equipment.

D.text: A water extinguisher is all red or carries the water wording, rather than a black medium panel.

questions.prompt: What is a blue-labelled fire extinguisher filled with?
questions.explanation: Extinguishers carry a coloured panel to identify their contents, and a blue panel indicates dry powder. Powder is a versatile multi-purpose agent that smothers solid, liquid and gas fires, though its residue makes it less ideal indoors.

A.text: Carbon dioxide is identified by black, not blue, and discharges as a gas rather than powder.

B.text: Extinguishers carry a coloured panel to identify their contents, and a blue panel indicates dry powder. Powder is a versatile multi-purpose agent that smothers solid, liquid and gas fires, though its residue makes it less ideal indoors.

C.text: Foam carries a cream identification panel and is selected for different classes of fire.

D.text: Water is identified by the plain red scheme and must not be confused with blue-labelled powder.

questions.prompt: What colour is a water filled fire extinguisher, or its label?
questions.explanation: Water extinguishers are identified by a red panel, historically the whole body being red before the panel system. Water cools and is effective on ordinary combustibles such as wood and paper, but must never be used on live electrical or flammable-liquid fires.

A.text: Black identifies carbon dioxide, a gas used for different fire risks from ordinary water extinguishers.

B.text: Cream identifies foam, not water, despite both media being useful on some solid combustibles.

C.text: Green is not the current UK identification colour for a water extinguisher.

D.text: Water extinguishers are identified by a red panel, historically the whole body being red before the panel system. Water cools and is effective on ordinary combustibles such as wood and paper, but must never be used on live electrical or flammable-liquid fires.

questions.prompt: What action should you take if you discover a fire?

options.A: Carry on working if it is safe to do so
options.B: Extinguish the fire without raising the alarm
options.C: Leave it because you will get the blame

questions.explanation: Raising the alarm will reduce the risk to others, particularly if the fire spreads.

A.text: Continuing work ignores an escalating emergency and prevents the site's fire procedure from starting.

B.text: Attempting extinction without warning people can delay evacuation and leave the worker trapped if the fire grows.

C.text: Fear of blame cannot justify leaving others unaware of a fire that may spread rapidly.

D.text: Raising the alarm will reduce the risk to others, particularly if the fire spreads.

questions.prompt: The extended use of powered hand-held tools and equipment may lead to which medical condition?
questions.explanation: Hand-arm vibration can cause a range of conditions (including vibration white finger) collectively known as hand-arm vibration syndrome, as well as diseases such as carpal tunnel syndrome.

A.text: Asbestosis follows inhalation of asbestos fibres, not vibration transmitted from powered hand tools.

B.text: Dermatitis arises from skin irritants or allergens and is not the characteristic vascular and nerve effect of vibration.

C.text: Hand-arm vibration can cause a range of conditions (including vibration white finger) collectively known as hand-arm vibration syndrome, as well as diseases such as carpal tunnel syndrome.

D.text: Weil's disease is an infection associated with animal urine, wet ground and waterways, not tool vibration.

questions.prompt: Wearing suitable hearing protection:

options.A: Brings noise down to an acceptable level

questions.explanation: Hearing protection still allows some noise to reach the ear, but, if it has been correctly chosen, will reduce noise levels to an acceptable level.

A.text: Hearing protection still allows some noise to reach the ear, but, if it has been correctly chosen, will reduce noise levels to an acceptable level.

B.text: Hearing protection prevents further exposure; it cannot repair sensory cells already damaged by noise.

C.text: Suitable protectors attenuate noise rather than eliminating all sound, allowing essential warnings to remain audible.

D.text: Conversation reduction may occur, but selection is based on hazardous noise exposure rather than social distraction.

questions.prompt: Which of the following does NOT cause skin problems?
questions.explanation: Asbestos is hazardous because its fibres are inhaled and cause serious lung disease, not because it attacks the skin. Bitumens, epoxy resins and solvents, by contrast, are recognised causes of dermatitis and other skin conditions through direct contact.

A.text: Asbestos is hazardous because its fibres are inhaled and cause serious lung disease, not because it attacks the skin. Bitumens, epoxy resins and solvents, by contrast, are recognised causes of dermatitis and other skin conditions through direct contact.

B.text: Bitumen and its solvents can irritate skin and cause dermatitis, especially with repeated hot-material contact.

C.text: Epoxy resins are potent skin sensitisers and can produce persistent allergic contact dermatitis.

D.text: Solvents remove natural skin oils and can cause irritation, dryness and occupational dermatitis.

questions.prompt: When should you wear safety footwear on site?

options.A: Only if the site conditions are wet
options.D: When there is a risk of a foot injury

questions.explanation: Suitable safety footwear should be worn if there is a risk of injury from objects falling onto the foot or sharp objects, such as nails, penetrating the sole.

A.text: Wet ground may justify waterproof footwear, but crushing and puncture risks also occur in dry conditions.

B.text: Scaffold work can present foot hazards, yet materials, nails and plant create the same need at ground level.

C.text: Indoor construction areas still contain falling objects, sharp debris and moving loads that can injure feet.

D.text: Suitable safety footwear should be worn if there is a risk of injury from objects falling onto the foot or sharp objects, such as nails, penetrating the sole.

questions.prompt: When is head protection required to be worn on a construction site to comply with the Personal Protective Equipment at Work Regulations?

options.A: At all times except by those who are self employed
options.B: At all times unless there is no foreseeable risk of injury to the head other than by falling.
options.C: At all times unless you are working on scaffold
options.D: Only when you feel like it

questions.explanation: If there is no risk of injury to the head, then hard hats are not required by law. However, on construction sites, despite controls being in place, there will almost always be situations where a risk of head injury remains and require head protection to be worn. Site rules will also require the wearing of head protection other than in any designated safe areas.

A.text: Self-employed status does not remove the need for head protection where the assessment identifies a foreseeable injury risk.

B.text: If there is no risk of injury to the head, then hard hats are not required by law. However, on construction sites, despite controls being in place, there will almost always be situations where a risk of head injury remains and require head protection to be worn. Site rules will also require the wearing of head protection other than in any designated safe areas.

C.text: Scaffold work can expose the head to falling or swinging objects; location on a scaffold is not an exemption.

D.text: Personal preference cannot override the risk assessment, site rules or instructions for required protective equipment.

questions.prompt: In which of the following ways should you wear your safety helmet?

options.A: Square on your head, properly adjusted
options.B: With the helmet back to front
options.C: With the peak raised to deflect falling material
options.D: With the peak raised to give good vision

questions.explanation: Any item of personal protective equipment must be used in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions, which will include how to correctly fit and wear it and what its limitations are.

A.text: Any item of personal protective equipment must be used in accordance with the manufacturer's instructions, which will include how to correctly fit and wear it and what its limitations are.

B.text: Reversing a helmet can compromise its suspension, peak and tested impact performance unless the manufacturer specifically permits it.

C.text: Tilting the peak changes the designed fit and can expose the forehead instead of deflecting material safely.

D.text: Visibility problems require a correctly selected and adjusted helmet, not lifting it away from its tested wearing position.

questions.prompt: An entry must be made in the accident book when:

options.A: an accident causes personal injury to an employee
options.C: the person has been off sick for over seven days
options.D: the severity of the accident may result in a compensation claim

questions.explanation: An accident causing an injury to an employee at work should be recorded in the accident book (BI 510).

A.text: An accident causing an injury to an employee at work should be recorded in the accident book (BI 510).

B.text: Management discretion is not a dependable recording threshold; the factual injury record should not depend on opinion.

C.text: Seven-day incapacity determines a category of RIDDOR reporting, while the accident record also covers shorter injuries.

D.text: The purpose of the record includes prevention and evidence, so it must not wait for someone to predict a compensation claim.

questions.prompt: In hot weather, what should you do where the risk assessment or site rules still require a safety helmet?

options.A: You can drill holes in your safety hat for ventilation
options.B: You can take off your helmet while working inside the building
options.C: You do not need to wear your helmet
options.D: You must continue to wear your helmet

questions.explanation: Continue to wear suitable head protection correctly while the residual head-injury risk remains. Do not drill or modify it; report heat concerns so shade, breaks, hydration or suitable compatible equipment can be considered without removing required protection.

A.text: Drilling holes weakens the shell and invalidates the helmet's tested impact and penetration performance.

B.text: Being indoors does not eliminate falling or swinging objects, so location alone cannot justify removing the helmet.

C.text: Hot weather does not cancel the assessed head-injury risk; heat must be managed without abandoning required protection.

D.text: Continue to wear suitable head protection correctly while the residual head-injury risk remains. Do not drill or modify it; report heat concerns so shade, breaks, hydration or suitable compatible equipment can be considered without removing required protection.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT classified as a specified injury to a worker under RIDDOR?
questions.explanation: Amputation of an arm, hand, finger, thumb, leg, foot or toe are classified as specified injuries, as are bone fractures other than to fingers, thumbs or toes.

A.text: A wrist fracture is a fracture outside the fingers, thumbs and toes, so it falls within RIDDOR's specified-injury category.

B.text: A fractured arm is explicitly within the reportable category of fractures other than fingers, thumbs or toes.

C.text: Amputation of an arm, hand, finger, thumb, leg, foot or toe are classified as specified injuries, as are bone fractures other than to fingers, thumbs or toes.

D.text: Amputation of a finger is specifically listed as a specified injury even though a simple finger fracture is excluded.

questions.prompt: If you are involved in a minor accident at work, whose duty is it to report it to site management?

options.C: The police, fire or ambulance who attend
options.D: The site foreman should report it

questions.explanation: The person involved is best placed to know what happened, so the duty to report rests with you. Prompt self-reporting ensures the event is recorded, first aid given if needed, and the cause investigated before it leads to a more serious incident.

A.text: A witness should report what was seen, but the injured worker must not assume somebody else will report a minor incident for them.

B.text: The person involved is best placed to know what happened, so the duty to report rests with you. Prompt self-reporting ensures the event is recorded, first aid given if needed, and the cause investigated before it leads to a more serious incident.

C.text: Emergency services may not attend a minor incident and are not responsible for the site's internal accident record.

D.text: A foreman can assist once told, but cannot report an injury they may not have seen or known about.

questions.prompt: Which is the correct way to lift a load?

options.A: Keep feet apart and bend back
options.B: Keep feet together and bend back
options.C: Squat near load, bend back and use leg muscles
options.D: Adopt a stable stance, get a secure hold, keep the load close and use slight bending of the back, hips and knees without twisting or further back flexion

questions.explanation: HSE advises a stable foot position, a secure hold, keeping the load close and slight bending of the back, hips and knees. A full deep squat or a deliberately bent back is not the universal correct technique, and handling technique does not replace risk reduction or lifting aids.

A.text: Bending mainly through the back while holding a load away from the body increases spinal leverage and instability.

B.text: Feet together provide a narrow, unstable base, and deliberate back bending increases strain.

C.text: A deep squat with a bent back is not a universal safe method and may create high knee and back loads.

D.text: HSE advises a stable foot position, a secure hold, keeping the load close and slight bending of the back, hips and knees. A full deep squat or a deliberately bent back is not the universal correct technique, and handling technique does not replace risk reduction or lifting aids.

questions.prompt: What is the most common type of injury resulting from lifting loads from the floor?
questions.explanation: Lifting from floor level encourages bending and twisting of the spine under load, placing great strain on the lower back. This makes back injuries the most common result, which is why correct technique and mechanical aids are emphasised in manual handling guidance.

A.text: Lifting from floor level encourages bending and twisting of the spine under load, placing great strain on the lower back. This makes back injuries the most common result, which is why correct technique and mechanical aids are emphasised in manual handling guidance.

B.text: Knee grazes may occur, but floor-level lifting more commonly overloads the lower back through poor posture and leverage.

C.text: A head injury is not the characteristic manual-handling outcome unless a separate falling-object event occurs.

D.text: Vibration white finger results from prolonged vibration exposure, not from a single floor-lifting movement.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is advisable when lifting a load manually?

options.A: Use a stable stance, keep the load close and use slight bending of the back, hips and knees while avoiding twist and further back flexion
options.B: Bend the knees, keep the back straight, use power of back
options.C: Keep legs and back straight, use power of legs
options.D: Keep legs straight, bend back, use power of legs

questions.explanation: Current HSE technique favours a stable posture and slight coordinated bending, not a rigidly straight back or a deep squat. Keep the heaviest side close, secure the load, move smoothly and turn with the feet instead of twisting.

A.text: Current HSE technique favours a stable posture and slight coordinated bending, not a rigidly straight back or a deep squat. Keep the heaviest side close, secure the load, move smoothly and turn with the feet instead of twisting.

B.text: The back is not the power source for the lift, and forcing it rigidly straight is not current HSE technique.

C.text: Keeping both legs and back straight forces reaching and spinal bending and prevents a stable, close hold.

D.text: Straight legs combined with a bent back places the load far from the body and increases spinal leverage.

questions.prompt: What is the main colour on a safety sign stating that you must NOT do something?
questions.explanation: Prohibitory signs are round and feature a black pictogram on a white background with red edging and diagonal line.

A.text: Blue means an action is mandatory, which is the opposite of a prohibition.

B.text: Green identifies a safe condition such as first aid or an emergency exit.

C.text: Prohibitory signs are round and feature a black pictogram on a white background with red edging and diagonal line.

D.text: Yellow is used to warn about a hazard and calls for caution rather than banning an action.

questions.prompt: The Health and Safety (Safety Signs and Signals) Regulations require the colour coding of safety signs. What colours are used on a sign indicating a prohibited activity, for example "No access for pedestrians"?
questions.explanation: Prohibitory signs are round and feature a black pictogram on a white background with red edging and diagonal line.

A.text: Blue and white communicates a mandatory positive instruction rather than an activity that is forbidden.

B.text: Green and white identifies a safe condition or emergency facility and does not prohibit pedestrian entry.

C.text: Prohibitory signs are round and feature a black pictogram on a white background with red edging and diagonal line.

D.text: Yellow and black warns of a hazard; prohibition requires the red circular form with black and white detail.

questions.prompt: Which is the part of your body MOST LIKELY to be injured during a manual handling activity which involves moving a heavy load?
questions.explanation: Moving heavy loads typically loads the spine, especially when the back is bent or twisted, so the back is the most vulnerable area. Damage to the discs and muscles there is a leading cause of long-term injury, hence the focus on good lifting posture.

A.text: Moving heavy loads typically loads the spine, especially when the back is bent or twisted, so the back is the most vulnerable area. Damage to the discs and muscles there is a leading cause of long-term injury, hence the focus on good lifting posture.

B.text: Chest injury is possible in a crush event, but ordinary heavy handling most commonly overloads the back and supporting tissues.

C.text: Forearms can fatigue while gripping, yet the spine usually bears the greater injury risk from load leverage and twisting.

D.text: Knees can be stressed by poor posture, but back injury is the most common concern across heavy manual-handling tasks.

questions.prompt: In a health and safety risk assessment, what does the term risk describe?

options.B: Any work activity that can be described as dangerous
options.C: Something with the potential to cause injury
options.D: The chance that a hazard will cause harm, considered together with how serious that harm could be

questions.explanation: A hazard is something with the potential to cause harm. Risk concerns the chance that harm will occur and the possible severity of its consequences; it is not simply the unsafe thing or activity itself.

A.text: An unsafe act or condition is a hazard or contributing circumstance, not the combination of likelihood and consequence.

B.text: Calling work dangerous identifies concern but does not evaluate how likely harm is or how severe it could be.

C.text: Something with potential to cause harm defines a hazard; risk evaluates that potential in its circumstances.

D.text: A hazard is something with the potential to cause harm. Risk concerns the chance that harm will occur and the possible severity of its consequences; it is not simply the unsafe thing or activity itself.

questions.prompt: In what circumstances can an HSE Improvement Notice be issued?

options.B: If there is a breach of legal requirements
options.C: Only between Monday and Friday on site

questions.explanation: Improvement notices require action to achieve standards which meet health and safety law.

A.text: An appointed inspector serves an improvement notice under statutory powers without first obtaining a police warrant.

B.text: Improvement notices require action to achieve standards which meet health and safety law.

C.text: Enforcement powers are not restricted to weekdays; the issue is the legal breach, not the day of inspection.

D.text: Prosecution is a separate enforcement route and is not the office through which an improvement notice is issued.

questions.prompt: Which one of the following must be in a company's written Health and Safety Policy:

options.A: Aims and objectives of the company
options.C: Name of the Health and Safety Adviser
options.D: Organization and arrangements in force for carrying out the health and safety policy

questions.explanation: This is a specific requirement of the Health and Safety at Work Act.

A.text: Aims belong in the statement of intent, but this choice omits the required responsibilities and practical arrangements.

B.text: A director's private address is not part of the policy structure and contributes nothing to managing workplace risk.

C.text: Naming an adviser does not allocate all responsibilities or describe the systems through which the policy operates.

D.text: This is a specific requirement of the Health and Safety at Work Act.

questions.prompt: What do the letters HSE stand for?
questions.explanation: HSE is the Health and Safety Executive, the body that enforces health and safety legislation across Great Britain. It publishes guidance, carries out inspections and prosecutes those who breach their statutory duties to protect people at work.

A.text: The organisation regulates and enforces workplace safety; it is not called an examiner.

B.text: HSE is the Health and Safety Executive, the body that enforces health and safety legislation across Great Britain. It publishes guidance, carries out inspections and prosecutes those who breach their statutory duties to protect people at work.

C.text: 'Exercise' describes an activity and is not part of the regulator's official name.

D.text: HSE is a national regulator, not a qualification or title for an electrician.

questions.prompt: In addition to preserving fire separation between areas of a building, which other important fire safety function can fire-stopping achieve?
questions.explanation: During the fire, it is essential that the load-bearing capacity of elements of the building structure are maintained until the occupants have escaped. Timber studs, joists or 'I' beams, for example, may only have a short survival time if exposed to fire and may rely on linings, such as plasterboard ceiling, for fire resistance. Services passing through such linings should therefore be fire-stopped.

A.text: During the fire, it is essential that the load-bearing capacity of elements of the building structure are maintained until the occupants have escaped. Timber studs, joists or 'I' beams, for example, may only have a short survival time if exposed to fire and may rely on linings, such as plasterboard ceiling, for fire resistance. Services passing through such linings should therefore be fire-stopped.

B.text: Acoustic sealing may be a secondary benefit, but it is not the additional life-safety function being tested here.

C.text: Nuisance alarms concern detection-system design; sealing service penetrations does not prevent detector activation.

D.text: Energy efficiency can improve when gaps are sealed, but it does not describe fire-stopping's structural protection role.

questions.prompt: The purpose of fire-stopping in a building is to:

options.B: Delay the passage of fire and smoke through openings in walls and floors

questions.explanation: Fire-stopping is a passive fire protection measure used to seal any openings created in a fire resistance-rated wall or floor assembly, e.g. to allow pipes or wiring systems to pass through. During fire conditions this will impede the spread of fire and smoke.

A.text: Sprinkler activation is an active-system function; fire-stopping is passive protection within walls and floors.

B.text: Fire-stopping is a passive fire protection measure used to seal any openings created in a fire resistance-rated wall or floor assembly, e.g. to allow pipes or wiring systems to pass through. During fire conditions this will impede the spread of fire and smoke.

C.text: Fire-stopping cannot prevent ignition, but it can contain the products of a fire after one starts.

D.text: Alarm initiation belongs to detectors and call points, not to the material sealing a compartment boundary.

questions.prompt: Why should different types of waste be separated on site?

options.A: So the local council can charge Landfill Tax
options.B: So the main contractor can check what's being thrown away
options.C: So waste can be recovered more easily
options.D: They will take up less room in the skip

questions.explanation: This is good practice, since waste recovery can save both energy and materials, compared to creating brand new materials or items. It will also cut the amount of waste that goes to landfill. If the waste is classed as hazardous (special waste in Scotland) then the effective separation of different wastes is a legal requirement.

A.text: Landfill tax is not the operational reason for separation; mixed waste prevents useful materials being recovered cleanly.

B.text: Inspection by the main contractor may support compliance, but it is not the environmental purpose of segregation.

C.text: This is good practice, since waste recovery can save both energy and materials, compared to creating brand new materials or items. It will also cut the amount of waste that goes to landfill. If the waste is classed as hazardous (special waste in Scotland) then the effective separation of different wastes is a legal requirement.

D.text: Separated containers may use more space; the benefit is preserving distinct recyclable and hazardous waste streams.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT best practice from a sustainability point of view?

options.A: Looking after the people working on or near the site
options.C: Saving materials, fuel, water and energy
options.D: Sending unused and waste copper cables to landfill

questions.explanation: Option D) would be wasting a valuable natural resource (copper) that could be effectively recovered for later use or recycling. Reusing or recycling copper has less environmental impact than mining and extracting new copper reserves.

A.text: Protecting workers and neighbours is part of the social element of sustainable construction.

B.text: Preventing pollution and ecological damage preserves resources for current and future users.

C.text: Reducing material, fuel, water and energy use cuts both resource depletion and avoidable emissions.

D.text: Option D) would be wasting a valuable natural resource (copper) that could be effectively recovered for later use or recycling. Reusing or recycling copper has less environmental impact than mining and extracting new copper reserves.

questions.prompt: If you have unused material left, what should you do before you consider putting non-hazardous waste items into a skip?

options.A: Check whether someone else on your team can make use of it
options.B: Make sure there is a label on it
options.C: Put it in a plastic bag and put it in a skip

questions.explanation: Although reducing the amount of waste is the first priority, the reuse of waste materials is much better than disposal, which is the most expensive option and which should be the last resort. Reuse is a better waste management option than recovery.

A.text: Although reducing the amount of waste is the first priority, the reuse of waste materials is much better than disposal, which is the most expensive option and which should be the last resort. Reuse is a better waste management option than recovery.

B.text: Labelling helps identify material but does not itself prevent a useful item from entering the waste stream.

C.text: Discarding a usable remainder creates avoidable waste before reuse by the team has been considered.

D.text: Weight may affect handling or waste records but does not determine whether another worker can use the material.

questions.prompt: The Electricity at Work Regulations require that:

options.A: A training course is necessary before anyone can work with electricity
options.B: Anyone supervised can work with electricity
options.C: Only electricians can work with electricity
options.D: People must have adequate knowledge or experience, or be under an appropriate degree of supervision, to prevent danger and injury

questions.explanation: Regulation 16 permits work where technical knowledge or experience is necessary only when the person has that competence or is under an appropriate degree of supervision. It does not require every worker to already possess the same unsupervised competence.

A.text: A course may contribute to competence, but the Regulation focuses on effective knowledge, experience or supervision.

B.text: Supervision must be appropriate to prevent danger; the mere presence of any supervisor is not enough.

C.text: Job title is not the legal test, and non-electricians may do limited work when competence or supervision is adequate.

D.text: Regulation 16 permits work where technical knowledge or experience is necessary only when the person has that competence or is under an appropriate degree of supervision. It does not require every worker to already possess the same unsupervised competence.

questions.prompt: Which of the following should be used to prove a circuit or equipment is dead after isolation?

options.A: A lamp holder with a length of flex attached
options.C: A proprietary test lamp or two-pole voltage detector

questions.explanation: Accident history has shown that using incorrectly set multimeters or makeshift devices for voltage detection has often caused accidents. The use of non-contact voltage indicators (voltage sticks) is also not advised as the sole means of proving dead.

A.text: A makeshift lamp and flex lacks protected probe tips, appropriate ratings and a controlled indication of voltage.

B.text: A multimeter can be mis-set or give a misleading reading and is not the preferred device for proving dead.

C.text: Accident history has shown that using incorrectly set multimeters or makeshift devices for voltage detection has often caused accidents. The use of non-contact voltage indicators (voltage sticks) is also not advised as the sole means of proving dead.

D.text: A non-contact voltage stick can miss screened or poorly coupled conductors and cannot prove absence of voltage.

questions.prompt: The use of a multi-lock hasp with the appropriate number of padlocks is a recommended method of safe isolation where:

options.A: Individual circuit breaker locking off devices are not available
options.B: Individual circuit breakers are not identified at the distribution board
options.C: More than one person will be working on circuits supplied from the same distribution board
options.D: You know the health and safety inspector is in the area

questions.explanation: A multi-lock hasp can be used to prevent operation of the isolator until such time that all persons working on the electrical installation have completed their work and removed their padlocks from the hasp.

A.text: The need for a hasp comes from multiple personal locks, not from the absence of a device for one circuit-breaker.

B.text: Unidentified circuits must be traced and labelled; a multi-lock hasp cannot correct uncertainty about the isolation point.

C.text: A multi-lock hasp can be used to prevent operation of the isolator until such time that all persons working on the electrical installation have completed their work and removed their padlocks from the hasp.

D.text: Isolation arrangements are based on people exposed to reconnection risk, not on whether an inspector is nearby.

questions.prompt: What colour cable USUALLY signifies 110 volt power supply on site?
questions.explanation: Yellow is the usual colour of cables, socket outlets, plugs and transformers etc which are used with a 110 volt supply.

A.text: Black is not the recognised site connector and cable identification for the 110 V reduced-low-voltage system.

B.text: Blue is associated with the 230 V range and would risk connecting equipment to the wrong nominal supply.

C.text: Red is associated with 400 V three-phase supplies, not the ordinary 110 V site-tool system.

D.text: Yellow is the usual colour of cables, socket outlets, plugs and transformers etc which are used with a 110 volt supply.

questions.prompt: What action should you take if a workmate gets an electric shock?

options.A: Cut off the power and call for help
options.B: Dial 999 and ask for the fire brigade
options.D: Try to pull them to safety

questions.explanation: If you can switch the power off, the electric hazard will be removed. First aid assistance will then probably be required. Do not touch someone who is still in contact with live electrical cables as you could also receive an electric shock.

A.text: If you can switch the power off, the electric hazard will be removed. First aid assistance will then probably be required. Do not touch someone who is still in contact with live electrical cables as you could also receive an electric shock.

B.text: Emergency medical help may be needed, but asking specifically for the fire brigade does not first stop current through the casualty.

C.text: The network operator is not the immediate rescue service and a phone call leaves the casualty connected to danger.

D.text: Touching or pulling the casualty before isolation can pass the shock current through the rescuer too.

questions.prompt: Under Regulation 14 of the Electricity at Work Regulations 1989, when may work on or near a live conductor that may give rise to danger proceed?

options.A: Only when it is unreasonable in all the circumstances for the conductor to be dead, it is reasonable to work live, and suitable precautions are taken to prevent injury
options.B: When the means of isolation cannot be identified
options.C: When the person carrying out the work is a competent person
options.D: When the person working on the equipment is wearing rubber gloves

questions.explanation: All three Regulation 14 conditions must be satisfied. Live work must be justified because making dead is unreasonable, carrying it out live must itself be reasonable, and suitable precautions, including suitable protective equipment where necessary, must prevent injury.

A.text: All three Regulation 14 conditions must be satisfied. Live work must be justified because making dead is unreasonable, carrying it out live must itself be reasonable, and suitable precautions, including suitable protective equipment where necessary, must prevent injury.

B.text: Difficulty identifying isolation does not satisfy the statutory tests; the supply must be traced and the work properly planned.

C.text: Competence is necessary for dangerous electrical work, but competence alone does not justify leaving the conductor live.

D.text: Rubber gloves are only one possible precaution and cannot replace the three legal conditions for live work.

questions.prompt: What is the purpose of using a 'permit to work' system?

options.A: To enable tools and equipment to be properly checked before the commencement of work
options.B: To ensure that the client will pay for the work
options.C: To ensure the job is carried out by the quickest method
options.D: To help ensure a safe system of work

questions.explanation: A permit to work is a written system used to control certain types of hazardous work. They allow work to start only when site procedures have been clarified.

A.text: Tool checks may be included, but a permit principally coordinates hazards, isolations, boundaries and authorisation for the work.

B.text: Payment belongs to the contract and is unrelated to the permit's control of hazardous work.

C.text: Speed is not the permit's objective and can conflict with the deliberate checks required for safe execution.

D.text: A permit to work is a written system used to control certain types of hazardous work. They allow work to start only when site procedures have been clarified.

questions.prompt: You have to enter a manhole in which you know there are toxic gases. You have all the PPE but there does not appear to be a rescue plan in place. What should you do?

options.A: Ask your mate to stand-by at the top of the manhole with a length of rope
options.B: Do not enter the manhole until a rescue plan and rescue equipment are in place
options.C: Just get on and do the job, it will probably be alright
options.D: Plan to carry out the job in short bursts

questions.explanation: A rescue plan must be in place before anyone enters a confined space. This is one of the requirements of the Confined Spaces Regulations 1997.

A.text: A person with a rope is not a competent rescue system and may become another casualty without suitable equipment.

B.text: A rescue plan must be in place before anyone enters a confined space. This is one of the requirements of the Confined Spaces Regulations 1997.

C.text: Possessing PPE does not control foreseeable emergency recovery, so entry without a rescue plan remains unsafe.

D.text: Short entries can still lead to sudden incapacitation, and planned bursts do not provide rescue capability.

questions.prompt: You have to walk across a site several times a day, but have to dodge a lot of site traffic. The first thing you should do is:

options.B: Jump on the back of a vehicle if you can, it's safer than walking
options.C: Tell your supervisor about the danger
options.D: Walk around the edges of the site to keep out of the way

questions.explanation: Pedestrian routes should have been set up to keep people and vehicles apart, so inform your employer if the system is not working. Don't hitch rides on vehicles unless safe seating is provided.

A.text: Speaking informally to drivers does not redesign the route or place the traffic risk under site management control.

B.text: Riding on an undesigned part of a vehicle creates a crushing or fall risk and is not a safe alternative to walking.

C.text: Pedestrian routes should have been set up to keep people and vehicles apart, so inform your employer if the system is not working. Don't hitch rides on vehicles unless safe seating is provided.

D.text: Walking at the edge may introduce blind corners or reversing hazards and should not replace an assessed pedestrian route.

questions.prompt: If an electric drill gives off blue smoke from the motor, you should:

options.C: Switch it off and report it

questions.explanation: Defective electric hand tools must not be used. Stop what you are doing and inform your supervisor.

A.text: Water on energised equipment creates a shock path and may spread an electrical fire or damage adjacent equipment.

B.text: Cooling time does not diagnose insulation or motor failure and cannot make a smoking drill safe to restart.

C.text: Defective electric hand tools must not be used. Stop what you are doing and inform your supervisor.

D.text: An extinguisher is for an established fire; smoke from a running motor first requires isolation and defect reporting.

questions.prompt: If you only have a mains voltage (230 V) hand drill and you want to use it on a construction site which only has yellow (110 V) socket-outlets, what should you do?

options.A: Cut the plug off and fit a yellow one instead
options.B: Make up an extension cable with a yellow plug on one end and a standard socket on the other end
options.C: Obtain a 110 V drill or a cordless one for the work
options.D: Use a transformer to boost the voltage

questions.explanation: Electrical equipment must not be modified or operated at voltages other than their design voltage.

A.text: Changing only the plug exposes a 230 V drill to the wrong voltage and defeats connector coding without converting the tool.

B.text: A mixed-voltage adaptor defeats keying and can allow 230 V equipment or sockets to be misused dangerously.

C.text: Electrical equipment must not be modified or operated at voltages other than their design voltage.

D.text: A boost transformer would require a properly designed system and defeats the safer site supply; it is not an improvised solution.

questions.prompt: If you are about to use a power tool and discover the guard is missing, you should:

options.A: Make up a temporary guard yourself
options.B: Not use the tool until a proper guard has been fitted
options.C: Use the tool but try to work quickly
options.D: Use the tool but work carefully and slowly

questions.explanation: Visual checks should be carried out before using equipment. Any faults should be reported immediately and rectified before use.

A.text: A homemade guard lacks the tool's tested strength, clearances and interlocks and may create new trapping hazards.

B.text: Visual checks should be carried out before using equipment. Any faults should be reported immediately and rectified before use.

C.text: Working quickly increases loss-of-control risk and gives no protection from the exposed moving part.

D.text: Slow operation does not prevent contact, ejection or entanglement with an unguarded power tool.

questions.prompt: What is the best method of securing a ladder?

options.B: Tying it to a suitable point
options.C: Using an effective ladder stability device
options.D: Wedging the ladder (eg against a wall)

questions.explanation: Tying the ladder is the safest option, making sure both stiles are tied.

A.text: Footing depends on another person's continuous attention and is HSE's last-resort method when securing is not practicable.

B.text: Tying the ladder is the safest option, making sure both stiles are tied.

C.text: A stability device is useful where tying is not practicable, but positive tying remains the preferred method listed.

D.text: Wedging can move or crush and does not provide the reliable upper restraint achieved by tying to a sound point.

questions.prompt: The power hand tool you are about to use has burn marks visible on the cable. What should you do?

options.A: Carry on and get the job done
options.B: Obtain another machine and carry on, but don't tell anyone
options.C: Tape over the affected area and continue
options.D: Tell your supervisor about the defect and do not use the tool

questions.explanation: It is essential that supervisors are aware of faulty or damaged equipment.

A.text: Visible heat damage may expose conductors or weakened insulation, so finishing the task risks shock or fire.

B.text: Using another tool controls immediate exposure but leaves the damaged one unreported and available to the next user.

C.text: Tape hides rather than assesses thermal damage and may not restore the cable's insulation, flexibility or strain relief.

D.text: It is essential that supervisors are aware of faulty or damaged equipment.

questions.prompt: A scaffold tower must be erected by:

options.C: The hire company who supply it

questions.explanation: There are a number of organizations that provide training for the safe erection and use of tower scaffolds.

A.text: There are a number of organizations that provide training for the safe erection and use of tower scaffolds.

B.text: Seniority does not demonstrate practical knowledge of the tower system, bracing sequence or stability requirements.

C.text: The supplier may erect it, but supply alone does not make that company the only competent erector.

D.text: A foreman's title does not automatically include recognised tower-scaffold training or demonstrated competence.

questions.prompt: On a mobile elevating work platform, what should you attach your safety harness to?

options.B: A secure anchorage point inside the platform
options.C: A strong part of the structure you are working on

questions.explanation: The priority is to stay within the platform (which is the safest place), and in any event you cannot be sure of the strength of other fixtures.

A.text: A nearby pipe or scaffold is outside the platform, may be weak and can create ejection or crushing during movement.

B.text: The priority is to stay within the platform (which is the safest place), and in any event you cannot be sure of the strength of other fixtures.

C.text: Clipping to the work structure defeats the platform's movement and can pull the worker from the basket.

D.text: The boom is not automatically a designated anchor and may expose the lanyard to moving or trapping points.

questions.prompt: What should you do immediately if you get a small cut on a finger whilst at work?

options.A: Ask your employer to report it to the HSE

questions.explanation: It is important to obtain first-aid to prevent further harm (e.g. through infection). It should also be recorded in the accident book (BI 510).

A.text: A small cut is not ordinarily reported to HSE; immediate cleaning, dressing and workplace recording come first.

B.text: Continuing exposes the open wound to contamination and can worsen bleeding or infection.

C.text: It is important to obtain first-aid to prevent further harm (e.g. through infection). It should also be recorded in the accident book (BI 510).

D.text: Washing is useful first aid, but the wound should also be assessed and dressed through the site's provision.

questions.prompt: What does the sound of a siren on-site normally indicate?
questions.explanation: A site siren is the agreed signal that an emergency is in progress and that workers should respond to the site's emergency procedure. It does not by itself identify the specific cause; its purpose is to prompt immediate action such as evacuation.

A.text: Fire may be one emergency signalled, but workers should follow the site procedure rather than assume one cause.

B.text: A toxic release may use a siren, yet the same general alarm can cover other events requiring different actions.

C.text: A site siren is the agreed signal that an emergency is in progress and that workers should respond to the site's emergency procedure. It does not by itself identify the specific cause; its purpose is to prompt immediate action such as evacuation.

D.text: An explosion could trigger the alarm, but the sound itself does not establish that this specific event occurred.

questions.prompt: The type of accident that kills most construction site workers is:
questions.explanation: Although the other dangers can kill or cause injury, falling from height is the biggest cause of fatalities.

A.text: Falling objects can kill, but recent construction fatality statistics attribute the largest share to falls from height.

B.text: Electrical accidents remain serious, yet they account for fewer construction deaths than falls from height.

C.text: Although the other dangers can kill or cause injury, falling from height is the biggest cause of fatalities.

D.text: Trench collapses are foreseeable and often fatal, but they are not the leading fatal-accident type in the listed data.

questions.prompt: The rung of a wooden ladder has started to split, what should you do?

options.B: Do not use it, tell your supervisor
options.C: Jump on it to see if it holds your weight

questions.explanation: It is essential that supervisors are aware of faulty or damaged equipment.

A.text: Cutting the rung changes the ladder's structure and leaves an incomplete climbing surface rather than a sound repair.

B.text: It is essential that supervisors are aware of faulty or damaged equipment.

C.text: Loading a visibly split rung may make it fail and cause the very fall the check is intended to prevent.

D.text: Tape cannot restore the timber's load capacity and may conceal growth of the split from the next user.

questions.prompt: A red-labelled fire extinguisher should NOT be used:

options.D: Where there is a risk of electrocution

questions.explanation: Red denotes water. Liquids should not be used on electrical fires, since they can conduct electricity.

A.text: Water can cool burning clothing once electrical sources are excluded; electrocution is the distinctive prohibition here.

B.text: Water is suitable for many ordinary solid combustibles such as furniture when no electrical or liquid-fuel hazard exists.

C.text: Wood is a Class A fuel for which a water extinguisher is normally effective after electrical risks are ruled out.

D.text: Red denotes water. Liquids should not be used on electrical fires, since they can conduct electricity.

questions.prompt: How often should a first-aider qualified in First Aid at Work (FAW) or Emergency First Aid at Work (EFAW) receive retraining?
questions.explanation: First Aid at Work (FAW) and Emergency First Aid at Work (EFAW) certificates are valid for three years and first-aiders are required to undertake retraining at the end of this period. However, the HSE also strongly recommends that first-aiders undertake annual (half-day) refresher training.

A.text: Four years exceeds the three-year validity period of an FAW or EFAW certificate, leaving a gap in qualification.

B.text: Six months is not the certificate-renewal interval; HSE separately recommends shorter annual refresher practice.

C.text: First Aid at Work (FAW) and Emergency First Aid at Work (EFAW) certificates are valid for three years and first-aiders are required to undertake retraining at the end of this period. However, the HSE also strongly recommends that first-aiders undertake annual (half-day) refresher training.

D.text: Two-year retraining may be chosen voluntarily, but it is not the standard three-year certificate cycle asked for.

questions.prompt: Modern portable fire extinguishers are predominantly red. How is the extinguishing medium additionally identified?

options.A: By the extinguisher's wording and a permitted colour-coded panel or band on the red body
options.B: During site induction, you will be told where the different types of extinguishers are
options.C: The type of extinguisher is written on a sign next to it
options.D: The weight and shape of the extinguisher

questions.explanation: The extinguisher label names the medium and a limited colour-coded area helps rapid identification, while the body is predominantly red. Location and shape alone are not reliable ways to choose the correct extinguisher for a fire.

A.text: The extinguisher label names the medium and a limited colour-coded area helps rapid identification, while the body is predominantly red. Location and shape alone are not reliable ways to choose the correct extinguisher for a fire.

B.text: Induction may explain locations, but memory of location does not identify an unfamiliar extinguisher in an emergency.

C.text: A nearby wall sign can be missing or obscured; identification must be carried on the extinguisher itself.

D.text: Different media can use similar cylinders, so weight and shape are not the standard identification system.

questions.prompt: If you discover a fire at work, what should you do first:

options.A: Raise the alarm and warn fellow workers
options.B: Run around looking for an alarm to sound
options.D: Use a fire extinguisher to put it out

questions.explanation: Raising the alarm will reduce the risk to others, particularly if the fire spreads.

A.text: Raising the alarm will reduce the risk to others, particularly if the fire spreads.

B.text: Searching without immediately warning others delays evacuation; use the nearest recognised alarm method at once.

C.text: Emergency services should be called under the procedure, but people in immediate danger must first be alerted.

D.text: Trying to fight the fire before raising the alarm can trap the worker and leaves everyone else unaware.

questions.prompt: What are the lower and upper action values with regard to daily personal noise exposure, as defined in the Control of Noise at Work Regulations 2005?
questions.explanation: Daily personal noise exposure is the average noise level experienced by an individual over an 8 hour period.

A.text: Seventy and eighty decibels understate both statutory exposure action values in the Noise Regulations.

B.text: The upper value is right, but the lower action value begins at 80 dB(A), not 75 dB(A).

C.text: Daily personal noise exposure is the average noise level experienced by an individual over an 8 hour period.

D.text: Eighty-five is the upper action value, not the lower one, and 90 dB(A) is not the current upper action value.

questions.prompt: Hearing protection should be worn:
questions.explanation: Employees must wear hearing protectors when exposed at or above the upper exposure action values and within hearing protection zones.

A.text: Universal wear can overprotect workers and interfere with communication where the noise assessment does not require it.

B.text: Employees must wear hearing protectors when exposed at or above the upper exposure action values and within hearing protection zones.

C.text: Hazardous noise occurs outdoors as well as indoors, so building enclosure is not the deciding factor.

D.text: Factories, workshops and many other workplaces also designate hearing-protection zones; the rule is not site-specific.

questions.prompt: An emergency route(s) must be provided on construction sites to ensure:

options.A: Safe passage to a secure place of safety
options.B: Safe passage to the ground from height
options.C: Safe passage to the open air
options.D: Safe passage to the rest area

questions.explanation: Construction sites must provide emergency routes so that, in an incident, everyone can reach a secure place of safety away from danger. These routes must be kept clear and signed so people can evacuate quickly without being trapped or exposed to harm.

A.text: Construction sites must provide emergency routes so that, in an incident, everyone can reach a secure place of safety away from danger. These routes must be kept clear and signed so people can evacuate quickly without being trapped or exposed to harm.

B.text: Reaching ground level addresses only escape from height and may still leave people inside the danger zone.

C.text: Open air is not automatically safe if it remains exposed to fire, smoke, collapse or another site emergency.

D.text: A rest area is provided for welfare, not necessarily as a protected destination during an emergency.

questions.prompt: When an assessment of hazardous substances has been carried out under the COSHH Regulations, the risks and control measures should be explained to:

options.D: the person in charge of the stores

questions.explanation: All those working with the hazardous substances in question need to know about any risks.

A.text: People who never use or encounter the substance do not need task-specific detail; information must reach everyone who may actually be exposed.

B.text: Accounts staff deal with purchasing and payment, not the exposure controls needed at the point of use.

C.text: All those working with the hazardous substances in question need to know about any risks.

D.text: The storekeeper needs safe-storage information, but that alone leaves the operatives handling the substance uninformed.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is TRUE when an employer issues personal protective equipment (PPE)?

options.A: The employer can charge you for the full cost of it
options.B: The employer can charge you for up to half the cost of it
options.C: The employer can only charge you for it if you lose or damage it
options.D: The employer cannot charge you for it

questions.explanation: Employers cannot charge for PPE such as hard hats, gloves, required by law (and the bulk of PPE is required by law).

A.text: Required PPE used at work must be supplied free; its purchase cost cannot be transferred to the employee.

B.text: The no-charge duty is not a cost-sharing scheme, so charging half is no more acceptable than charging all of it.

C.text: Loss or damage may be handled under fair workplace procedures, but it does not turn statutory PPE provision into a sale to the worker.

D.text: Employers cannot charge for PPE such as hard hats, gloves, required by law (and the bulk of PPE is required by law).

questions.prompt: Can you opt out of wearing personal protective equipment (PPE)?

options.B: Yes, by informing the site supervisor
options.C: Yes, by writing officially to your employer

questions.explanation: You cannot legally "opt out" of being protected from significant risks at work. This includes wearing the necessary PPE.

A.text: You cannot legally "opt out" of being protected from significant risks at work. This includes wearing the necessary PPE.

B.text: A supervisor cannot waive a control required by the risk assessment merely because the worker gives notice.

C.text: A written request does not transfer the employer's duty or remove the employee's duty to use issued protection properly.

D.text: Poor fit should be reported and corrected with suitable equipment; discomfort is not permission to remain exposed.

questions.prompt: When MUST an employer provide their employees with personal protective equipment (PPE)?

options.B: If the client or main contractor specifies it in the contract
options.D: When they may be exposed to a risk to their health & safety which cannot be controlled another way

questions.explanation: PPE is a last line of defence under the hierarchy of risk control, so it becomes mandatory only once a hazard cannot be eliminated or adequately controlled by other means. Employers must then provide suitable equipment free of charge to protect employee health and safety.

A.text: PPE provision responds to the present residual risk, not a five-year replacement timetable.

B.text: A contract may add site rules, but the employer's statutory duty exists even when the client says nothing about PPE.

C.text: Inspection and replacement intervals depend on the equipment and condition; twice-yearly issue is not the legal trigger.

questions.prompt: Which would you consider to be generally correct when lifting a load?

questions.prompt: Which option describes a manual-handling operation under the Manual Handling Operations Regulations?

B.text: Employees have a statutory duty to take reasonable care and cooperate with safety arrangements.
