D.text: Employers carry primary management duties, while employees still owe duties to themselves and people affected by their acts.

questions.prompt: Who would you expect to carry out a risk assessment on your working site?
questions.explanation: Risk assessments must be carried out by someone with the knowledge, training and experience to recognise hazards and judge controls, which is what competent means in law. An HSE inspector audits rather than assesses for you, and the duty rests with the employer through a competent person.

A.text: Risk assessments must be carried out by someone with the knowledge, training and experience to recognise hazards and judge controls, which is what competent means in law. An HSE inspector audits rather than assesses for you, and the duty rests with the employer through a competent person.

B.text: An inspector checks whether the duty holder has assessed risk; the inspector does not write the site's assessment for it.

C.text: The former CDM co-ordinator role no longer exists under CDM 2015 and never replaced the employer's competent assessment process.

D.text: A designer assesses design risks, but does not automatically understand the contractor's people, tools and live site conditions.

questions.prompt: What must be done before any work begins?
questions.explanation: This is a legal requirement of the Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations.

A.text: This is a legal requirement of the Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations.

B.text: Emergency arrangements are important where required, but they follow identification of the credible events and risks.

C.text: A geological survey is relevant to some ground works, not every electrical or construction activity.

D.text: Soil assessment is needed for particular excavation or contamination risks and is not a universal first step for all work.

questions.prompt: Who should sign the statement of intent in a company's health and safety policy?

options.C: The employer or most senior person in the company

questions.explanation: HSE says the employer or most senior person should sign the policy statement and review it regularly. That may be the managing director in one company, but the role rather than a particular job title is the governing principle.

A.text: A safety officer may advise and administer the system, but the most senior leadership must own the statement of intent.

B.text: Company-secretary status does not necessarily carry executive control over the undertaking's health and safety commitments.

C.text: HSE says the employer or most senior person should sign the policy statement and review it regularly. That may be the managing director in one company, but the role rather than a particular job title is the governing principle.

D.text: A site manager controls a location but is not ordinarily the most senior person responsible for the company-wide policy.

questions.prompt: If you discover a hole or gap in a fire rated wall or floor that has not been fire-stopped, what should you do?

options.A: Cover the hole or gap with insulating tape
options.B: Ignore it unless it is causing a draught
options.C: Report it to your supervisor without delay
options.D: Use decorators' sealant to fill the gap

questions.explanation: Supervisors need to be made aware of any observed inadequacies in fire-stopping - which can undermine fire precautions catastrophically during the construction of buildings and on their completion. Only a limited range of products are suitable and they must be correctly applied to provide the required degree of fire-stopping.

A.text: Insulating tape has no tested fire-resistance rating and cannot reinstate a breached fire compartment.

B.text: A draught is irrelevant: any unsealed penetration can let smoke and flame bypass the fire-rated barrier.

C.text: Supervisors need to be made aware of any observed inadequacies in fire-stopping - which can undermine fire precautions catastrophically during the construction of buildings and on their completion. Only a limited range of products are suitable and they must be correctly applied to provide the required degree of fire-stopping.

D.text: Ordinary decorators' sealant is not a certified fire-stopping system matched to the wall or floor construction.

questions.prompt: What are fire-stops designed to do?

options.B: Delay the passage of fire and smoke through openings in walls and floors
options.D: Protect services (such as wiring systems) against fire damage

questions.explanation: Fire-stops are designed to maintain the fireproofing of a wall or floor assembly. Fire-stopping delays the spread of fire and, generally, the spread of smoke as well.

A.text: Door closers act on fire doors; fire-stops seal gaps and service penetrations in compartment boundaries.

B.text: Fire-stops are designed to maintain the fireproofing of a wall or floor assembly. Fire-stopping delays the spread of fire and, generally, the spread of smoke as well.

C.text: Fire-stopping contains fire and smoke but does not extinguish the burning material or replace firefighting equipment.

D.text: The main purpose is to maintain compartmentation, not to shield the cable or pipe itself from heat damage.

questions.prompt: From an environmental point of view, why should materials be reused, where possible?

options.A: A lot of energy and raw materials go into making most construction products
options.B: It makes less mess on site

questions.explanation: Although reducing the amount of waste is the first priority, the re-use of materials can also contribute to effective waste management.

A.text: Although reducing the amount of waste is the first priority, the re-use of materials can also contribute to effective waste management.

B.text: Less mess is useful housekeeping, but it does not explain the upstream environmental cost avoided by reuse.

C.text: Reuse is not justified by a blanket European-law requirement; its benefit comes from conserving resources and energy.

D.text: Client savings may follow, but cost alone is not the environmental reason for retaining useful material.

questions.prompt: Do individuals have any responsibility for minimising the amount of waste created on site?

options.A: No, it's the responsibility of the client
options.B: Only during site clean-up, at the end of the project
options.C: Only if asbestos removal is being carried out
options.D: Yes, everyone on site has this responsibility

questions.explanation: Your actions will help your company, and others on site, to procure sensibly and to organise the job so that materials and substances are not wasted. Waste reduction is the best option when trying to manage site waste.

A.text: The client influences procurement, but every worker can prevent damage, use only what is needed and sort remaining waste.

B.text: Waste is best prevented throughout delivery and installation; end-of-project clean-up is too late to recover wasted material.

C.text: Waste minimisation applies to ordinary packaging, off-cuts and surplus as well as specially controlled asbestos waste.

D.text: Your actions will help your company, and others on site, to procure sensibly and to organise the job so that materials and substances are not wasted. Waste reduction is the best option when trying to manage site waste.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a suitable means of isolating a circuit?

options.A: Fitting a padlocked circuit breaker lockout
options.C: Removing a fuse and securing the distribution board against access
options.D: Putting insulating tape over the circuit breaker instead of applying a secure lock-off device

questions.explanation: Tape does not secure an isolating device against inadvertent or unauthorised operation. HSE construction guidance explicitly contrasts tape over a circuit-breaker with a proper lock-off device, personal lock and safety notice.

A.text: A purpose-made circuit-breaker lockout and padlock secure the device against inadvertent operation.

B.text: Padlocking a suitable isolating switch provides the positive security that a safe isolation needs.

C.text: Removing the fuse and securing access can disconnect the circuit and prevent unauthorised replacement under the procedure.

D.text: Tape does not secure an isolating device against inadvertent or unauthorised operation. HSE construction guidance explicitly contrasts tape over a circuit-breaker with a proper lock-off device, personal lock and safety notice.

questions.prompt: Which of the following should be disposed of as hazardous/special waste?
questions.explanation: Hazardous wastes (special wastes in Scotland) are specified in waste legislation. Aerosol sealants are included because they can explode if not recovered or disposed of properly, and they may still contain hazardous solvents.

A.text: Hazardous wastes (special wastes in Scotland) are specified in waste legislation. Aerosol sealants are included because they can explode if not recovered or disposed of properly, and they may still contain hazardous solvents.

B.text: Uncontaminated glass-fibre off-cuts are not automatically hazardous waste, though dust still needs exposure control.

C.text: Ordinary untreated timber sheet off-cuts can normally follow a segregated wood-recovery route rather than hazardous disposal.

D.text: A nuisance-dust mask is not automatically hazardous unless it is contaminated by a substance that changes its classification.

questions.prompt: A portable electric generator on site has two power outlets, 110 volts and 230 volts. What colour would the 110 volt outlet be?
questions.explanation: Yellow is the usual colour of cables, socket outlets, plugs and transformers etc which are used with a 110 volt supply.

A.text: Black is not the BS EN 60309 identification colour for a 110 V reduced-low-voltage site connector.

B.text: Blue identifies the normal 200-250 V range, so it distinguishes 230 V equipment from the site 110 V supply.

C.text: Red identifies the 380-480 V range, commonly used for 400 V three-phase connections rather than 110 V.

D.text: Yellow is the usual colour of cables, socket outlets, plugs and transformers etc which are used with a 110 volt supply.

questions.prompt: Electrical installations on construction sites should be periodically inspected and tested:
questions.explanation: Three monthly inspections of construction site installations are recommended in IEE Guidance Note 3.

A.text: Three monthly inspections of construction site installations are recommended in IEE Guidance Note 3.

B.text: Six months exceeds the commonly specified three-month construction-site interval for temporary installations.

C.text: Monthly inspection may be chosen for higher risk, but it is not the stated general periodic interval.

D.text: A yearly interval is too long for temporary systems exposed to frequent movement, weather and site damage.

questions.prompt: Your job involves you working near to hanging electrical cables which have bare ends. What should you do?

options.A: Attempt to push the cables back into the ceiling void so that you can start work
options.B: Carry on working, as there shouldn't be a problem
options.C: Inform your supervisor and keep well away
options.D: Touch the cables to see if they are live

questions.explanation: You must always assume that exposed cables are live until you know they are not. Contact with live electrical cables can kill.

A.text: Moving unidentified bare conductors may bring them into contact with the worker or another live surface.

B.text: Appearance cannot prove the ends dead, so continuing nearby leaves an uncontrolled electrocution and arc risk.

C.text: You must always assume that exposed cables are live until you know they are not. Contact with live electrical cables can kill.

D.text: The human body must never be used as a voltage detector; touching can produce fatal current before any reaction is possible.

questions.prompt: An electrical Permit to Work is primarily a statement that:

options.A: Certain instructions need to be followed
options.B: Someone else has taken responsibility for the work
options.C: The circuit or equipment has been isolated and is safe to work on
options.D: The circuit or equipment is live

questions.explanation: Permits to work describe the procedures that prevent a major hazard, such as electricity or moving machinery, from causing harm, usually by isolation to effectively ensure (in the case of electricity) 'dead' working with no chance of it going 'live'.

A.text: A permit contains instructions, but its central assurance is the defined equipment state and boundary released for work.

B.text: Issuing a permit coordinates responsibilities; it does not transfer all responsibility away from the people doing the work.

C.text: Permits to work describe the procedures that prevent a major hazard, such as electricity or moving machinery, from causing harm, usually by isolation to effectively ensure (in the case of electricity) 'dead' working with no chance of it going 'live'.

D.text: A permit-to-work for dead work is not authority to treat the circuit as live or to bypass isolation.

questions.prompt: The nominal single phase voltage in the UK is?
questions.explanation: This is the nominal voltage for public electricity supply systems within Europe.

A.text: This is the nominal voltage for public electricity supply systems within Europe.

B.text: The harmonised UK nominal single-phase supply is 230 V, even though measured voltage may be near the historical 240 V value.

C.text: Four hundred volts is the nominal voltage between phases on a three-phase system, not single phase to neutral.

D.text: Four hundred and fifteen volts is the former three-phase nominal value and is not the present single-phase rating.

questions.prompt: To determine the safety of the atmosphere in an excavation, which of the following is essential

options.B: Only entering for a short period to enable a quick escape

questions.explanation: Use a suitable detector. Many dangerous gases have no smell, and cannot be seen. Workers can be overcome in seconds in dangerous atmospheres.

A.text: Toxic gases and oxygen deficiency are often invisible, so visual inspection cannot establish atmospheric safety.

B.text: A dangerous atmosphere can overcome a worker before a quick escape is possible, even during a short entry.

C.text: Smell is unreliable and the attempt exposes the worker; some lethal gases have no detectable odour.

D.text: Use a suitable detector. Many dangerous gases have no smell, and cannot be seen. Workers can be overcome in seconds in dangerous atmospheres.

questions.prompt: You are asked to enter a manhole where a toxic or oxygen-deficient atmosphere may be present, but no assessed safe system or suitable respiratory protection has been provided. What should you do?

options.A: Just get on with the job, and accept the risks
options.B: Look into the manhole to see if you can see any harmful gases
options.C: Sniff the atmosphere in the manhole to see if you can smell harmful gases
options.D: Do not enter; report it so entry can be avoided or a competent risk-assessed system, atmosphere controls, training and rescue arrangements can be put in place

questions.explanation: Confined-space entry should be avoided where possible. If it is essential, the employer must assess the atmosphere and other risks, implement a safe system, provide suitable equipment and training, and establish adequate rescue arrangements before entry. Asking only for generic RPE would be incomplete.

A.text: Entering without controls risks rapid collapse, poisoning or asphyxiation and may also endanger would-be rescuers.

B.text: Many toxic gases and oxygen deficiency are invisible, so looking into the opening cannot establish a safe atmosphere.

C.text: Hazardous atmospheres may have no warning odour, and sniffing exposes the worker before any measurement is made.

D.text: Confined-space entry should be avoided where possible. If it is essential, the employer must assess the atmosphere and other risks, implement a safe system, provide suitable equipment and training, and establish adequate rescue arrangements before entry. Asking only for generic RPE would be incomplete.

questions.prompt: A Cable Avoidance Tool (C.A.T.) and a 'Genny' (generator) can be used successfully to locate underground cables by whom:
questions.explanation: Equipment used to locate buried services must only be used by people who have been trained to use it.

A.text: Equipment used to locate buried services must only be used by people who have been trained to use it.

B.text: Employment by an electricity company does not prove training on the particular locator or site conditions.

C.text: Incorrect CAT and Genny use can falsely show an area clear, so unrestricted use by anyone is unsafe.

D.text: A foreman's role does not automatically include locator competence; training and demonstrated skill remain necessary.

questions.prompt: What is the preferred nominal voltage for portable hand tools on construction sites?
questions.explanation: 110 volt reduced low voltage systems are strongly preferred for the supply to such equipment.

A.text: 110 volt reduced low voltage systems are strongly preferred for the supply to such equipment.

B.text: Twelve volts may suit specialist very-high-risk conditions, but it is not the standard nominal site-tool supply.

C.text: Portable 230 V tools create a greater shock risk and are not the preferred general construction-site arrangement.

D.text: Twenty-four volts can be used for particular equipment, but UK site power tools normally use 110 V centre-tapped-to-earth.

questions.prompt: When using an extension cable reel, which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: Do not exceed the reeled or unreeled rating as appropriate
options.B: Leave as much as possible coiled up on the reel

questions.explanation: The rating of a partially unreeled extension cable is much lower than when fully unreeled. Overheating of the cable will occur if the rating is exceeded. Care should also be taken to prevent extension cables becoming a tripping hazard.

A.text: The rating of a partially unreeled extension cable is much lower than when fully unreeled. Overheating of the cable will occur if the rating is exceeded. Care should also be taken to prevent extension cables becoming a tripping hazard.

B.text: Leaving cable coiled can trap heat, and the lower reeled rating may be exceeded by the connected load.

C.text: Partial uncoiling still concentrates heat and is safe only when the manufacturer's corresponding current rating is observed.

D.text: Full uncoiling is unnecessary for a small load within the reel's stated coiled rating and can add trip hazards.

questions.prompt: Who should operate plant and equipment on site?

options.A: An employee holding a full driving license
options.C: Only people over 18 years of age

questions.explanation: Never operate plant or equipment unless you have been trained and are authorised to do so.

A.text: A road driving licence does not cover construction plant controls, stability, attachments or site-specific hazards.

B.text: General experience does not demonstrate training on the particular machine or formal authority to use it.

C.text: Age alone cannot establish competence, and trained authorised younger workers may use some equipment under suitable controls.

D.text: Never operate plant or equipment unless you have been trained and are authorised to do so.

questions.prompt: Hand and power tools must be:

options.C: Suitable for the task and regularly inspected
options.D: The best that you can buy

questions.explanation: Tools must not create a risk to the user or others. This means they must be suitable and kept in good condition. This requires inspection before use.

A.text: Corporate colour has no bearing on guarding, electrical integrity or suitability for the material and operation.

B.text: Availability helps scheduling but cannot justify using an unsuitable, damaged or unmaintained tool.

C.text: Tools must not create a risk to the user or others. This means they must be suitable and kept in good condition. This requires inspection before use.

D.text: Price or marketing quality does not replace task suitability, correct safety features and maintained condition.

questions.prompt: Ladders should not be painted because:

options.B: The paint may cover a defect or damaged part of the ladder
options.C: The paint may not be suitable on metal parts of the ladder
options.D: The paint will make them slippery to use

questions.explanation: Paint can conceal cracks, splits or other damage in a ladder's stiles and rungs, hiding defects that would otherwise be visible during inspection. Because hidden damage could cause the ladder to fail in use, only clear protective coatings are acceptable.

A.text: Future repainting is a maintenance inconvenience, not the safety reason for keeping the ladder surface visible.

B.text: Paint can conceal cracks, splits or other damage in a ladder's stiles and rungs, hiding defects that would otherwise be visible during inspection. Because hidden damage could cause the ladder to fail in use, only clear protective coatings are acceptable.

C.text: Material compatibility can matter, but the principal danger is paint concealing cracks, splits or corrosion.

D.text: Suitable dry paint need not make every rung slippery; hidden structural damage is the more fundamental concern.

questions.prompt: A working platform used for construction work, and from which a person could fall 2 metres or more, must not be used unless it has been inspected (and a report is subsequently prepared) by a competent person:
questions.explanation: Under these specific circumstances a report is required to be prepared by the competent person and given to the person for whom the inspection was done (e.g. the site manager). This is in addition to the more general requirement to inspect equipment for work at height: prior to use in that position (or site if it is mobile); following exceptional circumstances (e.g. high winds); and at suitable intervals.

A.text: An accident triggers an additional inspection, but it is not the only event requiring a platform inspection.

B.text: Inspection on the same day may be prudent but is not the maximum recurring seven-day interval stated in the Regulations.

C.text: A month is too long between recorded inspections for a construction working platform from which a person may fall.

D.text: Under these specific circumstances a report is required to be prepared by the competent person and given to the person for whom the inspection was done (e.g. the site manager). This is in addition to the more general requirement to inspect equipment for work at height: prior to use in that position (or site if it is mobile); following exceptional circumstances (e.g. high winds); and at suitable intervals.

questions.prompt: If work on or near a fragile roof cannot be avoided, which listed measure is part of the required fall-protection approach?

options.A: As long as you avoid any fragile areas it is safe
options.B: Use suitable stagings or platforms and combine them with appropriate edge protection and measures that prevent or mitigate a fall
options.C: It is safe to walk on the purlins
options.D: Walk straight across the roof to where you need to get to

questions.explanation: HSE's first requirement is to avoid work on or near a fragile surface where possible. Where access is unavoidable, a planned combination of stagings or platforms, guardrails, coverings, restraint or arrest and safety nets is normally needed; a crawling board by itself is not a complete control system.

A.text: Fragile areas may be hidden or poorly marked, and simply intending to avoid them provides no fall prevention.

B.text: HSE's first requirement is to avoid work on or near a fragile surface where possible. Where access is unavoidable, a planned combination of stagings or platforms, guardrails, coverings, restraint or arrest and safety nets is normally needed; a crawling board by itself is not a complete control system.

C.text: Purlins are not designed as access routes and a slip can put the worker directly onto a fragile sheet.

D.text: Crossing directly gives no protection against misidentified panels, loss of balance or a surface failing unexpectedly.

questions.prompt: What should you do immediately if you get a small cut on a finger whilst at work?

options.A: Ask your employer to report it to the HSE

questions.explanation: It is important to obtain first-aid to prevent further harm (e.g. through infection). It should also be recorded in the accident book (BI 510).

A.text: A small cut is not ordinarily reported to HSE; immediate cleaning, dressing and workplace recording come first.

B.text: Continuing exposes the open wound to contamination and can worsen bleeding or infection.

C.text: It is important to obtain first-aid to prevent further harm (e.g. through infection). It should also be recorded in the accident book (BI 510).

D.text: Washing is useful first aid, but the wound should also be assessed and dressed through the site's provision.

questions.prompt: According to HSE's Construction statistics in Great Britain 2025, which listed accident kind accounted for the largest share of construction worker deaths over 2020/21 to 2024/25?
questions.explanation: The fixed claim of about 70 deaths a year was obsolete. HSE recorded 35 worker fatalities in construction in 2024/25 and an annual five-year average of 40; falls from height accounted for 53% of deaths over that five-year period.

A.text: Vehicle and plant incidents cause deaths, but their five-year share was lower than that of falls from height.

B.text: Excavation collapse is a severe site hazard but did not account for the largest fatality category in the cited period.

C.text: The fixed claim of about 70 deaths a year was obsolete. HSE recorded 35 worker fatalities in construction in 2024/25 and an annual five-year average of 40; falls from height accounted for 53% of deaths over that five-year period.

D.text: Fire must be controlled, yet it represented far fewer construction worker deaths than falls from height.

questions.prompt: Before being used, a ladder should be inspected:
questions.explanation: The person about to climb is responsible for a pre-use check because they are there at the moment of use and rely on the ladder being sound. A quick inspection of stiles, rungs and feet catches damage that has appeared since any formal inspection.

A.text: A foreman may arrange formal checks, but the person using the ladder must still make the pre-use inspection.

B.text: Manufacturer inspection precedes sale and cannot reveal damage, contamination or alteration arising on site.

C.text: A safety officer cannot inspect every ladder immediately before each use or notice damage since a scheduled visit.

D.text: The person about to climb is responsible for a pre-use check because they are there at the moment of use and rely on the ladder being sound. A quick inspection of stiles, rungs and feet catches damage that has appeared since any formal inspection.

questions.prompt: A labourer gets an electric shock; looks a bit pale but says they are alright. What should you do?

options.A: Go and check the electrics so it cannot happen again
options.B: See if they want a drink or a cigarette
options.D: Tell them to report it to their supervisor

questions.explanation: Electric shock can disturb the heart's rhythm with effects that may not appear straight away, so the casualty needs proper assessment even if they seem fine. Fetching the first-aider ensures they are monitored, since looking pale can be an early warning of a deteriorating condition.

A.text: Investigating the equipment can expose another person and delays assessment of a casualty with possible internal effects.

B.text: Drink or smoking offers no treatment and may be unsafe if the casualty deteriorates or needs medical care.

C.text: Electric shock can disturb the heart's rhythm with effects that may not appear straight away, so the casualty needs proper assessment even if they seem fine. Fetching the first-aider ensures they are monitored, since looking pale can be an early warning of a deteriorating condition.

D.text: Reporting to a supervisor is necessary, but the pale casualty first needs a trained health assessment.

questions.prompt: Your workmate suddenly gets a foreign body in the eye. What should you do?

options.B: Take your workmate to the supervisor
options.C: Use a clean handkerchief to try and remove it
options.D: Wash your hands before touching your mate's face

questions.explanation: A foreign body in the eye should be dealt with by trained first-aid help, as attempting to remove it yourself can scratch the cornea or drive it deeper. Summoning the first-aider ensures the eye is treated correctly and irrigated rather than rubbed.

A.text: A foreign body in the eye should be dealt with by trained first-aid help, as attempting to remove it yourself can scratch the cornea or drive it deeper. Summoning the first-aider ensures the eye is treated correctly and irrigated rather than rubbed.

B.text: A supervisor is not necessarily trained to assess an eye injury, so this detour can delay appropriate first aid.

C.text: A handkerchief can scratch the cornea or push an embedded particle deeper into the eye.

D.text: Clean hands do not make untrained removal safe; the eye should be assessed by the first-aider.

questions.prompt: A workmate lifting a big box suddenly shouts "oh, my back" and drops the box. What should you do?

options.A: Find them somewhere comfortable to sit and rest
options.B: Help them to lift the box
options.D: Tell them to leave it for someone else to lift

questions.explanation: The priority for any back injury is to obtain first-aid advice, in order to prevent further damage.

A.text: Rest may feel helpful, but sudden back pain after lifting needs assessment before the casualty is moved or work resumes.

B.text: Continuing the lift can worsen the casualty's injury and expose the helper to the same uncontrolled load.

C.text: The priority for any back injury is to obtain first-aid advice, in order to prevent further damage.

D.text: Leaving the box addresses the task but not the injured person, who still needs competent first-aid assessment.

questions.prompt: For fires involving spilled petrol, which types of fire extinguisher could you use?

options.A: Foam, carbon dioxide or dry powder
options.B: Water, carbon dioxide or dry powder

questions.explanation: Burning petrol is a flammable-liquid fire that must be smothered, so foam, carbon dioxide or dry powder are suitable because they cut off the oxygen supply. Water is excluded because it spreads the floating fuel and carries the flames further.

A.text: Burning petrol is a flammable-liquid fire that must be smothered, so foam, carbon dioxide or dry powder are suitable because they cut off the oxygen supply. Water is excluded because it spreads the floating fuel and carries the flames further.

B.text: This combination includes water, which can spread floating petrol and enlarge the burning surface.

C.text: Carbon dioxide and foam may be suitable, but adding water makes the listed combination unsafe for spilled petrol.

D.text: Powder and foam may control the fire, yet the water in this group can carry burning fuel outward.

questions.prompt: Which types of fire extinguishers should be used on electrical fires?
questions.explanation: Carbon dioxide and dry powder are non-conductive extinguishing media, so they can be used where live electrical equipment is involved. CO2 leaves no residue; dry powder leaves substantial residue that can contaminate and damage electrical equipment, so power should be isolated and CO2 is normally the cleaner choice where it is suitable for the fire.

A.text: Carbon dioxide and dry powder are non-conductive extinguishing media, so they can be used where live electrical equipment is involved. CO2 leaves no residue; dry powder leaves substantial residue that can contaminate and damage electrical equipment, so power should be isolated and CO2 is normally the cleaner choice where it is suitable for the fire.

B.text: Dry powder can be used, but ordinary foam is conductive or leaves residue and is not the paired electrical-fire choice.

C.text: Both foam and water can conduct electricity and expose the operator while equipment remains energised.

D.text: Carbon dioxide is suitable, but pairing it with water introduces an electrocution risk.

questions.prompt: If there had been a small fire, who should you report it to?
questions.explanation: The supervisor should be aware, so that further preventative measures can be considered.

A.text: The main contractor may need notification through site arrangements, but the worker's immediate reporting line is the supervisor.

B.text: A resident engineer may have no responsibility for the worker or fire procedure and is not the normal first report.

C.text: The fire marshal manages evacuation duties; reporting through the supervisor ensures the incident is recorded and investigated.

D.text: The supervisor should be aware, so that further preventative measures can be considered.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is one of the recommended means of protecting your hearing?
questions.explanation: The others are not considered to be suitable types of hearing protection.

A.text: Loose cotton wool has no tested attenuation, fit or repeatable seal and is not certified hearing PPE.

B.text: The others are not considered to be suitable types of hearing protection.

C.text: Rolled tissue provides unpredictable, inadequate attenuation and can lodge in the ear canal.

D.text: Cloth pads do not seal the ear or provide a rated reduction across hazardous frequencies.

questions.prompt: How would you recognise a hazardous substance?

options.A: By the hazard pictograms and other warning information on its label and safety data sheet
options.C: It will be in a suitable container
options.D: The colour of the label on the container

questions.explanation: Hazardous chemicals are identified from their classified label information, including pictograms, signal words and hazard statements, supported by the safety data sheet. Smell, container appearance or label colour alone is not a reliable test.

A.text: Hazardous chemicals are identified from their classified label information, including pictograms, signal words and hazard statements, supported by the safety data sheet. Smell, container appearance or label colour alone is not a reliable test.

B.text: Odour is subjective, may be absent and can occur only above a harmful exposure concentration.

C.text: Safe packaging does not mean the contents are harmless; hazardous substances should also be stored in suitable containers.

D.text: Label background colour is not the classification system; pictograms, signal words and hazard statements carry the warning.

questions.prompt: If you have been handling lead, how is it most likely to get into your blood stream?

options.A: By not reporting the matter to the HSE
options.B: By not using the correct safety footwear
options.C: By not washing your hands before eating

questions.explanation: The route into the body is ingestion, normally from lead contamination on the hands.

A.text: Failure to notify HSE does not itself put lead into the bloodstream; exposure occurs through physical routes into the body.

B.text: Safety footwear protects the feet but does not stop contaminated hands transferring lead to food or the mouth.

C.text: The route into the body is ingestion, normally from lead contamination on the hands.

D.text: Goggles protect the eyes; they do not control ingestion from eating with lead-contaminated hands.

questions.prompt: When using personal protective equipment (PPE) legally you must do which of the following?

options.A: Clean it properly once a week
options.B: Not interfere with it or misuse it
options.C: Replace it at your own expense if it is damaged
options.D: Return it to the manufacturer when damaged

questions.explanation: Interfering with or misusing items provided in the interests of health, safety or welfare is an offence under the HSW Act 1974 (section 8)

questions.prompt: How can you protect your eyesight while working on site?

options.A: By not looking directly at what you are doing
options.D: By wearing the correct type of eye protection

questions.explanation: Eyes are vulnerable to flying debris, dust, splashes and arc flash, and once damaged the harm is often irreversible. Correctly specified eye protection matched to the hazard is the only reliable safeguard, whereas avoiding looking or squinting offers no physical barrier at all.

A.text: Looking away makes accurate work harder and provides no physical barrier against dust, fragments or splashes.

B.text: Squinting cannot stop a high-speed particle or chemical splash from reaching and damaging the eye.

C.text: Ordinary sunglasses lack the impact rating and side protection required for typical construction hazards.

D.text: Eyes are vulnerable to flying debris, dust, splashes and arc flash, and once damaged the harm is often irreversible. Correctly specified eye protection matched to the hazard is the only reliable safeguard, whereas avoiding looking or squinting offers no physical barrier at all.

questions.prompt: Why should a high visibility vest be worn when working on roads?

options.A: Because it will keep you warm
options.B: Because you were told to do so
options.C: So road users and plant operators can see you
options.D: So that your mates can see you

questions.explanation: Roadworks expose workers to moving traffic and site plant whose operators have restricted visibility. High-visibility clothing makes the wearer conspicuous to both drivers and machine operators, giving them time to react and reducing the risk of being struck.

A.text: A high-visibility vest is not thermal clothing and may provide little insulation in cold conditions.

B.text: Following an instruction is required, but it does not explain the road-traffic hazard that the garment controls.

C.text: Roadworks expose workers to moving traffic and site plant whose operators have restricted visibility. High-visibility clothing makes the wearer conspicuous to both drivers and machine operators, giving them time to react and reducing the risk of being struck.

D.text: Colleague recognition is secondary; the critical need is early detection by approaching drivers and mobile-plant operators.

questions.prompt: Which of the following must your safety helmet comply with to meet with the requirements of the Personal Protective Equipment at Work Regulations?

options.A: It can be adjusted to suit your head size
options.B: It has a label with your name on it
options.C: It is a good visible colour
options.D: It is less than 1 year old

questions.explanation: An assessment of the suitability of head protection would include consideration of whether it can be adjusted to suit the individual who is to wear it, that it is compatible with the work to be done and that it is comfortable to wear.

A.text: An assessment of the suitability of head protection would include consideration of whether it can be adjusted to suit the individual who is to wear it, that it is compatible with the work to be done and that it is comfortable to wear.

B.text: A name label assists identification but contributes no impact protection, fit or compatibility with the user's head.

C.text: Visibility may be useful for some tasks, but colour alone does not make a helmet fit and remain secure on its wearer.

D.text: Being less than a year old cannot compensate for poor fit, damage or use contrary to the manufacturer's instructions.

questions.prompt: Under which of the following circumstances should an accident be recorded in the site's accident book?

options.A: Only when a person is injured and will be off work for more than seven days
options.B: When an accident causes damage to plant or equipment
options.C: When an accident causes injury to an employee while at work
options.D: When the injury is serious enough for first aid to be needed.

questions.explanation: An accident causing an injury to an employee at work should be recorded in the accident book (BI 510).

A.text: Seven-day incapacity is a separate RIDDOR reporting threshold and is not the threshold for an accident-book entry.

B.text: Plant damage without personal injury belongs in maintenance or incident records, not necessarily the statutory accident book.

C.text: An accident causing an injury to an employee at work should be recorded in the accident book (BI 510).

D.text: The recording duty is not triggered only when first aid is needed; even a minor work injury should be recorded.

questions.prompt: What must an employer do with their accident records following completion of a construction project?

options.A: They are destroyed on site with other non-essential documents
options.B: They are kept safe by the employer
options.C: They are sent to the employer's insurance company
options.D: They are sent to the Health and Safety Executive

questions.explanation: Accident records must be kept by an employer for at least three years.

A.text: Project completion does not end the retention requirement, so the records must not be destroyed with temporary paperwork.

B.text: Accident records must be kept by an employer for at least three years.

C.text: An insurer may receive relevant information for a claim, but sending it does not replace the employer's duty to retain the record.

D.text: The employer keeps the underlying records; only reportable events are notified to the enforcing authority through RIDDOR.

questions.prompt: When picking up an object, you should:

options.C: Adopt a stable stance, keep the load close and use a slight bend of the back, hips and knees without further flexing the back while lifting

questions.explanation: Current HSE guidance does not prescribe a deep squat or simply say 'bend your knees'. Use a stable position, secure hold and slight bend at the back, hips and knees, keep the load close and move smoothly without twisting or further back flexion.

A.text: Arm position alone does not stabilise the body or control back loading, grip, load distance and twisting.

B.text: Deliberately bending through the back while lifting increases spinal loading and loss of control.

C.text: Current HSE guidance does not prescribe a deep squat or simply say 'bend your knees'. Use a stable position, secure hold and slight bend at the back, hips and knees, keep the load close and move smoothly without twisting or further back flexion.

D.text: A back brace is not a substitute for avoiding hazardous handling, assessing the task and using sound movement.

questions.prompt: When an article has to be moved for a long distance, you should:

options.C: Get someone else to do it for you

questions.explanation: Manual handling regulations require loads to be moved in ways that reduce strain and injury risk. Using a barrow or trolley transfers the weight to wheels, cutting the muscular effort and cumulative strain of carrying or dragging something over a long distance.

A.text: Carrying for the whole route increases fatigue and cumulative strain when wheeled assistance is available.

B.text: Dragging requires sustained force, can damage the load and gives poor control over obstacles and slopes.

C.text: Passing an avoidable risk to another person does not control it; suitable handling equipment should be used.

D.text: Manual handling regulations require loads to be moved in ways that reduce strain and injury risk. Using a barrow or trolley transfers the weight to wheels, cutting the muscular effort and cumulative strain of carrying or dragging something over a long distance.

questions.prompt: Under RIDDOR, which one of the following must be reported to the enforcing authority?

options.A: Accidents where the injured person wishes to make a claim
options.B: All 'near misses' even if no one is hurt
options.D: Fracture other than to fingers, thumbs or toes

questions.explanation: This is one of a number of reportable 'specified injuries' and must be reported to the enforcing authority under the Reporting of Injuries, Diseases and Dangerous Occurrences Regulations (RIDDOR).

A.text: A possible civil claim does not determine RIDDOR status; the event and injury category do.

B.text: Near misses are valuable internally, but only listed dangerous occurrences require notification when nobody is hurt.

C.text: Minor injuries belong in workplace records but are not all reportable to the enforcing authority.

D.text: This is one of a number of reportable 'specified injuries' and must be reported to the enforcing authority under the Reporting of Injuries, Diseases and Dangerous Occurrences Regulations (RIDDOR).

questions.prompt: What does UK manual-handling law say about a single maximum weight that an individual may lift?

options.A: 15kg provided that it is a compact load
options.B: 35kg provided that it has no sharp edges
options.C: There is no single legal maximum; the task, load, environment and individual's capability must be assessed

questions.explanation: The law does not set one maximum lifting weight. Employers must avoid hazardous manual handling where reasonably practicable, assess unavoidable operations and reduce risk, taking account of the whole task and the individual rather than treating comfort as a safe limit.

A.text: Fifteen kilograms is not a universal legal ceiling; posture, frequency, grip and individual capability can change the risk.

B.text: Removing sharp edges does not make 35 kg universally acceptable, and the Regulations set no single maximum weight.

C.text: The law does not set one maximum lifting weight. Employers must avoid hazardous manual handling where reasonably practicable, assess unavoidable operations and reduce risk, taking account of the whole task and the individual rather than treating comfort as a safe limit.

D.text: A supervisor's instruction cannot override the duty to avoid, assess and reduce hazardous manual handling.

questions.prompt: If moving a load may cause injury, what should you do before proceeding?

options.A: Stop and tell the supervisor or responsible person so the operation can be avoided where possible or properly assessed and controlled
options.D: Getting someone to assist you over the distance

questions.explanation: The correct response is not simply to carry, drag or recruit someone informally. Hazardous handling should first be avoided where reasonably practicable; otherwise the task needs assessment and controls such as redesign, an aid or a planned team lift.

A.text: The correct response is not simply to carry, drag or recruit someone informally. Hazardous handling should first be avoided where reasonably practicable; otherwise the task needs assessment and controls such as redesign, an aid or a planned team lift.

B.text: Proceeding despite a known injury risk bypasses both the duty to avoid the handling and the need for assessment.

C.text: Dragging can add high force, poor posture and damage and is not automatically safer than carrying.

D.text: Informally adding a helper can create coordination hazards; a team lift must follow an assessed plan where appropriate.

questions.prompt: The Health and Safety (Safety Signs and Signals) Regulations require the colour coding of safety signs. What colours are used on a sign indicating a mandatory activity, for example "Safety helmets must be worn"?
questions.explanation: The Safety Signs and Signals Regulations use a fixed colour code so signs are understood at a glance. Mandatory signs, which instruct a required action such as wearing a helmet, are shown as a blue circle with a white symbol.

A.text: The Safety Signs and Signals Regulations use a fixed colour code so signs are understood at a glance. Mandatory signs, which instruct a required action such as wearing a helmet, are shown as a blue circle with a white symbol.

B.text: Green and white marks safe conditions and emergency facilities, not an instruction that must be followed.

C.text: Red, black and white prohibits an activity; it is not used for a positive helmet-wearing command.

D.text: Yellow and black warns of a hazard but does not prescribe the action that the viewer must take.

questions.prompt: Under the Health and Safety at Work Act 1974, which of the following have a duty to work safely?
questions.explanation: Employers, employees and the self-employed all have duties to work safely under the Act.

A.text: Employers, employees and the self-employed all have duties to work safely under the Act.

B.text: Employees have duties, but employers and self-employed people also must conduct work without endangering others.

C.text: Employers carry overarching duties, yet workers must also take reasonable care and cooperate with controls.

D.text: Members of the public are protected by work duties, but the question asks who at work carries a duty to work safely.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: All employees must take reasonable care, not only to protect themselves but also their colleagues
options.B: Employees have no responsibility for Health and Safety on site
options.C: Only the client is responsible for safety on site
options.D: The duty for health and safety falls only on the employer

questions.explanation: This is a legal requirement under Section 7 of the Health & Safety at Work Act.

A.text: This is a legal requirement under Section 7 of the Health & Safety at Work Act.

B.text: Employees have a statutory duty to take reasonable care and cooperate with safety arrangements.

C.text: The client has important CDM duties, but employers, contractors and workers retain their own responsibilities.

D.text: Employers carry primary management duties, while employees still owe duties to themselves and people affected by their acts.

questions.prompt: What is a HAZARD?

options.B: Something with the potential to cause harm
options.C: The likelihood of something going wrong
options.D: Where an accident is likely to happen

questions.explanation: Examples of hazards include: a drum of acid, breeze blocks on an elevated plank; cables running across a floor.

A.text: The phrase predicts an event but does not identify the thing or condition that has potential to cause harm.

B.text: Examples of hazards include: a drum of acid, breeze blocks on an elevated plank; cables running across a floor.

C.text: Likelihood is part of risk; a hazard exists because it can cause harm regardless of how likely exposure is.

D.text: A place can contain hazards, but location alone is not the definition of the harmful agent or condition.

questions.prompt: A Health and Safety Executive Inspector can?

options.A: Only visit if accompanied by the principal contractor
options.B: Only visit if they have made an appointment
options.C: Only visit to interview the site manager
options.D: Enter premises at any reasonable time, or at any time when the inspector believes a dangerous situation exists

questions.explanation: HSWA section 20 empowers an appointed inspector to enter at any reasonable time, and at any time where the inspector has reasonable cause to believe a dangerous situation exists. 'Visit at any time' without that qualification overstated the ordinary power.

A.text: The inspector's statutory entry power does not depend on the principal contractor accompanying the visit.

B.text: Requiring an appointment would allow dangerous conditions to be hidden and is not a condition in section 20.

C.text: Inspectors may examine premises, evidence, articles and people; their power is not limited to one manager interview.

D.text: HSWA section 20 empowers an appointed inspector to enter at any reasonable time, and at any time where the inspector has reasonable cause to believe a dangerous situation exists. 'Visit at any time' without that qualification overstated the ordinary power.

questions.prompt: Employers have to produce a written Health and Safety Policy statement when:

options.D: They employ five people or more

questions.explanation: This is a specific requirement of the Health and Safety at Work Act.

A.text: Starting a contract does not set the written-policy threshold; it depends on the employer's workforce size.

B.text: The duty arises automatically from law and does not wait for an HSE notification.

C.text: A safety representative may request information, but their request is not what creates the statutory requirement.

D.text: This is a specific requirement of the Health and Safety at Work Act.

questions.prompt: What are fire-stops designed to do?

options.B: Delay the passage of fire and smoke through openings in walls and floors
options.D: Protect services (such as wiring systems) against fire damage

questions.explanation: Fire-stops are designed to maintain the fireproofing of a wall or floor assembly. Fire-stopping delays the spread of fire and, generally, the spread of smoke as well.

A.text: Door closers act on fire doors; fire-stops seal gaps and service penetrations in compartment boundaries.

B.text: Fire-stops are designed to maintain the fireproofing of a wall or floor assembly. Fire-stopping delays the spread of fire and, generally, the spread of smoke as well.

C.text: Fire-stopping contains fire and smoke but does not extinguish the burning material or replace firefighting equipment.

D.text: The main purpose is to maintain compartmentation, not to shield the cable or pipe itself from heat damage.

questions.prompt: What should you do if you disturb fire-stopping around a wiring system penetrating a wall or floor whilst carrying out work?

options.A: Ensure that the fire-stopping is reinstated to the necessary standard as soon as possible
options.B: Fill any holes or gaps with squashed paper
options.D: Nail a piece of wood over any gaps

questions.explanation: It is essential that the integrity of fire compartments is maintained during the construction of buildings and on their completion. Compromising compartmentation, such as failing to adequately fire-stop (seal) openings for services to pass through, can undermine fire precautions catastrophically. Only a limited range of products are suitable and they must be correctly applied to provide the required degree of fire-stopping.

A.text: It is essential that the integrity of fire compartments is maintained during the construction of buildings and on their completion. Compromising compartmentation, such as failing to adequately fire-stop (seal) openings for services to pass through, can undermine fire precautions catastrophically. Only a limited range of products are suitable and they must be correctly applied to provide the required degree of fire-stopping.

B.text: Paper is combustible, untested and easily displaced, so it cannot restore the required fire resistance.

C.text: Recording the damage does not close the penetration or protect occupants while the breach remains open.

D.text: A nailed board leaves untested joints and may itself be combustible; it is not a compliant penetration seal.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is NOT best practice from a sustainability point of view?

options.A: Looking after the people working on or near the site
options.C: Saving materials, fuel, water and energy
options.D: Sending unused and waste copper cables to landfill

questions.explanation: Option D) would be wasting a valuable natural resource (copper) that could be effectively recovered for later use or recycling. Reusing or recycling copper has less environmental impact than mining and extracting new copper reserves.

A.text: Protecting workers and neighbours is part of the social element of sustainable construction.

B.text: Preventing pollution and ecological damage preserves resources for current and future users.

C.text: Reducing material, fuel, water and energy use cuts both resource depletion and avoidable emissions.

D.text: Option D) would be wasting a valuable natural resource (copper) that could be effectively recovered for later use or recycling. Reusing or recycling copper has less environmental impact than mining and extracting new copper reserves.

questions.prompt: Do individuals have any responsibility for minimising the amount of waste created on site?

options.A: No, it's the responsibility of the client
options.B: Only during site clean-up, at the end of the project
options.C: Only if asbestos removal is being carried out
options.D: Yes, everyone on site has this responsibility

questions.explanation: Your actions will help your company, and others on site, to procure sensibly and to organise the job so that materials and substances are not wasted. Waste reduction is the best option when trying to manage site waste.

A.text: The client influences procurement, but every worker can prevent damage, use only what is needed and sort remaining waste.

B.text: Waste is best prevented throughout delivery and installation; end-of-project clean-up is too late to recover wasted material.

C.text: Waste minimisation applies to ordinary packaging, off-cuts and surplus as well as specially controlled asbestos waste.

D.text: Your actions will help your company, and others on site, to procure sensibly and to organise the job so that materials and substances are not wasted. Waste reduction is the best option when trying to manage site waste.

questions.prompt: Optical fibre cable remnants should not be left lying around on site because:

options.A: Laser beams still exist in the cut pieces
options.C: They can be hot and burn upon contact
options.D: They can pierce the skin or eyes

questions.explanation: Fibre fragments can enter the bloodstream and cause infections in the skin or eyes. All fibre waste, particularly small pieces, should be placed in suitable receptacles.

D.text: Fibre fragments can enter the bloodstream and cause infections in the skin or eyes. All fibre waste, particularly small pieces, should be placed in suitable receptacles.

questions.prompt: Which of the following should be disposed of as hazardous/special waste?
questions.explanation: Hazardous wastes (special wastes in Scotland) are specified in waste legislation. Aerosol sealants are included because they can explode if not recovered or disposed of properly, and they may still contain hazardous solvents.

A.text: Hazardous wastes (special wastes in Scotland) are specified in waste legislation. Aerosol sealants are included because they can explode if not recovered or disposed of properly, and they may still contain hazardous solvents.

B.text: Uncontaminated glass-fibre off-cuts are not automatically hazardous waste, though dust still needs exposure control.

C.text: Ordinary untreated timber sheet off-cuts can normally follow a segregated wood-recovery route rather than hazardous disposal.

D.text: A nuisance-dust mask is not automatically hazardous unless it is contaminated by a substance that changes its classification.

questions.prompt: A portable electric generator on site has two power outlets, 110 volts and 230 volts. What colour would the 110 volt outlet be?
questions.explanation: Yellow is the usual colour of cables, socket outlets, plugs and transformers etc which are used with a 110 volt supply.

D.text: Yellow is the usual colour of cables, socket outlets, plugs and transformers etc which are used with a 110 volt supply.

questions.prompt: Which listed value is the conventional upper boundary of extra-low voltage for AC and the level above which HSE warns that contact can cause shock injury?
questions.explanation: Fifty volts AC is a conventional voltage boundary used in electrical-safety measures; it is not a guaranteed safe body-withstand voltage. Shock outcome also depends on current path, duration, skin condition, environment and other factors, and HSE warns that contact above about 50 V AC can injure.

A.text: One hundred and ten volts exceeds the conventional extra-low-voltage boundary even when centre-tapped site supplies reduce voltage to earth.

Shock outcome also depends on current path, duration, skin condition, environment and other factors, and HSE warns that contact above about 50 V AC can injure.

questions.prompt: Which of the following statements is true with regard to the dangers of electricity?

options.A: Electricity is dangerous at any time because you cannot tell by looking at a cable whether or not it is live
options.B: Electricity is only dangerous if you are not wearing wellington boots
options.C: Electricity is only dangerous in wet weather
options.D: Electricity is perfectly safe so long as you wear cotton gloves

questions.explanation: The features which make electricity so dangerous are that you cannot see, hear or smell it. It can give you a very unpleasant surprise. Always assume that cables are live.

B.text: Wellington boots are not a universal electrical safeguard and may be wet, damaged or unsuitable for the voltage.

C.text: Dry weather does not prove a conductor dead or remove the possibility of a fatal current path.

D.text: Cotton gloves have no electrical insulating rating and do not make contact with energised parts safe.

questions.prompt: Which of the following does the Electricity at Work (EAW) regulations apply to?

options.A: All persons engaged for work purposes

questions.explanation: The EAW Regulations impose duties on employers, employees and the self employed.

A.text: The EAW Regulations impose duties on employers, employees and the self employed.

B.text: The Regulations also impose duties beyond employees, including on employers and self-employed people at work.

C.text: Employers carry major duties, but employees and self-employed people also have obligations under the Regulations.

D.text: Self-employed people are covered, but limiting the scope to them excludes employees and employers who are also covered.

questions.prompt: The lowest level of electrical current which can harm the human body is normally measured in:
questions.explanation: Research has shown that a person is in serious danger of a fatal electric shock at, or above, approximately 30 milliamps.

A.text: Whole amperes are far above the range where shock can already disrupt breathing or heart rhythm.

B.text: Kiloamperes describe fault-current magnitudes, not the small body current capable of causing physiological injury.

C.text: Microamperes are one-thousandth of a milliampere and are generally below the ordinary harmful-shock thresholds discussed.

D.text: Research has shown that a person is in serious danger of a fatal electric shock at, or above, approximately 30 milliamps.

questions.prompt: What must be considered first when planning to carry out work in a confined space?

options.A: Can the work be done from the outside
options.C: Has the job been priced properly
options.D: Have the correct tools been arranged

questions.explanation: Working outside will remove the risks of working in the confined space.

C.text: Commercial pricing cannot determine whether a worker should be exposed to a dangerous enclosed atmosphere.

D.text: Tool selection follows the safe method; arranging tools first assumes entry before avoidance has been considered.

questions.prompt: Before entering an excavation to start work, it must first be:
questions.explanation: Excavation work is hazardous. A competent person, knowledgeable about how to reduce risks, notably from collapse of the walls, must inspect the excavation first.

A.text: Covering and waiting does not establish that the sides, access, atmosphere or buried services are safe.

B.text: Flooding an excavation adds instability and drowning risk and is not a substitute for competent inspection.

questions.prompt: You are asked to enter a manhole where a toxic or oxygen-deficient atmosphere may be present, but no assessed safe system or suitable respiratory protection has been provided. What should you do?

options.A: Just get on with the job, and accept the risks
options.B: Look into the manhole to see if you can see any harmful gases
options.C: Sniff the atmosphere in the manhole to see if you can smell harmful gases
options.D: Do not enter; report it so entry can be avoided or a competent risk-assessed system, atmosphere controls, training and rescue arrangements can be put in place

questions.explanation: Confined-space entry should be avoided where possible. questions.prompt: What is the preferred nominal voltage for portable hand lamps for general use on construction sites?

questions.prompt: When using an extension cable reel, which of the following statements is correct?

options.A: Do not exceed the reeled or unreeled rating as appropriate
options.B: Leave as much as possible coiled up on the reel

questions.prompt: What hazard is created when the head of a cold chisel 'mushrooms'?

questions.prompt: The power hand tool you are about to use has burn marks visible on the cable. What should you do?

questions.prompt: When working above public areas, what should be considered?

questions.prompt: If work at height cannot be avoided and collective fall-prevention equipment is not reasonably practicable, which listed approach is required before the work proceeds?

options.A: Use a properly selected work-restraint or fall-arrest system connected to a suitable anchor, with competent users and planned rescue arrangements
options.B: Work without fall protection at all times when no one else is about
options.C: Work without fall protection, provided the weather is not too windy

questions.explanation: Personal fall protection comes below collective prevention in the work-at-height hierarchy. A harness alone is not protection: the system, lanyard and anchorage must suit the task, users must be competent, and foreseeable rescue must be planned.

questions.prompt: Once the casualty is away from the hot metal and there is no immediate life-threatening danger, what should you do first for the hand burn?

questions.prompt: After checking that approaching the casualty will not expose you or them to immediate danger, what should you do first on finding an injured person on site?

questions.prompt: Modern portable fire extinguishers are predominantly red. How is the extinguishing medium additionally identified?

questions.prompt: When discharging carbon dioxide fire extinguishers, the nozzle:

questions.prompt: The effects of damage to your hearing by long-term exposure to high noise levels:

questions.prompt: Which of the following would not reduce the risks from hand-arm vibration when using a hammer-action tool?

questions.prompt: If there is a risk of injury from lifting loads what should you think about first?

questions.prompt: In a health and safety risk assessment, what does the term risk describe?

questions.prompt: Complete the following sentence: A risk assessment

options.B: Is a piece of paper required by law

questions.explanation: Risk assessment involves a careful review of what can cause harm and the practical measures to be taken to reduce the risk of harm.

questions.prompt: What is an "Improvement Notice"?

questions.prompt: Who needs to understand relevant environmental risks on a construction site?

questions.prompt: From an environmental point of view, why should materials be reused, where possible?

questions.prompt: How should you get rid of hazardous/special waste?

questions.prompt: A residual current device is designed to operate in the event of one of the following:

questions.prompt: The normal procedure for working on electrical equipment should be which one of the following?

questions.prompt: Which of the following would you use to replace the fuse in a plug if fuses were NOT available?
questions.explanation: A fuse is often the main safety device in an electrical circuit. A blown fuse must only be replaced by a fuse of the correct type and rating.

questions.prompt: Under Regulation 14 of the Electricity at Work Regulations 1989, when may work on or near a live conductor that may give rise to danger proceed?

options.C: When the person carrying out the work is a competent person
options.D: When the person working on the equipment is wearing rubber gloves

questions.explanation: All three Regulation 14 conditions must be satisfied. Live work must be justified because making dead is unreasonable, carrying it out live must itself be reasonable, and suitable precautions, including suitable protective equipment where necessary, must prevent injury.

A.text: All three Regulation 14 conditions must be satisfied. Live work must be justified because making dead is unreasonable, carrying it out live must itself be reasonable, and suitable precautions, including suitable protective equipment where necessary, must prevent injury.

questions.prompt: A Cable Avoidance Tool (C.A.T.) and a 'Genny' (generator) can be used successfully to locate underground cables by whom:

questions.prompt: You have to walk across a site several times a day, but have to dodge a lot of site traffic. The first thing you should do is:

questions.prompt: What is the preferred nominal voltage for local lighting up to 2 kW on construction sites?

questions.prompt: To operate a powered hand tool you must be:

questions.prompt: What is the best method of securing a ladder?

questions.prompt: What must you do when work equipment is found damaged?

options.C: Take it out of use and report the defect to your supervisor or other responsible person

questions.prompt: What precaution should you take before adjusting an electrical tool?

questions.prompt: Ladders should not be painted because:

questions.prompt: How many people should be working on a ladder at one time?

questions.prompt: A labourer gets an electric shock; looks a bit pale but says they are alright. What should you do?

questions.prompt: Which listed statement best describes the role of personal protective equipment at work?

options.B: Personal protective equipment (PPE) need only be provided if it is not too expensive

A.text: Blue and white indicates a mandatory action, not a safe escape route.
