C.text: Red and white identifies fire-fighting equipment or prohibition features, not the direction of escape.

D.text: Red and yellow does not represent the standard safe-condition colour scheme for an emergency exit.

questions.prompt: Why should regular inspections of the workplace take place?

options.A: To check that all employees are present
options.B: To check that everyone is doing their job
options.C: To check whether the working environment is safe
options.D: To prepare for a visit from an HSE Inspector

questions.explanation: The Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations require that routine inspections of workplaces are carried out to ensure that preventative and protective measures are in place and effective.

A.text: Attendance is an administrative check and gives no assurance that access, guarding or housekeeping remains safe.

B.text: Performance supervision may be needed, but a workplace inspection looks for hazards and control failures, not productivity.

C.text: The Management of Health and Safety at Work Regulations require that routine inspections of workplaces are carried out to ensure that preventative and protective measures are in place and effective.

D.text: Inspections should find and correct risks routinely, rather than being cosmetic preparation for a regulator's visit.

questions.prompt: Which is the part of your body MOST LIKELY to be injured during a manual handling activity which involves moving a heavy load?
questions.explanation: Moving heavy loads tends to load the spine through bending and twisting, so the back bears the greatest strain and is most prone to injury. Sound technique keeps the load close, maintains a straight back and lifts using the powerful leg muscles.

A.text: Moving heavy loads tends to load the spine through bending and twisting, so the back bears the greatest strain and is most prone to injury. Sound technique keeps the load close, maintains a straight back and lifts using the powerful leg muscles.

B.text: Chest injury is possible in a crush event, but ordinary heavy handling most commonly overloads the back and supporting tissues.

C.text: Forearms can fatigue while gripping, yet the spine usually bears the greater injury risk from load leverage and twisting.

D.text: Knees can be stressed by poor posture, but back injury is the most common concern across heavy manual-handling tasks.

questions.prompt: What do the letters ACoP stand for?
questions.explanation: An ACOP is a code of practice approved by the Health and Safety Executive (or the Health and Safety Commission prior to April 2008).

A.text: The statutory term is Approved, not Accepted; an ACOP has a specific evidential status under health and safety law.

B.text: Neither 'Accepted' nor 'Provisions' forms the recognised title used for HSE-approved practical guidance.

C.text: An ACOP is a code of practice approved by the Health and Safety Executive (or the Health and Safety Commission prior to April 2008).

D.text: An ACOP is a Code of Practice, not a single approved condition attached to an activity.

questions.prompt: What is a HAZARD?

options.B: Something with the potential to cause harm
options.C: The likelihood of something going wrong
options.D: Where an accident is likely to happen

questions.explanation: Examples of hazards include: a drum of acid, breeze blocks on an elevated plank; cables running across a floor.

A.text: The phrase predicts an event but does not identify the thing or condition that has potential to cause harm.

B.text: Examples of hazards include: a drum of acid, breeze blocks on an elevated plank; cables running across a floor.

C.text: Likelihood is part of risk; a hazard exists because it can cause harm regardless of how likely exposure is.

D.text: A place can contain hazards, but location alone is not the definition of the harmful agent or condition.

questions.prompt: What happens when an HSE or local-authority inspector serves a prohibition notice that takes immediate effect?

options.A: The work can continue if adequate safety precautions are put in place
options.B: The work can continue, provided a risk assessment is carried out
options.C: The work in hand can be completed, but no new work started
options.D: The activity covered by the notice must cease immediately and must not resume until the matters giving rise to the risk have been remedied

questions.explanation: An immediate prohibition notice stops the specified activity because it involves an imminent risk of serious personal injury. A prohibition notice can instead be deferred to a stated time, so the original unqualified wording was too broad.

A.text: Only remedying the matters identified in the notice permits resumption; informal precautions do not authorise continued work.

B.text: A new risk assessment cannot postpone an immediate statutory stop or replace the required remedial action.

C.text: An immediate notice does not allow the current job to be finished before the prohibited activity ceases.

D.text: An immediate prohibition notice stops the specified activity because it involves an imminent risk of serious personal injury. A prohibition notice can instead be deferred to a stated time, so the original unqualified wording was too broad.

questions.prompt: Who should sign the statement of intent in a company's health and safety policy?

options.C: The employer or most senior person in the company

questions.explanation: HSE says the employer or most senior person should sign the policy statement and review it regularly. That may be the managing director in one company, but the role rather than a particular job title is the governing principle.

A.text: A safety officer may advise and administer the system, but the most senior leadership must own the statement of intent.

B.text: Company-secretary status does not necessarily carry executive control over the undertaking's health and safety commitments.

C.text: HSE says the employer or most senior person should sign the policy statement and review it regularly. That may be the managing director in one company, but the role rather than a particular job title is the governing principle.

D.text: A site manager controls a location but is not ordinarily the most senior person responsible for the company-wide policy.

questions.prompt: If you discover a hole or gap in a fire rated wall or floor that has not been fire-stopped, what should you do?

options.A: Cover the hole or gap with insulating tape
options.B: Ignore it unless it is causing a draught
options.C: Report it to your supervisor without delay
options.D: Use decorators' sealant to fill the gap

questions.explanation: Supervisors need to be made aware of any observed inadequacies in fire-stopping - which can undermine fire precautions catastrophically during the construction of buildings and on their completion. Only a limited range of products are suitable and they must be correctly applied to provide the required degree of fire-stopping.

A.text: Insulating tape has no tested fire-resistance rating and cannot reinstate a breached fire compartment.

B.text: A draught is irrelevant: any unsealed penetration can let smoke and flame bypass the fire-rated barrier.

C.text: Supervisors need to be made aware of any observed inadequacies in fire-stopping - which can undermine fire precautions catastrophically during the construction of buildings and on their completion. Only a limited range of products are suitable and they must be correctly applied to provide the required degree of fire-stopping.

D.text: Ordinary decorators' sealant is not a certified fire-stopping system matched to the wall or floor construction.

questions.prompt: What can help to prevent harm to the environment from oil spillages?

options.A: A supply of water to flush the spill away
options.C: Store oils in an area that can catch any spills, such as a bund or a drip tray.
options.D: Turning liquid containers upside down so the top can't come off

questions.explanation: The use of a bund (fully walled storage area) or a drip tray will help any spillage to be contained in a small area for clear up. Any spillage could get into the ground or drains, which is likely to be an offence under environmental legislation.

A.text: Flushing spreads oil into soil or drainage and turns a contained spill into a wider pollution incident.

B.text: Soil only hides and absorbs the contamination; the polluted material still requires controlled recovery and disposal.

C.text: The use of a bund (fully walled storage area) or a drip tray will help any spillage to be contained in a small area for clear up. Any spillage could get into the ground or drains, which is likely to be an offence under environmental legislation.

D.text: Inverting containers can damage closures and promote leakage rather than providing secondary containment.

questions.prompt: Which of the following should you do on site in the interest of sustainability?

options.B: Comply with site instructions on handling waste materials
options.C: Pour waste liquids down a drain off-site
options.D: Run plant and equipment when they are not needed

questions.explanation: Your actions will help your company, and others working on site, to achieve more sustainable work practices, such as waste recovery.

A.text: Burying waste evades authorised disposal and risks long-term contamination of land and groundwater.

B.text: Your actions will help your company, and others working on site, to achieve more sustainable work practices, such as waste recovery.

C.text: Moving off site does not make drain disposal lawful; liquids still need classification and an authorised waste route.

D.text: Unneeded running wastes fuel, creates emissions and adds noise and maintenance without productive work.

questions.prompt: Which of the following procedures should be used when more than one person will be working on circuits supplied from a distribution board which has been switched off?

options.A: Blowing a horn before the power is switched on again
options.B: Giving each operative a volt stick
options.C: Telling everyone what time the power will be switched on again
options.D: The use of a multi-lock hasp on the isolator with a padlock for each operative

questions.explanation: A multi-lock hasp can be used to prevent operation of the isolator until such time that all persons working on the electrical installation have completed their work and removed their padlocks from the hasp.

A.text: An audible warning relies on memory and hearing and gives no personal control over reconnection at the isolator.

B.text: A voltage stick cannot secure isolation or prevent another person from energising the distribution board.

C.text: An agreed time is not a lock-off; work may overrun and someone may reconnect without knowing who remains exposed.

D.text: A multi-lock hasp can be used to prevent operation of the isolator until such time that all persons working on the electrical installation have completed their work and removed their padlocks from the hasp.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is classed as hazardous/special waste?
questions.explanation: Hazardous wastes (special wastes in Scotland) are specified in waste legislation. Fluorescent tubes are included because of their mercury content.

A.text: Empty cement bags are normally a non-hazardous construction waste stream when uncontaminated and correctly segregated.

B.text: Hazardous wastes (special wastes in Scotland) are specified in waste legislation. Fluorescent tubes are included because of their mercury content.

C.text: Non-asbestos insulation is not automatically hazardous, although dust and product-specific controls may still be needed.

D.text: Clean polythene and shrink wrap are generally segregated for recycling rather than treated as hazardous waste.

questions.prompt: Electrical installations on construction sites should be periodically inspected and tested:
questions.explanation: Three monthly inspections of construction site installations are recommended in IEE Guidance Note 3.

A.text: Three monthly inspections of construction site installations are recommended in IEE Guidance Note 3.

B.text: Six months exceeds the commonly specified three-month construction-site interval for temporary installations.

C.text: Monthly inspection may be chosen for higher risk, but it is not the stated general periodic interval.

D.text: A yearly interval is too long for temporary systems exposed to frequent movement, weather and site damage.

questions.prompt: The probes of voltage detectors and test instruments used on electrical systems should be:

options.D: Shaped or have barriers to prevent finger contact with the tips

questions.explanation: In addition, to protect against damage by overcurrent whilst in use, the probes or instrument should incorporate suitable high breaking capacity (hbc) fuses with a low current rating (usually not exceeding 500 mA), or current-limiting resistors.

A.text: Calibration evidence concerns instrument accuracy; it does not stop a finger sliding onto an exposed probe tip.

B.text: Colour can help identification but provides no physical protection against touching conductive metal.

C.text: Country of manufacture does not determine probe safety; construction, ratings and exposed-tip protection do.

D.text: In addition, to protect against damage by overcurrent whilst in use, the probes or instrument should incorporate suitable high breaking capacity (hbc) fuses with a low current rating (usually not exceeding 500 mA), or current-limiting resistors.

questions.prompt: Under the Electricity at Work Regulations, live working is considered:

options.C: Only to be allowed in exceptional circumstances

questions.explanation: Extra controls must be employed, including training, supervision and use of suitable tools and protective equipment.

A.text: Live work is not freely acceptable; each task must satisfy the strict conditions in Regulation 14.

B.text: An absolute ban is also inaccurate because carefully justified live work is lawful in exceptional circumstances.

C.text: Extra controls must be employed, including training, supervision and use of suitable tools and protective equipment.

D.text: Normalising live work reverses the hierarchy: equipment should ordinarily be isolated and proved dead.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is not a requirement of low voltage safe isolation practice?

options.A: A caution notice should be applied at the point of isolation
options.B: Ensuring that the correct point of isolation is identified
options.C: The conductors are proved to be dead at the point of work
options.D: The person carrying out the work is issued with insulating gloves

questions.explanation: Safe isolation practice refers to dead working. The use of insulating gloves will generally only be applicable to live working.

A.text: A caution notice communicates the isolation and warns others not to operate the secured device.

B.text: Identifying the correct isolator prevents the wrong circuit being locked while the intended conductors remain live.

C.text: Proving dead at the work point confirms isolation has actually removed dangerous voltage from every relevant conductor.

D.text: Safe isolation practice refers to dead working. The use of insulating gloves will generally only be applicable to live working.

questions.prompt: Where mains voltage is used to supply portable equipment on a construction site, what additional protection is required?
questions.explanation: Reduced low voltage systems (e.g. 110 volt centre point earthed) are strongly preferred in such circumstances. Where only mains voltage (230 V) equipment is available, however, a 30 mA RCD will give additional protection against fatal electric shock.

A.text: A cable locator prevents excavation strikes and provides no automatic disconnection for a shock from portable equipment.

B.text: Reduced low voltage systems (e.g. 110 volt centre point earthed) are strongly preferred in such circumstances. Where only mains voltage (230 V) equipment is available, however, a 30 mA RCD will give additional protection against fatal electric shock.

C.text: A generator is a source, not additional personal shock protection for a 230 V portable appliance.

D.text: A step-down transformer would change the equipment voltage and cannot supply a tool designed solely for 230 V at its rated operation.

questions.prompt: To determine the safety of the atmosphere in an excavation, which of the following is essential

options.B: Only entering for a short period to enable a quick escape

questions.explanation: Use a suitable detector. Many dangerous gases have no smell, and cannot be seen. Workers can be overcome in seconds in dangerous atmospheres.

A.text: Toxic gases and oxygen deficiency are often invisible, so visual inspection cannot establish atmospheric safety.

B.text: A dangerous atmosphere can overcome a worker before a quick escape is possible, even during a short entry.

C.text: Smell is unreliable and the attempt exposes the worker; some lethal gases have no detectable odour.

D.text: Use a suitable detector. Many dangerous gases have no smell, and cannot be seen. Workers can be overcome in seconds in dangerous atmospheres.

questions.prompt: Why may young people be more at risk on site?

options.A: There is no requirement to provide PPE to young people
options.B: There is no specific legislation applying to them
options.C: They are inexperienced and may not recognize danger
options.D: They are usually left to work alone to gain experience

questions.explanation: Health and Safety guidance lists young people as often being 'at particular risk', due to their lack of practical experience.

A.text: Young workers have the same right to suitable PPE where risk remains; age does not remove the employer's duty.

B.text: Health and safety law includes specific protection for young people through assessment of their inexperience and maturity.

C.text: Health and Safety guidance lists young people as often being 'at particular risk', due to their lack of practical experience.

D.text: Leaving an inexperienced person alone would increase rather than explain or control their vulnerability.

questions.prompt: What action should you take if an electric drill cuts out while you are using it?

options.A: Put it back into the tool box
options.B: Remove it from use and tell your supervisor
options.D: Switch the power off and on

questions.explanation: A tool that cuts out unexpectedly may have a developing electrical or mechanical fault that could become dangerous if used again. Removing it from service and reporting it ensures it is inspected or repaired by a competent person before anyone is put at risk.

A.text: Returning a suspected faulty drill to storage leaves it available for another person to use without warning.

B.text: A tool that cuts out unexpectedly may have a developing electrical or mechanical fault that could become dangerous if used again. Removing it from service and reporting it ensures it is inspected or repaired by a competent person before anyone is put at risk.

C.text: Shaking the tool can worsen loose electrical or mechanical parts and provides no competent diagnosis.

D.text: Repeated switching may re-energise a fault and expose the user to shock, heat or unexpected movement.

questions.prompt: If an electric drill gives off blue smoke from the motor, you should:

options.C: Switch it off and report it

questions.explanation: Defective electric hand tools must not be used. Stop what you are doing and inform your supervisor.

A.text: Water on energised equipment creates a shock path and may spread an electrical fire or damage adjacent equipment.

B.text: Cooling time does not diagnose insulation or motor failure and cannot make a smoking drill safe to restart.

C.text: Defective electric hand tools must not be used. Stop what you are doing and inform your supervisor.

D.text: An extinguisher is for an established fire; smoke from a running motor first requires isolation and defect reporting.

questions.prompt: Why may a confined space be dangerous to work in?

options.A: Air in the space may be unbreathable due to poisonous gas
options.C: Temperature and poor ventilation may affect the worker
options.D: There may not be sufficient working space

questions.explanation: There can be a range of hazards associated with confined spaces, and these can include all of those mentioned

A.text: A poisonous or oxygen-deficient atmosphere is one confined-space hazard, but heat, access and restricted movement also matter.

B.text: There can be a range of hazards associated with confined spaces, and these can include all of those mentioned

C.text: Temperature and ventilation are important, but this choice omits atmospheric toxicity and restricted working space.

D.text: Restricted space can hamper work and rescue, but it does not capture the separate atmospheric and thermal dangers.

questions.prompt: Of the following, which is the poorest method of securing a ladder?

options.B: Securing the base of the ladder

questions.explanation: Footing a ladder is the last resort and should be avoided. Other more suitable access equipment should be used where practicable.

A.text: Footing a ladder is the last resort and should be avoided. Other more suitable access equipment should be used where practicable.

B.text: Securing the base is a physical restraint and is more reliable than depending on another person's attention and strength.

C.text: Tying the ladder near the top provides positive restraint and is preferred where a suitable point is available.

D.text: A suitable stability device controls movement mechanically and is preferable to relying on a person footing it.

questions.prompt: What do the letters SWL stand for?
questions.explanation: Machinery and accessories for lifting loads should be clearly marked to indicate their safe working loads.

A.text: SWL marks a permissible load, not a working height or level from which equipment may be used.

B.text: Machinery and accessories for lifting loads should be clearly marked to indicate their safe working loads.

C.text: The recognised term uses 'safe working', not 'satisfactory weight', because it defines an equipment loading limit.

D.text: 'Satisfactory working limit' is not the standard expansion shown on lifting equipment and accessories.

questions.prompt: Hand and power tools must be:

options.C: Suitable for the task and regularly inspected
options.D: The best that you can buy

questions.explanation: Tools must not create a risk to the user or others. This means they must be suitable and kept in good condition. This requires inspection before use.

A.text: Corporate colour has no bearing on guarding, electrical integrity or suitability for the material and operation.

B.text: Availability helps scheduling but cannot justify using an unsuitable, damaged or unmaintained tool.

C.text: Tools must not create a risk to the user or others. This means they must be suitable and kept in good condition. This requires inspection before use.

D.text: Price or marketing quality does not replace task suitability, correct safety features and maintained condition.

questions.prompt: When can you work from a ladder?

options.A: For short periods and then only if it is safe to do so
options.D: When not being used for access

questions.explanation: Ladders are primarily means of access, not workplaces. They can be worked from, but only if the use of other, more suitable, work equipment is not appropriate and the task is of low risk and of short duration.

A.text: Ladders are primarily means of access, not workplaces. They can be worked from, but only if the use of other, more suitable, work equipment is not appropriate and the task is of low risk and of short duration.

B.text: Availability is not a risk assessment; a safer platform may be required even when a ladder is close at hand.

C.text: Sufficient length addresses reach only and says nothing about duration, task risk, stability or maintaining handhold.

D.text: A ladder used as access does not become a suitable workplace merely when nobody is climbing through it.

questions.prompt: On a mobile elevating work platform, what should you attach your safety harness to?

options.B: A secure anchorage point inside the platform
options.C: A strong part of the structure you are working on

questions.explanation: The priority is to stay within the platform (which is the safest place), and in any event you cannot be sure of the strength of other fixtures.

A.text: A nearby pipe or scaffold is outside the platform, may be weak and can create ejection or crushing during movement.

B.text: The priority is to stay within the platform (which is the safest place), and in any event you cannot be sure of the strength of other fixtures.

C.text: Clipping to the work structure defeats the platform's movement and can pull the worker from the basket.

D.text: The boom is not automatically a designated anchor and may expose the lanyard to moving or trapping points.

questions.prompt: In an emergency situation at work you should do what?

options.A: Ensure your work mates are all accounted for

questions.explanation: A site emergency plan should have been drawn up and you should be familiar with the emergency procedure.

A.text: Accounting for colleagues is a designated marshal's function within the plan, not a reason to delay following the procedure.

B.text: Leaving by an unplanned route may enter the hazard area and prevents an accurate roll call at the assembly point.

C.text: A site emergency plan should have been drawn up and you should be familiar with the emergency procedure.

D.text: HSE is not the site's emergency-response service; calling it does not replace alarm, evacuation and emergency contacts.

questions.prompt: Most deaths on site are caused by:
questions.explanation: Although the other dangers can kill or cause injury, falling from height is the bigger cause of fatalities.

A.text: Chemical burns cause serious harm but account for a smaller share of construction fatalities than falls from height.

B.text: Although the other dangers can kill or cause injury, falling from height is the bigger cause of fatalities.

C.text: Solvent inhalation is a controlled health risk, not the leading immediate fatal-accident category on sites.

D.text: Vehicle movements kill workers, but current construction statistics still show falls from height as the largest category.

questions.prompt: Ladders should be:

options.D: Tied or footed AND at the right angle AND in good condition

questions.explanation: All the measures listed are required to reduce the risk of falls.

A.text: The correct angle is necessary but cannot compensate for damaged rungs or an unsecured ladder.

B.text: Good condition is essential but does not stop a sound ladder sliding when set badly or left unsecured.

C.text: Securing controls movement, but the ladder must also be sound and placed at the correct angle.

D.text: All the measures listed are required to reduce the risk of falls.

questions.prompt: How often should a first-aider qualified in First Aid at Work (FAW) or Emergency First Aid at Work (EFAW) receive retraining?
questions.explanation: First Aid at Work (FAW) and Emergency First Aid at Work (EFAW) certificates are valid for three years and first-aiders are required to undertake retraining at the end of this period. However, the HSE also strongly recommends that first-aiders undertake annual (half-day) refresher training.

A.text: Four years exceeds the three-year validity period of an FAW or EFAW certificate, leaving a gap in qualification.

B.text: Six months is not the certificate-renewal interval; HSE separately recommends shorter annual refresher practice.

C.text: First Aid at Work (FAW) and Emergency First Aid at Work (EFAW) certificates are valid for three years and first-aiders are required to undertake retraining at the end of this period. However, the HSE also strongly recommends that first-aiders undertake annual (half-day) refresher training.

D.text: Two-year retraining may be chosen voluntarily, but it is not the standard three-year certificate cycle asked for.

questions.prompt: After confirming it is safe to approach an unresponsive person, what should you do when they are not breathing normally?

options.B: Call 999 or send someone to call and fetch an AED, then start CPR immediately and follow the call handler's instructions
options.C: Try to give the casualty a drink
options.D: Try to start the casualty breathing

questions.explanation: An unresponsive person who is not breathing normally may be in cardiac arrest. Activate emergency help and obtain an AED without avoidable delay, then begin CPR; broken bones and drinks are not the immediate priority.

A.text: Broken bones are secondary to absent normal breathing; circulation and oxygenation require immediate action.

B.text: An unresponsive person who is not breathing normally may be in cardiac arrest. Activate emergency help and obtain an AED without avoidable delay, then begin CPR; broken bones and drinks are not the immediate priority.

C.text: An unresponsive person can aspirate fluid and must never be given a drink.

D.text: Starting breathing is part of CPR, but calling emergency services and obtaining an AED must happen without avoidable delay.

questions.prompt: Your workmate suddenly gets a foreign body in the eye. What should you do?

options.B: Take your workmate to the supervisor
options.C: Use a clean handkerchief to try and remove it
options.D: Wash your hands before touching your mate's face

questions.explanation: Trying to remove a foreign body from the eye yourself can scratch the cornea or push the object deeper, causing lasting damage. A trained first-aider can treat it correctly or arrange proper medical care, so the safest action is to fetch them.

A.text: Trying to remove a foreign body from the eye yourself can scratch the cornea or push the object deeper, causing lasting damage. A trained first-aider can treat it correctly or arrange proper medical care, so the safest action is to fetch them.

B.text: A supervisor is not necessarily trained to assess an eye injury, so this detour can delay appropriate first aid.

C.text: A handkerchief can scratch the cornea or push an embedded particle deeper into the eye.

D.text: Clean hands do not make untrained removal safe; the eye should be assessed by the first-aider.

questions.prompt: What colour is a water filled fire extinguisher, or its label?
questions.explanation: Since all UK extinguishers share a red body, the colour scheme now identifies water units by the body being entirely red with no contrasting panel. Water is suited to ordinary combustibles like wood and paper but must never be used on live electrical or flammable-liquid fires.

A.text: Black identifies carbon dioxide, a gas used for different fire risks from ordinary water extinguishers.

B.text: Cream identifies foam, not water, despite both media being useful on some solid combustibles.

C.text: Green is not the current UK identification colour for a water extinguisher.

D.text: Since all UK extinguishers share a red body, the colour scheme now identifies water units by the body being entirely red with no contrasting panel. Water is suited to ordinary combustibles like wood and paper but must never be used on live electrical or flammable-liquid fires.

questions.prompt: For fires involving spilled petrol, which types of fire extinguisher could you use?

options.A: Foam, carbon dioxide or dry powder
options.B: Water, carbon dioxide or dry powder

questions.explanation: Burning petrol is a flammable-liquid fire where water would spread the blaze by floating the fuel. Foam blankets the surface to cut off oxygen, while carbon dioxide and dry powder smother the flames, making all three suitable for this class of fire.

A.text: Burning petrol is a flammable-liquid fire where water would spread the blaze by floating the fuel. Foam blankets the surface to cut off oxygen, while carbon dioxide and dry powder smother the flames, making all three suitable for this class of fire.

B.text: This combination includes water, which can spread floating petrol and enlarge the burning surface.

C.text: Carbon dioxide and foam may be suitable, but adding water makes the listed combination unsafe for spilled petrol.

D.text: Powder and foam may control the fire, yet the water in this group can carry burning fuel outward.

questions.prompt: If there had been a small fire, who should you report it to?
questions.explanation: The supervisor should be aware, so that further preventative measures can be considered.

A.text: The main contractor may need notification through site arrangements, but the worker's immediate reporting line is the supervisor.

B.text: A resident engineer may have no responsibility for the worker or fire procedure and is not the normal first report.

C.text: The fire marshal manages evacuation duties; reporting through the supervisor ensures the incident is recorded and investigated.

D.text: The supervisor should be aware, so that further preventative measures can be considered.

questions.prompt: What should you do if you hear the fire alarm?

options.A: Evacuate the premises to a designated place of safety
options.B: Go towards the sound to find out what is going on
options.C: Ignore it because it might be someone playing around

questions.explanation: It is essential that people go to a place of safety, where supervisors or fire marshals know where they are, in the event of a fire.

A.text: It is essential that people go to a place of safety, where supervisors or fire marshals know where they are, in the event of a fire.

B.text: Moving toward the alarm can take the worker into smoke or fire and obstruct the response.

C.text: Every alarm must be treated as real until authorised otherwise; assuming a prank can be fatal.

D.text: Leaving for home bypasses the assembly-point roll call and may send the person through an unsafe route.

questions.prompt: What are the lower and upper action values with regard to daily personal noise exposure, as defined in the Control of Noise at Work Regulations 2005?
questions.explanation: Daily personal noise exposure is the average noise level experienced by an individual over an 8 hour period.

A.text: Seventy and eighty decibels understate both statutory exposure action values in the Noise Regulations.

B.text: The upper value is right, but the lower action value begins at 80 dB(A), not 75 dB(A).

C.text: Daily personal noise exposure is the average noise level experienced by an individual over an 8 hour period.

D.text: Eighty-five is the upper action value, not the lower one, and 90 dB(A) is not the current upper action value.

questions.prompt: Exposure to asbestos fibres may cause which one of the following?
questions.explanation: Breathing in asbestos fibres can also lead to a number of other diseases, including lung cancer and mesothelioma

A.text: Breathing in asbestos fibres can also lead to a number of other diseases, including lung cancer and mesothelioma

B.text: Asthma can have many workplace causes, but it is not the characteristic fibrotic lung disease caused by asbestos fibres.

C.text: Dermatitis is an inflammatory skin condition; inhaled asbestos primarily causes serious diseases of the lungs and pleura.

D.text: Glandular fever is a viral infection and has no causal link to breathing asbestos fibres.

questions.prompt: If you have been handling lead, how is it most likely to get into your blood stream?

options.A: By not reporting the matter to the HSE
options.B: By not using the correct safety footwear
options.C: By not washing your hands before eating

questions.explanation: The route into the body is ingestion, normally from lead contamination on the hands.

A.text: Failure to notify HSE does not itself put lead into the bloodstream; exposure occurs through physical routes into the body.

B.text: Safety footwear protects the feet but does not stop contaminated hands transferring lead to food or the mouth.

C.text: The route into the body is ingestion, normally from lead contamination on the hands.

D.text: Goggles protect the eyes; they do not control ingestion from eating with lead-contaminated hands.

questions.prompt: Which listed requirement must apply to a safety helmet supplied as PPE for work in Great Britain?

options.A: It is less than 1 year old
options.B: It must meet the applicable PPE product-safety requirements and bear a recognised conformity marking such as CE or UKCA
options.C: It is less than 2 years old
options.D: It is less than 5 years old

questions.explanation: A helmet's suitability is not established by a generic age limit. PPE placed on the Great Britain market must meet the applicable essential safety requirements and carry an accepted conformity marking; current law recognises both CE and UKCA routes, so CE-only wording was incomplete.

A.text: A one-year age limit is not a general conformity requirement and says nothing about the helmet's standard or condition.

B.text: A helmet's suitability is not established by a generic age limit. PPE placed on the Great Britain market must meet the applicable essential safety requirements and carry an accepted conformity marking; current law recognises both CE and UKCA routes, so CE-only wording was incomplete.

C.text: Two years is not a universal expiry period; service life depends on the maker's instructions, use and damage.

D.text: Five years is neither an automatic acceptance nor rejection rule and cannot replace conformity and pre-use checks.

questions.prompt: When considering what measures to take to protect people's health and safety, PPE should always be regarded as:

options.A: The best way to tackle the job

questions.explanation: Engineering controls and safe systems of work should always be considered first.

A.text: PPE does not remove the hazard and should follow consideration of elimination, substitution and engineering controls.

B.text: Treating PPE as the first defence bypasses controls that protect everyone without depending on correct wear.

C.text: Engineering controls and safe systems of work should always be considered first.

D.text: PPE is rarely the only practical measure; safe methods, guarding, ventilation or segregation may control risk more effectively.

questions.prompt: When MUST an employer provide their employees with personal protective equipment (PPE)?

options.B: If the client or main contractor specifies it in the contract
options.D: When they may be exposed to a risk to their health & safety which cannot be controlled another way

questions.explanation: Under the PPE at Work Regulations, personal protective equipment is a last resort used only when a risk cannot be removed or controlled by safer means first. The employer must then provide suitable PPE free of charge wherever such residual risk to health and safety remains.

A.text: PPE provision responds to the present residual risk, not a five-year replacement timetable.

B.text: A contract may add site rules, but the employer's statutory duty exists even when the client says nothing about PPE.

C.text: Inspection and replacement intervals depend on the equipment and condition; twice-yearly issue is not the legal trigger.

D.text: Under the PPE at Work Regulations, personal protective equipment is a last resort used only when a risk cannot be removed or controlled by safer means first. The employer must then provide suitable PPE free of charge wherever such residual risk to health and safety remains.

questions.prompt: Which of the following have to be entered into the accident book?

options.D: Only accidents causing time off work

questions.explanation: An accident causing an injury to an employee at work should be recorded in the accident book (BI 510).

A.text: An accident causing an injury to an employee at work should be recorded in the accident book (BI 510).

B.text: Property damage without injury belongs in other site records and is not, by itself, an entry about an injured person.

C.text: Minor injuries can worsen and reveal recurring hazards, so recording cannot be restricted to cases initially judged serious.

D.text: An injury may need treatment without causing absence; waiting for time off would leave the original event undocumented.

questions.prompt: Why is it important to report 'near miss' accidents to your employer?

options.B: So lessons can be learned, preventing an accident next time
options.C: So that someone can be disciplined
options.D: To make the figures look good

questions.explanation: The HSE advises that 'near misses' should be investigated to prevent their recurrence.

A.text: Not every near miss is itself RIDDOR-reportable, so prevention rather than a blanket statutory report is the reason.

B.text: The HSE advises that 'near misses' should be investigated to prevent their recurrence.

C.text: Discipline-focused reporting discourages openness and does not address the conditions that could injure someone next time.

D.text: Near-miss reporting can initially raise figures; its purpose is learning and risk reduction, not cosmetic statistics.

questions.prompt: When working in dusty conditions, what of the following would give the LEAST level of protection?
questions.explanation: Protection factors are given in HSE publication HSG53 'Respiratory protective equipment at work - A practical guide'

A.text: A supplied-air helmet provides clean air and a high assigned protection factor when correctly selected and used.

B.text: Protection factors are given in HSE publication HSG53 'Respiratory protective equipment at work - A practical guide'

C.text: A positive-pressure powered respirator generally provides greater inward-leakage protection than a negative-pressure half mask.

D.text: Self-contained breathing apparatus supplies its own breathable air and provides far higher protection for suitable trained use.

questions.prompt: What immediate action should you take if you suffer an injury through carrying a load?

options.A: Advise your doctor of your injury
options.B: Carry on working as best you can

questions.explanation: All injuries must be recorded in the Company accident book (BI 510).

A.text: Medical advice may be needed, but the workplace must first know about the injury so help, recording and controls can be arranged.

B.text: Continuing can worsen a strain and prevents assessment of the handling task that caused it.

C.text: All injuries must be recorded in the Company accident book (BI 510).

D.text: A companion cannot authorise treatment or change the system of work; the supervisor or employer needs the report.

questions.prompt: What would you NOT consider in making a judgement of the risks from a load?
questions.explanation: A, C and D can all affect the difficulty of lifting an object.

A.text: An offset centre of gravity changes how a load tips and how close its heavy side must be held.

B.text: A, C and D can all affect the difficulty of lifting an object.

C.text: Size, damage and shape affect grip, visibility, stability and whether mechanical assistance is needed.

D.text: Weight directly affects handling force and must be considered alongside posture, frequency and capability.

questions.prompt: What does UK manual-handling law say about a single maximum weight that an individual may lift?

options.A: 15kg provided that it is a compact load
options.B: 35kg provided that it has no sharp edges
options.C: There is no single legal maximum; the task, load, environment and individual's capability must be assessed

questions.explanation: The law does not set one maximum lifting weight. Employers must avoid hazardous manual handling where reasonably practicable, assess unavoidable operations and reduce risk, taking account of the whole task and the individual rather than treating comfort as a safe limit.

A.text: Fifteen kilograms is not a universal legal ceiling; posture, frequency, grip and individual capability can change the risk.

B.text: Removing sharp edges does not make 35 kg universally acceptable, and the Regulations set no single maximum weight.

C.text: The law does not set one maximum lifting weight. Employers must avoid hazardous manual handling where reasonably practicable, assess unavoidable operations and reduce risk, taking account of the whole task and the individual rather than treating comfort as a safe limit.

D.text: A supervisor's instruction cannot override the duty to avoid, assess and reduce hazardous manual handling.

questions.prompt: Which of the following is advisable when lifting a load manually?

options.A: Use a stable stance, keep the load close and use slight bending of the back, hips and knees while avoiding twist and further back flexion
options.B: Bend the knees, keep the back straight, use power of back
options.C: Keep legs and back straight, use power of legs
options.D: Keep legs straight, bend back, use power of legs

questions.explanation: Current HSE technique favours a stable posture and slight coordinated bending, not a rigidly straight back or a deep squat. Keep the heaviest side close, secure the load, move smoothly and turn with the feet instead of twisting.

A.text: Current HSE technique favours a stable posture and slight coordinated bending, not a rigidly straight back or a deep squat. Keep the heaviest side close, secure the load, move smoothly and turn with the feet instead of twisting.

B.text: The back is not the power source for the lift, and forcing it rigidly straight is not current HSE technique.

C.text: Keeping both legs and back straight forces reaching and spinal bending and prevents a stable, close hold.

D.text: Straight legs combined with a bent back places the load far from the body and increases spinal leverage.

questions.prompt: Which listed answer best describes using good manual-handling technique after hazardous handling has first been avoided or reduced as far as reasonably practicable?

options.A: Getting a friend to help you with the load
options.B: Handling the load in a controlled and efficient way using a stable posture, secure hold, close load position and smooth movement
options.C: Using a crane or some other mechanical means
options.D: Using a forklift truck or pallet truck

questions.explanation: 'Kinetic lifting' is dated shorthand and must not imply that technique makes an otherwise hazardous lift safe. Good handling technique supplements task redesign and lifting aids; it uses balance, a close load, controlled movement and avoids twisting or sudden force.

A.text: A second person may reduce individual force, but an unplanned team lift can introduce poor coordination and does not describe technique.

B.text: 'Kinetic lifting' is dated shorthand and must not imply that technique makes an otherwise hazardous lift safe. Good handling technique supplements task redesign and lifting aids; it uses balance, a close load, controlled movement and avoids twisting or sudden force.

C.text: A crane can eliminate manual lifting and may be the better control, but it is mechanical handling rather than good manual technique.

D.text: Forklifts and pallet trucks are handling aids used to avoid or reduce manual effort, not a body-movement technique.

questions.prompt: What do the blue and white health and safety signs tell you?

options.D: Where the nearest fire exit is

questions.explanation: Blue and white safety signs are mandatory signs giving a positive instruction that must be obeyed, such as wearing eye protection or a hard hat. The circular blue shape and white pictogram are standardised so the message is recognised instantly regardless of language or literacy.

A.text: Hazard warnings use yellow and black, not the blue circular mandatory-sign format.

B.text: Blue and white safety signs are mandatory signs giving a positive instruction that must be obeyed, such as wearing eye protection or a hard hat. The circular blue shape and white pictogram are standardised so the message is recognised instantly regardless of language or literacy.

C.text: Prohibitions use red edging and a diagonal bar to show an action that must not be taken.

D.text: Safe-condition signs such as emergency exits use green and white rather than blue and white.

questions.prompt: The Health and Safety at Work Act 1974 and any regulations made under the Act are:

options.C: Not compulsory, but should be complied with if convenient
options.D: Practical advice for the employer to follow

questions.explanation: The requirements of health and safety law are mandatory and failure to follow them can lead to prosecution.

A.text: Acts and regulations impose enforceable duties; they are not optional recommendations for companies or individuals.

B.text: The requirements of health and safety law are mandatory and failure to follow them can lead to prosecution.

C.text: Convenience is not a defence to non-compliance with a statutory health and safety requirement.

D.text: Practical guidance explains ways to comply, whereas the Act and regulations themselves create legal obligations.

questions.prompt: Regulations that govern health and safety on construction sites:

options.D: Do not apply during 'out of hours' working

questions.explanation: The requirements of health and safety law are mandatory, and failure to follow them can lead to prosecutions.

A.text: Health and safety duties apply according to work and risk, not according to whether a worker is inexperienced.

B.text: Small employers and small projects remain subject to construction health and safety law.

C.text: The requirements of health and safety law are mandatory, and failure to follow them can lead to prosecutions.

D.text: Legal duties continue outside ordinary hours; the time of day does not suspend the Regulations.

questions.prompt: In what circumstances can an HSE Improvement Notice be issued?

options.B: If there is a breach of legal requirements
options.C: Only between Monday and Friday on site

questions.explanation: Improvement notices require action to achieve standards which meet health and safety law.

A.text: An appointed inspector serves an improvement notice under statutory powers without first obtaining a police warrant.

B.text: Improvement notices require action to achieve standards which meet health and safety law.

C.text: Enforcement powers are not restricted to weekdays; the issue is the legal breach, not the day of inspection.

D.text: Prosecution is a separate enforcement route and is not the office through which an improvement notice is issued.

questions.prompt: Employers are required to provide information to their employees on their health and safety rights and responsibilities and how to get advice by:

options.A: Displaying a poster or giving them leaflets approved by the HSE
options.C: Making them read the company health and safety policy
options.D: Telling them verbally when they start work for them

questions.explanation: This is a requirement of the Health and Safety Information for Employees Regulations (as amended).

A.text: This is a requirement of the Health and Safety Information for Employees Regulations (as amended).

B.text: An ordinary email is not one of the prescribed methods unless it supplies the approved leaflet itself in an acceptable way.

C.text: The company policy explains local arrangements but does not replace the official law poster or approved employee leaflet.

D.text: A verbal induction can add site detail, but it does not satisfy the separate duty to provide the approved rights information.

questions.prompt: Employers have to produce a written Health and Safety Policy statement when:

options.D: They employ five people or more

questions.explanation: This is a specific requirement of the Health and Safety at Work Act.

A.text: Starting a contract does not set the written-policy threshold; it depends on the employer's workforce size.

B.text: The duty arises automatically from law and does not wait for an HSE notification.

C.text: A safety representative may request information, but their request is not what creates the statutory requirement.

D.text: This is a specific requirement of the Health and Safety at Work Act.
